We map the resulting interactions onto the sixteen-potential Dobrescu--Mocioiu basis and use this mapping to translate existing experimental constraints into numerical limits on spin-1 and spin-2 coupling products in the small- and large-mediator-mass regimes, together with representative limits at finite mediator masses. The derived relations between the boson-exchange coupling constants and the coefficients of the basis potentials also allow published exclusion curves to be rescaled to arbitrary mediator masses.

items.title: Contrast-Enhanced Nonlinear Imaging with Moiré Flat-Band Superlattices
items.summary: Nonlinear metasurfaces offer a compact platform for infrared-to-visible conversion and imaging, yet resonant enhancement is often accompanied by restricted angular acceptance, limiting the range of transverse spatial frequencies that can interact efficiently with the nonlinear modes. Here, we address this challenge using a one-dimensional photonic moiré superlattice supporting multiple quasi-flat bands in the near-infrared. These moiré modes combine strong near-field enhancement with broad momentum-space accessibility, enabling efficient third-harmonic generation (THG) while maintaining stable excitation over a large angular range. Experimentally, we observe strong THG emission near $467~\mathrm{nm}$ under broadband excitation from $ 1180$ to $ 2000~\mathrm {nm} $. We further employ the nonlinear moiré superlattice for infrared imaging by converting an infrared target into visible through the THG process. By encoding image information into displacement-dependent THG signals and decoding their spatial variations, we experimentally resolve weak features and internal textures with improved contrast compared with THG imaging using nonlinear films or conventional nonlinear metasurfaces. These results establish photonic moiré superlattices as a versatile platform combining efficient frequency conversion, broad angular acceptance, and mode-sensitive spatial encoding for high-contrast, label-free nonlinear imaging with enhanced feature discrimination.

items.title: Observation of room-temperature intrinsic antiferroelectricity in van der Waals NbOCl2
items.summary: In recent years, two-dimensional (2D) ferroelectricity has been extensively investigated across a wide range of 2D materials, while intrinsic 2D antiferroelectricity remains exceptionally rare, limiting its implementation in next-generation photonic and electronic devices. Here, we report the observation of room-temperature-stable antiferroelectricity in the layered transition metal oxyhalide NbOCl2, and demonstrate a reversible, stimuli-driven antiferroelectric-to-ferroelectric (AFE-to-FE) phase transition in this material. Second-harmonic generation (SHG) mapping reveals a well-defined stripe-like spatial distribution of SHG intensity across as-grown NbOCl2 flakes spanning thickness from few-layer to bulk-like configurations. This distinctive SHG signature originates from the existence of antiferroelectric phase and the coexistence of antiferroelectric and ferroelectric phases within individual crystals, as evidenced by a combined incident-angle-dependent SHG measurement and Raman spectroscopy. By integrating NbOCl2 with one-dimensional silver nanowires, we achieve spatially selective, strain-mediated AFE-to-FE phase transition. Moreover, an ultralow electric field (~20 kV/cm) induces a reversible SHG response, consistent with switching from the centrosymmetric antiferroelectric state (SHG-silent) to the non-centrosymmetric ferroelectric state (SHG-active). This study not only expands the family of room-temperature 2D antiferroelectrics but also establishes a versatile platform for dynamic manipulation of nonlinear light, paving the way toward electric-field-programmable nonlinear photonics and optical information processing.

items.title: Bandgap fluctuations and robustness in two-dimensional hyperuniform dielectric materials
items.summary: We numerically study the statistical fluctuations of photonic band gaps in ensembles of stealthy hyperuniform disordered patterns. We find that at low stealthiness, where correlations are weak, band gaps of different system realizations appear over a wide frequency range, are narrow, and generally do not overlap. Interestingly, above a critical value of stealthiness $χ\gtrsim 0.35$, the bandgaps become large and overlap significantly from realization to realization, while a second gap appears. These observations extend our understanding of photonic bandgaps in disordered systems and provide information on the robustness of gaps in practical applications.

items.title: Evaluation of tracking plane pitch and xenon-helium gas mixtures for the NEXT experiment
items.summary: NEXT is an experimental program to search for neutrinoless double-beta decay ($ββ0ν$) in high-pressure xenon gas using electroluminescent time projection chambers. A key feature of the NEXT technology is the reconstruction of MeV-scale electron tracks, which plays a key role in identifying $ββ0ν$ events. This work presents a Monte Carlo study aimed at determining the optimal configuration for NEXT detectors employing SiPM-based tracking planes. The simulations are carried out in the NEXT-100 detector geometry, and to classify the events as signal or background, we use a Sparse Convolutional Neural Network. We find that topological rejection power improves by approximately a factor of two at the lower pressure studied (5 bar) compared to the baseline design (13.5 bar). A finer pitch also offers consistent improvement, where reducing pitch from 15 mm to 5 mm decreased the accepted background fraction by a factor of approximately 1.4 at 13.5 bar for a fixed signal efficiency in the different configurations studied. The addition of helium to reduce electron diffusion provides a comparable enhancement, reducing the accepted background fraction by up to a factor of 1.5 at 13.5 bar. We highlight two key practical configurations at 13.5 bar pressure: the present NEXT-100 (pure Xe with a 15 mm tracking plane pitch) and an upgraded NEXT-100 (a Xe-He gas mixture and a 10 mm tracking plane pitch). These results provide quantitative guidance for the design and optimisation of future NEXT detectors, balancing physics performance with technical and financial constraints.

items.title: A note on semidiurnal motions in the deep Mediterranean
items.summary: The Mediterranean Sea is known for its limited tidal motions. For example, surface barotropic tidal elevations have an amplitude of about 0.1 m in the Northwestern Mediterranean. Nevertheless, small significant peaks occur at semidiurnal frequencies in spectra of temperature variance measured near the 2450-m deep seafloor at a multiple-line mooring. These semidiurnal signals appear to be surface tides commonly measured by pressure sensors, but are only observable in temperature under near-homogeneous conditions when buoyancy frequency N < f, the inertial frequency. After transfer of pressure to temperature units via the local adiabatic lapse rate, the observed internal-wave temperature signals may thus be corrected for 1.5x10^-5 degrC amplitude semidiurnal, predominantly lunar barotropic tides. The remaining baroclinic tides are embedded in the broad and featureless inertio-gravity wave (IGW) band, with small but significant energy enhancement near its boundaries including the precise semidiurnal frequency, also under tenfold-larger energetic stratified-water conditions. The similar IGW bands under both stratification conditions suggest slanted convection during stratified-water conditions, as the stratification is near-homogenous in the direction slanted to the vertical. The use of multiple instruments improves spectral statistics at frequencies exceeding IGW, and including the IGW band under some near-homogeneous conditions but not under stratified-water conditions during which more coherent motions prevail.

items.title: FDM+: A Framework for Constrained Control of the 2D Radiative Transport Equation
items.summary: Applying the frozen diffusion model (FDM) [29] to the constrained control of the 2D radiative transport equation presents several challenges. These include the dimensional difference between control variables and state functions, the resolution mismatch between traditional numerical solvers and deep learning models, and solution non-uniqueness. To address these obstacles, we propose a novel approach, FDM+, which includes three key improvements. Firstly, a decoupled prediction architecture is introduced to address the dimensional heterogeneity. Secondly, an efficient parameterization strategy resolves the resolution mismatch. Meanwhile, we derive a total error bound to analyze how the parameterization error and the model estimation error jointly affect the performance. Thirdly, the conditional distribution learned by the diffusion model is leveraged to perform design space exploration for multi-solution problems. A series of numerical experiments demonstrate that FDM+ outperforms existing methods in reconstruction accuracy and design flexibility.

items.title: Polarized positron generation via laser-engineered quasistatic magnetic fields in a spatially extended herringbone target
items.summary: Polarized positron sources are of interest for precision studies of spin-dependent interactions and future high-energy colliders, motivating laser-driven approaches for producing relativistic polarized positrons. Here, we propose a scheme in which a herringbone plasma target organizes laser-driven return currents to generate spatially extended quasi-static magnetic fields. Three-dimensional spin-resolved quantum electrodynamics particle-in-cell simulations show that a 3.4-PW laser produces magnetic fields exceeding $10^6$ T, with opposite polarities on the two sides of the target and a duration exceeding 100 fs. A delayed 10-GeV electron beam generates high-energy photons through nonlinear Compton scattering, followed by positron production via the nonlinear Breit--Wheeler process. The resulting positrons exhibit opposite spin polarizations and deflection directions in the two magnetic-field regions, enabling angular selection of positrons with polarization exceeding $63\%$ at a yield of approximately $0.007$ positrons per incident electron, compared with a total yield of $0.029$. More restrictive angular selection can further increase the polarization to nearly $90\%$, albeit at a substantially reduced yield. These results suggest a route to polarized positron generation through the spatial organization of laser-driven quasi-static magnetic fields.

items.title: Design Optimization of Nuclear Fusion Reactor through Deep Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: In this research, we investigate deep reinforcement learning (DRL) as a practical tool for constrained, multi-objective optimization for tokamak fusion reactor designs. The task is to optimize the design configurations that minimize building cost while achieving high energy gain and long energy confinement time, subject to the four operational limits required for stable operation. Due to the coupled physics-engineering evaluation, the resulting objectives and constraints are black-box, making it challenging to find optimal solutions with conventional search strategies. To address this, we implement Reward-Constrained Policy Optimization (RCPO) for tokamak fusion reactor design. This method integrates multiple constraints into the reward functions, guiding the policy towards feasible solutions and simplifying the design optimization process. Our numerical results show that the proposed DRL-based approach finds more feasible designs that satisfy operational constraints more efficiently than other data-driven optimization methods, demonstrating the potential of DRL for efficient future reactor design.

items.title: The ALICE asynchronous software trigger processing for LHC Run 3
items.summary: The detector and computing upgrades for LHC Run 3 enable ALICE to continuously acquire proton--proton (pp) and lead--lead (Pb--Pb) collisions at interaction rates of up to 1.5 MHz and 50 kHz, respectively. The resulting pp dataset is more than three orders of magnitude larger than the combined Run 1 and Run 2 samples, and its long-term retention in full would be impractical given the available storage capacity. To address this challenge, ALICE has implemented a physics-driven asynchronous software trigger designed to retain only collisions containing signals of physics interest. Following full asynchronous reconstruction, the Central Event Filter Processor applies more than 100 analysis-based selection channels spanning the ALICE pp physics programme. The selected collisions are then used to skim the original Compressed Time Frames (CTFs), preserving the relevant detector information within detector-specific time windows. This procedure reduces the retained CTF volume to approximately 4.5% of its original size, while preserving the possibility of future reconstruction with improved calibrations and software. This contribution describes the implementation and operation of the asynchronous software trigger, from collision selection to CTF skimming, and highlights how this strategy provides access to rare signals and processes across the ALICE physics programme.
authors: Sara Pucillo for the ALICE Collaboration

items.title: Particle accelerators as a path to intergovernmental collaboration: the case of the first electron positron collider and the power of theoretical physics
items.summary: I revisit the history of the first matter-antimatter collider built in Italy in 1960 and carried to success through an inter-European collaboration with France, to underline the need for large intergovernmental efforts in the realization of particle accelerators such as the proposed electron synchrotron in the Greater Caribbean region. The foundational role of the Austrian born theoretical physicist Bruno Touschek and his life path through Europe before and after World War II is briefly recalled. The role of CERN as a post-war intergovernmental institution in jump-starting the international collaboration between the Frascati National Laboratories in Italy and the Laboratoire de l'Accelerateur Lineaire d'Orsay in France is highlighted through historical documents, and contributions from interviews with the protagonists of Touschek's game-changing proposal.

items.title: Enhancement of Weak Interactions in Phase Transitions in Condensed Matter and Early Universe
items.summary: Parity-violating weak interactions produce extremely small energy differences between left- and right-handed chiral systems. We show that these microscopic effects may be amplified during collective phenomena such as phase transitions. The enhancement factor is proportional to the critical number of atoms, $N_c$, in the nucleus of the new phase. Measurement of the ratio of produced left- and right-handed chiral structures may provide a way to determine $N_c$. Experiments in which spin-chiral structures are formed in ZnCr$_2$Se$_4$ during a phase transition in crossed electric and magnetic fields indicate an effective amplification corresponding to $N_c\sim 10^9-10^{10}$. We emphasize, however, that such large values cannot be inferred from homogeneous capillary nucleation alone, since the same parameters imply a very large nucleation barrier; in real crystals heterogeneous nucleation, defects, strain, and domain-growth dynamics may be essential. We also discuss, more cautiously, whether analogous collective enhancement could operate in first-order cosmological phase transitions beyond the Standard Model. The Standard-Model electroweak transition for the observed Higgs mass is a crossover and therefore has no critical bubble nucleus.

items.title: Memory-like effects and kinematics of trajectories in Cyclotron motion
items.summary: We investigate the collective dynamics of a bundle of charged particles undergoing cyclotron motion in a uniform magnetic field when subjected to a short-duration electric pulse. Using the geometric framework based on the evolution of trajectory congruences, we analyze how the pulse affects the expansion, shear, and rotation of a small family of trajectories. We show that the geometric imprint persists after the pulse has vanished, manifesting as a memory of the transient perturbation. Unlike gravitational memory effects, this does not manifest itself in focusing behaviour of the trajectories, and instead implies a restructuring of the shear component before and after the pulse. We offer direct analytic and regression based arguments for the same.

items.title: Six-Degree-of-Freedom Rotor-Load Cross-Spectral Density from Rotor-Plane Turbulence Cross-Spectra
items.summary: A frequency-domain response analysis of a wind turbine rotor requires the complete hub-load spectrum, but the customary scalar thrust and torque spectra retain neither the four in-plane components nor the coupling between them. This paper derives the full six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) rotor-load cross-spectral-density (CSD) matrix from the IEC Kaimal turbulence model. By decoupling the spatial order of inflow coherence from the temporal Doppler shift, the formulation introduces a two-index rotational-sampling kernel. Rotor symmetry and azimuthal averaging constrain the observed Doppler carrier strictly to blade-passing harmonics $pBf_{\mathrm{rot}}$, while the azimuthal aerodynamic transfer shifts the spatial coherence order to $pB+s$. A convergence study of the retained azimuthal order $s$ shows that $\lvert s\rvert\le4$ suffices, the assembled CSD then deviating from the full-band result by less than $10^{-5}$ in relative norm. The formulation is compared with OpenFAST simulations of a rigid floating wind turbine over nine wind speeds: the six auto-spectral densities agree closely below 1~Hz, and the present theory over-predicts the spectra near the 6P and 9P rotational harmonics.

items.title: Twister After Dark: Diagnosing a Damaging Nocturnal Tornado in Iloilo, Philippines (08 August 2026)
items.summary: At ~1430 UTC (2230 LST) on 08 August 2026, a significant tornado struck the Mandurriao and Jaro districts of Iloilo City, Philippines. Its parent supercell developed within the southwest monsoon enhanced by Typhoon Dolphin, under weak synoptic forcing, as a nocturnal low-level jet of ~40 kt near 1.5-3 km advected warm, moist marine air onshore. ERA5 depicted MUCAPE of ~2000 J kg$^{-1}$, negligible inhibition, an LCL below 300 m, and nearly purely streamwise low-level vorticity, but deep-layer shear (DLS, 0-6 km bulk wind difference) below 3 m s$^{-1}$. Hodographs from the newly operational Iloilo S-band dual-polarization radar (S-ILO), ~5-7 km from the storm, revealed low-level shear (LLS, 0-1 km bulk wind difference) of ~16 m s$^{-1}$ and 0-1 km storm-relative helicity of 124-211 m$^2$ s$^{-2}$. The storm exhibited a hook echo with a weak echo hole, a $Z_{DR}$ arc and ring, an elevated 55-60 dBZ rear-flank core consistent with a descending reflectivity core, and a ~50 dBZ ring interpreted as a debris ball. A survey of 31 damage indicators documented a ~2.9 km long and up to ~340 m wide path rated IF2 on the International Fujita Scale. Processor smoothing of the radial velocity and a $ρ_{HV}$ threshold for rainfall estimation masked any tornadic vortex or debris signature, although a radial velocity simulation shows that a narrow vortex (core radius ~50-100 m) with a rotational velocity of ~35-45 m s$^{-1}$ could have been concealed. This case shows that significant tornadoes can develop at night during the Philippine monsoon season and that operational radar quality control should be revised to retain severe-storm signatures.

items.title: Enabling joint chemical and meteorological data assimilation with an atmospheric foundation model
items.summary: The hydroxyl radical (OH) is the main oxidant in the troposphere and accounts for 88% of the methane sink, yet its abundance and trends remain poorly constrained. Satellites observe many of the chemical and meteorological drivers of OH, but assimilating both requires a model that represents chemistry and meteorology together. Existing chemistry-climate models are too expensive for joint data assimilation. Here, we present AuroraChem, a fine-tuned version of the Aurora atmospheric foundation model that jointly simulates meteorology and the GEOS-Chem chemical fields needed to constrain OH. A one-year AuroraChem rollout takes 12 minutes on one GPU. Free rollouts remain stable for one year but do not fully capture seasonal cycles. Using idealized data assimilation, we find that chemical observations can constrain the meteorological state and meteorological observations can constrain the chemical state. Inserting only the chemical fields raises the annual mean spatial correlation of 500 hPa temperature from 0.89 to 0.92 and recovers the moisture and circulation pattern of the Indian summer monsoon. Inserting only the meteorological fields raises the 500 hPa OH correlation from 0.89 to 0.93, close to the 0.94 from inserting the chemical fields themselves, and recovers the OH seasonal cycle. Inserting only NO2 columns sampled at TROPOMI pixels gives an OH correlation of 0.93. These relationships likely reflect learned covariances rather than physical coupling, and covariances are what data assimilation uses to let an observation of one variable update the others. AuroraChem therefore provides a new pathway to joint chemical and meteorological data assimilation.

items.title: A Lie-Group Approach to Alfvénic Turbulence: The SO(3) Rotational p-model
items.summary: The inner heliosphere is permeated by fully developed, highly intermittent nonlinear turbulence. Conventional stochastic models synthesize these multiscale fluctuations by injecting additive noise within a flat Euclidean space. However, such approaches fundamentally violate the topological constraints of ideal magnetohydrodynamics, inadvertently breaking the kinetic incompressibility of the plasma and introducing spurious magnetic compressibility. To preserve the exact geometrical invariants of Alfvénic fluctuations, a novel mathematical framework is presented: the rotational p-model. By mapping a multifractal singular measure directly into the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ and integrating the associated stochastic differential equations in the Stratonovich sense on the spherical manifold $S^{2}$, the model generates highly intermittent, scale-dependent rotational dynamics. This Lie-group formulation conserves the magnetic field modulus while perfectly reproducing the fractional spectral envelopes and the non-Gaussian directional intermittency observed in space plasmas. Furthermore, by isolating purely directional reorientations, the framework provides exact analytical control over the waiting time statistics of magnetic intermittent bursts and the multifractal scaling exponents of angular deflections, offering a powerful new paradigm for the study of nonlinear turbulent phenomena.

items.title: A Quantum Chemistry Dataset of 120 Kilo Organic Molecules with 20 Million Conformations
items.summary: Quantum-chemical datasets of molecular geometries, electronic energies and atomic forces support the development of atomistic machine-learning models. Here we present QO2Mol, comprising 116,127 organic molecular fragments and more than 20 million three-dimensional conformations. The fragments were obtained by bond cleavage and capping of source compounds and contain H, C, N, O, F, P, S, Cl, Br and I. The geometries include optimized structures and configurations generated through torsional sampling and local bond-length and bond-angle perturbations. Electronic energies and atomic forces were calculated at the B3LYP/def2-SVP level of theory. Each conformational record also contains dipole moments, isotropic polarizabilities, electronic spatial extents and frequency-derived correction values. The dataset and its documented generation and validation procedures support molecular energy and force modelling and studies of geometry-dependent molecular properties.

items.title: Quantifying AI data center nitrogen oxide (NO$_x$) emissions from space
items.summary: AI data center power demand is spurring rapid deployment of on- and near-site natural gas turbines. The resulting nitrogen oxide NO$_x$ pollution is a growing concern but has not previously been quantified with atmospheric observations. Here we demonstrate space-based detection and quantification of NO$_x$ emissions from the SpaceXAI Colossus 2 power plant in Southaven, Mississippi. Using observations from the geostationary TEMPO satellite instrument, we detect a strong increase in local mean NO$_2$ column concentrations after the plant began operations in late 2025. We then use TEMPO to estimate two-week-average NO$_x$ source rates from August 2025 to August 2026, calibrating against continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS) data from US power plants. TEMPO first detected NO$_x$ emissions in December 2025 at 530$\pm$220 kg h$^{-1}$. We find that emissions increased through August 2026, averaging 870$\pm$165 kg h$^{-1}$ after February 2026, roughly 19$\pm$4 times higher than expected from the facility's March 2026 permit for 41 turbines operating under best available control technology (BACT) requirements ($\sim$47 kg h$^{-1}$). Emissions at the expected level would be undetectable by our TEMPO analysis.

items.title: Multi-Species Multi-Reaction Model Parametrization of a Commercial NCA Positive Electrode from Half-Cell Open-Circuit Potential Data
items.summary: Physics-based models of lithium-ion batteries require the open-circuit potential (OCP) of each electrode as a function of its lithiation. The multi-species multi-reaction (MSMR) model provides a compact, thermodynamically grounded description of this relationship, representing each insertion reaction by a standard potential, a site fraction and a disorder parameter. Here, we parametrize the MSMR model for nickel-cobalt-aluminum oxide (NCA), a cathode chemistry widespread in automotive cells, using the positive electrode of a commercial silicon-graphite/NCA cell. Cathode material was harvested from a pristine cell and from cells cycle-aged to the end of life under two state-of-charge windows, and its half-cell OCP was measured by slow galvanostatic cycling. Smooth differential-capacity curves were obtained by histogram counting, and the charge and discharge branches were fitted with a constrained, scale-invariant optimization that keeps every reaction anchored to a visible peak. We report the first MSMR parameter set for an NCA cathode and show, through a differential-capacity peak analysis across aging states, that its thermodynamic signature is essentially unchanged by aging. This finding supports the common modeling practice of holding the electrode's intrinsic parameters fixed and ascribing aging to electrode-level capacity and alignment changes.

items.title: Efficient Spectra and Dynamics with Tangent-Space Chebyshev Tree Tensor Networks
items.summary: We present a tangent-space Chebyshev method (TaChe), which combines tree tensor network states with Chebyshev recursion and maximum entropy spectral analysis in a tree tensor network tangent space, for quantum many-body spectra and dynamics. Implemented tensor network state calculations in the tangent space of the ground state, the core advantage of TaChe is that it can substantially reduce the computational complexity, memory usage, and numerical instability associated with tensor network state compression. Implemented on the GPU platform, it produces accurate spectra with speedups of up to $46.8$ over the previous Chebyshev tensor network method and $13.7$ over one-site time-dependent variational principle propagation in the reported benchmarks. Applications to acetonitrile, thermal aggregate emission, finite-temperature charge transport on a \(6\times6\) lattice, and internal conversion in aggregates of up to 100 molecules demonstrate the efficiency and versatility of TaChe in simulating complex molecular systems.

items.title: Quantum Mpemba effect in a driven-dissipative atom-waveguide coupled system
items.summary: The quantum Mpemba effect (QME) describes the counterintuitive phenomenon in which a more strongly perturbed quantum system relaxes toward its steady state faster than a less perturbed one. Here, we investigate the QME in a weakly driven-dissipative atomic array coupled to a one-dimensional chiral waveguide. Starting from the steady state, we introduce a local quench by resetting a single atom to its ground state and examine the subsequent relaxation dynamics. We find that quenching atoms near the array boundaries induces faster initial relaxation through enhanced coupling to superradiant modes and direct photon emission into the waveguide, giving rise to an edge-enhanced QME. Strong directional decay further amplifies this effect by promoting the spatial accumulation of superradiant modes near the preferred boundary, leading to a skin-enhanced QME. At later times, relaxation is increasingly governed by long-lived subradiant modes localized predominantly in the bulk of the array. By coupling two atomic arrays with different interparticle spacings, we further demonstrate an interface-induced QME, where quenching an atom near the interface makes the system relax more slowly at early times but approach its steady state faster at later times, owing to weak participation in both superradiant and subradiant modes. Our findings reveal how the spatial structure of collective decay modes and directional dissipation jointly govern anomalous quantum relaxation, offering potential routes toward accelerated steady-state preparation in waveguide QED systems.

items.title: Buoyancy-induced transitions in mixed convective flow past a heated square cylinder
items.summary: The effect of aiding buoyancy on flow past a square cylinder has previously been shown to suppress vortex shedding above a critical Richardson number (Ri), transitioning from unsteady to steady flow. Building on this, the present study uses two-dimensional direct numerical simulations (DNS) of vertically upward flow past a heated square cylinder to examine two buoyancy-induced transitions for a range of Ri and Reynolds number (Re). The secondary flow induced by buoyant force enhances positive entrainment in the momentum-deficit region aft of the cylinder, thereby suppressing vortex shedding. At higher Ri, this buoyant flow continues to gain downstream momentum, leading to a far-field plume-like instability. Extended domain simulations show that the far-field transition depends on the downstream distance available for buoyancy-driven disturbances to grow. Increasing Re delays near-field suppression but advances far-field instability. A local-flow analysis shows that a Reynolds number based on local mean velocity and plume width substantially improves the collapse of the far-field instability onset, while the corresponding plume-based Strouhal number also exhibits an approximate collapse across the investigated cases. Correlations for drag, surface-averaged Nusselt number, and far-field frequency are proposed using a mixed-convective velocity scale. Linear stability analysis (LSA) about the two-dimensional base flow captures both transitions as Hopf bifurcations and accurately predicts the dominant frequencies and finite-domain transition thresholds observed in DNS. The corresponding eigenmodes reveal localized oscillatory structures that shift downstream with increasing Ri. These results demonstrate the dual role of buoyancy in stabilizing the near wake while destabilizing the far field.

items.title: Scattering features of a self-dual spectral singularity in coupled ring resonators with balanced gain and loss
items.summary: We theoretically and numerically discuss the general scattering property of a coupled two-ring-resonators externally coupled to a straight bus waveguide. Specifically, we require one ring resonator to be light field amplifying and another to be that dissipative, where the associated attenuation and gain factors for a field amplitude after one-round trip are formed in a reciprocal pair as well as the effective wave propagation constants are same. Obtained from reciprocity and an effective PT-symmetric transfer matrix, we exploit parametrization to propose a general phase diagram, identifying overall scattering outcomes. Especially, we find that the formation of a self-dual spectral singularity, namely coherent perfect absorption-lasing (CPAL), is occurred at a certain relation of a coupling coefficient and an attenuation factor as well as resonant whispering gallery modes. Reducing light amplification and dissipation strengths in each rings narrows the spectral bandwidth associated with CPAL. We further discover that any system with the CPAL parameters would exhibit a same scattering feature: transmission extinction, CPAL, and uni-directional reflectionless at the loss ring side, with respect to an incident wavelength. Additionally, a transmission extinction can be away from the resonance. These analytical predictions are verified by electromagnetic simulations.

items.title: Analysis of the Second-Harmonic Generation Process in Nonlinear Metasurfaces Based on Multiple Quantum Wells: The Approach of Nonlinear Current Density, and The Development of Boundary Conditions
items.summary: Using plasmonic metasurfaces integrated with nonlinear materials, such as multiple quantum wells (MQWs), has been an excellent solution to enhance nonlinear light-matter interactions. In this approach, a plasmonic resonator enhances the intensity of the fundamental harmonic within the MQWs region, increasing the strength of the intersubband transitions inside the MQWs. As a result, the efficiency of second harmonic generation (SHG) increases significantly. In this paper, we present a new approach to analyze the SHG process in nonlinear metasurfaces based on MQWs. In this approach, first, we formulate the nonlinear current density within the MQW region, which serves as the radiation source of the second harmonic wave. Notably, the saturation effect in MQWs, that limits the nonlinear response, is accounted for. Second, we address the development of boundary conditions for the second harmonic (SH) field in periodic structures, which ultimately leads us to define periodic boundary conditions for the SH field. Third, we combine these elements into a semi-analytical framework and validate it against previously reported experimental data. Finally, an efficient MQWs structure and plasmonic metasurface are designed for the fundamental wavelength of 8 $μ$m. After implementing the proposed algorithm, we observe that the designed nonlinear metasurface achieves a significant conversion efficiency of 0.02% under the incident intensity of 23.5 kW/cm$^2$. KEYWORDS: Second harmonic generation, metasurface, multiple quantum wells, nonlinear current density, periodic boundary conditions

items.title: General Noise Channels and Mid-Circuit Measurements for Pre-Trajectory Sampling with Batched Execution
items.summary: Many studies of quantum protocols require fast sampling of large amounts of measurement data from noisy quantum circuits, such as for training machine-learning decoders for quantum error correction. Exact simulation of realistic noise is expensive, while stabilizer-based simulators are fast but approximate, for example through Pauli twirling, which generally alters the output statistics. Pre-trajectory sampling with batched execution (PTSBE) accelerates exact trajectory simulation by sampling noise before state evolution. This method requires the outcome probability of every stochastic event to be independent of the state, which excludes mid-circuit measurements and general Kraus channels. We present a generalization of PTSBE to measurement and Kraus operators without approximation. Each event is partially pre-sampled, while deferred outcomes are drawn during grouped execution via multinomial branching and cached-state reuse. We implement the method for GPUs as an extension of CUDA-Q. On distance-3 topological code memories under amplitude damping, it is up to 24x faster than conventional trajectory sampling in CUDA-Q. On 30-qubit random circuits with mid-circuit measurements, it is up to 83x faster and outperforms the near-Clifford simulator Clifft when more than about 25% of the gates are non-Clifford. With repeated sampling of each final state, its sampling rate per trajectory exceeds that of CUDA-Q by nearly five orders of magnitude. Our method also allows us to compare exact amplitude damping with its Pauli-twirled channel on a surface-code memory, revealing that twirling overestimates the detection rate by 21% and raises the logical error rate of a lookup decoder by 8%. This work makes exact, high-throughput simulation practical for general noisy circuits, from data generation for training decoders to studying measurement-based fault-tolerant protocols under realistic noise.

items.title: A structure-based model of the bacterial chemosensory array reveals how the scaffolding protein CheW tunes sensory responses
items.summary: We introduce a structure-based Ising model of the bacterial chemosensory array to investigate how the scaffolding protein CheW tunes signaling responses. The model couples the activity states of core signaling units and of CheW subunits within hexameric rings on a lattice with the structure observed in cryoEM experiments. Recent experiments show that increasing CheW participation in hexameric rings raises response cooperativity in non-adapting cells and sensitivity in adaptation-proficient cells. Our lattice model quantitatively reproduces both effects, while mean-field theory shows that CheW increases the effective coupling between core units, sharpening the response in both cell types. The statistics of CheW placement (complete hexameric rings versus random distribution) substantially alter how responses vary with CheW abundance. Moreover, different coupling strengths can yield the same static response yet markedly different activity fluctuations and dynamics. CheW abundance further controls a crossover from relaxational to oscillatory fluctuations, whose location depends on the spatial distribution of CheW. These dynamical signatures, including oscillations predicted near native CheW levels, are testable by single-cell dynamics measurements. Combined with CheW titration and our modeling results, these measurements can probe the array's assembly dynamics and allosteric couplings. Beyond the chemosensory array, our approach can generalize to other large protein complexes, providing a framework to study the functional role of scaffolding proteins and allosteric interfaces in signal processing.

items.title: Projected Sensitivity of a Differential Torsion Sensor for Tests of the Weak Equivalence Principle
items.summary: Tests of the weak equivalence principle (WEP) are among the most sensitive probes of new long-range, composition-dependent interactions beyond general relativity and the Standard Model. We evaluate the potential of a differential torsion sensor, which combines long mechanical coherence times with optical-cavity readout and common-mode rejection, for laboratory WEP tests and fifth-force searches. For a representative configuration based on an existing prototype, with Be-Ti test masses and 180 days of coherent integration, the projected noise-limited sensitivity to the Eötvös parameter is $η\simeq7.5\times10^{-16}$ and $2.4\times10^{-16}$ for signal modulation at 2 and 20 mHz, respectively, below current ground-based torsion-balance limits. For a baryon-coupled Yukawa interaction sourced by the Earth, the corresponding projected sensitivity to the coupling strength is $α\simeq3.1\times10^{-13}$ and $9.8\times10^{-14}$ for ranges $λ\gtrsim10^{7}$ m. We identify the modulation scheme, the material contrast, and the source geometry as the main factors that set the projected reach, and the control of systematic couplings as the main experimental requirement for attaining it. These results indicate that differential torsion sensors are a promising platform for future laboratory WEP tests.

items.title: DIVO: a direct divertor configuration plasma start-up scheme aimed at tokamak fusion reactors
items.summary: The tokamak, one of the mainstream approaches to magnetic confinement in nuclear fusion devices, will be the first approach to reach reactor class prototyping. Plasma start-up is expected to be more challenging in large superconducting next-step tokamaks such as ITER due to the low inductive toroidal electric field and potentially long durations in limiter configuration when plasma-wall interactions lead to easier impurity contamination of the confined plasma. Such limiter start-up is the standard way of early plasma formation in the vast majority of today's experimental devices and is planned on ITER. To mitigate these issues, a novel plasma start-up scheme with divertor geometry only (DIVO start-up) was recently developed for the first time on the EAST superconducting tokamak. The key breakthrough in this work is the use of a non-inductive, electron cyclotron wave generated plasma formed in a poloidal field configuration which is a superposition of a barrel-like geometry around the centre of the vacuum vessel and a mirror-like geometry across the whole vessel cross-section. Such a non-inductive discharge avoids the drawback of low inductive electric field which is unavoidable in large superconducting devices as a consequence of the relatively low voltages which can be applied to the magnet coils. In addition to the low toroidal electric field, the DIVO start-up scheme as demonstrated on EAST significantly reduces impurity sources compared to the conventional limiter phase approach, even in cases with relatively poorly conditioned plasma-facing surfaces. The robustness of the DIVO start-up has also been verified on EAST with varying prefill gas pressure, impurity level and inductive electric field. It thus offers a potential solution to one of the main issues facing routine successful start-up on large tokamak reactors.

items.title: In Situ Training of Optical Neural Networks by Coding Agents
items.summary: Optical neural networks promise fast, energy-efficient computing, but every device departs from its design and must be trained with the hardware. In situ training relies on an expert-built calibrated digital model of each device or on gradient-free trial and error. Coding agents, large language models that write and run programs, have shown an emergent ability to understand and edit the weights of digital neural networks. Here we introduce optics as code, a method in which a coding agent trains an optical neural network from measurements alone, through a harness that returns camera images of its probes and requires a hypothesis per request. We discovered that the agent forms a physical understanding of the optics and reparametrizes the network with interpretable optical elements tuned on the hardware. It outperforms gradient-free methods in classification and image encoding, approaching backpropagation through a calibrated model at a fraction of the cost. Needing neither per-device calibration nor gradients through the hardware, and improving with more capable models, optics as code offers a practical route to large, scalable optical neural networks and a general tool for calibrating and optimizing optical experiments.

items.title: Technical Note on Matlantis PFP v9: Extending the Element and Domain Coverage of the r2SCAN Training Data
items.summary: Universal machine learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) make atomistic simulations possible at scales beyond the reach of density functional theory (DFT). Matlantis PFP is a uMLIP that treats a variety of domains, including crystals, molecules, and surfaces, with a single model. PFP v8 incorporated a training dataset computed with the r2SCAN functional, chosen for its good agreement with experiment, but the elements and domains covered by that dataset were limited. Here we present Matlantis PFP v9, in which the training data computed with the r2SCAN functional are extended to the lanthanides from Pr to Lu and to the elements from Po to Cm, for a total of 96 elements, and to additional domains such as clusters and adsorption structures. The formation energies of crystals containing the newly supported elements reproduce experimental standard enthalpies of formation with the same level of accuracy as crystals composed only of previously supported elements, and the adsorption energies of molecules on transition-metal surfaces have an overall error against experiment comparable to that of DFT-PBE, although chemisorbed species are overbound. On the same type of GPU (A100), the inference speed and the maximum system size exceed those of SevenNet-Omni, a public uMLIP trained on r2SCAN data: forces are evaluated three to four times faster, and five to ten times as many atoms can be handled. As a result, PFP-R2SCAN is now applicable to systems containing rare-earth and actinide elements and to adsorption on surfaces.

items.title: Localized active phase in the coevolving voter model with fixed links
items.summary: The coevolving voter model (CVM) describes the evolution of node states and network topology through copying and rewiring dynamics. It traditionally assumes that all ties can be rewired, overlooking unbreakable real-world relationships like family or close friendships. To address this, we introduce fixed links that cannot be rewired and study how these structural constraints modify the collective dynamics of the CVM. In addition to the active and frozen phases of the CVM, we find a new localized active phase in which activity is sustained, beyond a percolation transition, by a giant component of fixed links. The existence of this new phase is predicted by a moment-closure approximation that goes beyond the standard pair approximation. The finite-size manifestation of this phase is an asymmetric fragmented phase. In addition, the active-frozen transition of the CVM, manifested as a fragmentation transition for finite systems, is delayed by the existence of fixed links to larger values of the rewiring rate.

items.title: Comparing Data-Driven and Numerical Weather Prediction Forecasts of Extreme Weather: A Review
items.summary: Data-driven weather forecasting models, chiefly trained on reanalysis data, now match or beat physics-based numerical weather prediction (NWP) models on most headline scores, but whether this advantage extends to extreme weather is contested. We review peer-reviewed studies that directly compare data-driven forecasts with NWP for extremes, from nowcasting to subseasonal lead times. We discuss grey literature in the outlook but do not include it in the formal review. There is good agreement on the fact that data-driven models mostly outperform NWP on temperature extremes, tropical cyclone tracks and the location of synoptic features across time scales. The evidence is mixed for extreme precipitation and feature-based extreme event detection such as extremes related to atmospheric rivers, while it leans toward better NWP performance for estimating event intensity. For record-breaking events that lie outside the training distribution, the evidence is narrower. Nonetheless, both a systematic global evaluation and several case studies find that physics-based models retain the advantage, with data-driven models underestimating both the frequency and the magnitude of records. Hybrid systems that post-process NWP with machine-learning (ML), or couple data-driven forecasts with physics-based models, deliver some of the largest and most consistent gains. We argue that headline scores, verification choices and case selection explain much of the apparent disagreement in the literature, and provide recommendations for a more trustworthy and interpretable evaluation of data-driven models for extreme and record-breaking weather.

items.title: Euler-Lagrange Equations Formulated in Terms of Angular Velocity
items.summary: We propose a novel variant of the Euler--Lagrange (EL) equation for rigid body rotation, explicitly formulated in terms of orientation parameters $\thh$ and angular velocity $\omm$. Variational analysis of the stationarity condition of the action integral for a Lagrangian in terms of $\thh$ and $\omm$ yields a modified EL formulation. For pure rotational motion, the proposed equation directly recovers equations of motion fully consistent with the classical Euler equations, bypassing explicit geometry-based torque analysis. Furthermore, the framework seamlessly accommodates coupled translational and rotational dynamics, as validated through a spring-suspended symmetrical top, exhibiting exact agreement with the Newton--Euler equations. We also identify an inherent discrepancy in the standard EL approach, demonstrating that applying a direct coordinate transformation $\dot\thh\mapsto\omm$ causes the resulting formulation to deviate from both the classical Euler equation and our proposed formulation. The proposed framework is expected to provide an intuitive, versatile modeling tool for spatial rigid body dynamics.

items.title: Observation of Exact Mobility-Edge Phases in Two-Dimensional Photonic Quasicrystals
items.summary: Mobility edges, separating localized and extended states in energy, are central to localization physics. While exact mobility edges have been established in several one-dimensional quasiperiodic models, their realization in two dimensions remains largely unexplored. Here, we uncover a general route to exact mobility edges in the two-dimensional Aubry-Andre quasicrystal by introducing auxiliary subsystems. Through isospectral reduction, we reveal a hidden self-dual structure that yields exact mobility-edge conditions, separating extended, localized, and partially localized states in the spectrum. Tailoring the auxiliary structures controls the effective couplings and resulting mobility edge configurations, while auxiliary resonances further support flat-band states. In a decorated Lieb-type quasicrystal, we experimentally realize these predicted phases in photonic waveguide lattices and probe their energy-dependent localization through site-selective quench dynamics. Our results provide a versatile platform for controlling localization and can be readily extended to other physical platforms and higher-dimensional systems.

items.title: A State-Level Assessment of Space Weather Impact on the Virginia Power Grid: From Vulnerability to Mitigation Strategies
items.summary: Contemporary methodologies exist for assessing the nationwide impacts of geomagnetically induced currents (GICs), such as the Coupled Space Weather Impact Model (C-SWIM), which links power grid vulnerability with economic losses. Yet regional mitigation requires adapting the national model to the local transmission network so operators and planners can identify substations at risk and evaluate economic and population consequences and protective actions. We present the first adaptation of C-SWIM to Virginia, modeling the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnection, which includes Dominion Energy Virginia and Appalachian Power. Its extra high voltage network was assessed under the May 2024 Gannon, October 2003 Halloween, and March 2015 St. Patrick's Day storms in addition to nine return period scenarios derived from statistical fits to 92 historical events. Using the Leontief consumption and production input-output model, we estimated daily losses of USD 145.5M for a 100-year storm and USD 230.6M for a 250-year storm, with 339,000-535,000 people and up to 12,000 businesses at risk of power outage. The Ghosh input-output model was used to evaluate three island selection algorithms for protective islanding, which temporarily disconnects parts of the grid to reduce transformer damage. Only one algorithm yielded benefits exceeding costs across all twelve scenarios, with avoided losses up to USD 9.69M per day and a cost of USD 0.204M per intervention. However, these islanding benefits assume disconnection for 6 hours and transformer replacement after 365 days. Moreover, the analysis uses national economic relationships and models only transformer thermal failure, excluding voltage collapse, cascading failures, and restoration. Transmission operators and state energy policymakers can use this statewide assessment to prioritize regional monitoring and appraise protective islanding.

items.title: Geometry-bridge flow matching for blind rigid-motion correction in head cone-beam CT
items.summary: Rigid motion of a patient head during head cone-beam CT (CBCT) scan can degrade image quality and complicate recovery of accurate anatomical structures from the measured projections. We present a 3D flow-matching prior approach that learns the image changes induced by motion. Its geometry-bridge connects motion-corrupted and motion-free Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) reconstructed images of the same source volume through progressively reduced simulated motion. The forward projector's geometry derivative supplies analytic velocity targets along this path. A plug-and-play loop encompasses the learned image updates together with spline-based pose estimation, conjugate-gradient data consistency, and image total-variation regularization. Both the refined image volume and the FDK reconstructed image volume at the estimated poses are evaluated. On simulated 360-view scans from 30 held-out CQ500 patients with nominal per-component motion amplitudes within 10 mm / 10 degrees, the framework achieved state-of-the-art image reconstruction quality and motion accuracy in comparison with other methos such as learned autofocus and diffusion-based joint reconstruction. Mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) reached 37.1 dB and mean detector-plane reprojection error (RPE) was 0.27 mm. With matched endpoints at the inference settings, the geometry bridge improved PSNR by 1.6 dB and reduced RPE by 33% relative to image-linear training. With 50 prior updates and coarse-to-fine motion estimation, total processing time averaged 9.1 minutes per patient on an RTX A6000.

items.title: Learning Similarity-Reduced Ion Kinetics across Scales and Regimes in Capacitively Coupled Plasmas
items.summary: Systematic kinetic investigations of discharge-mode and heating-mechanism transitions in low-pressure capacitively coupled plasmas (CCPs) are computationally expensive because particle-in-cell/Monte Carlo collision (PIC/MCC) simulations must resolve the inherently slow ion relaxation. In this Letter, we propose a similarity-reduced ion-kinetic representation and a machine learning (ML) reconstruction method for weakly ionized Boltzmann-Poisson discharge systems. Using discharge similarity, the three-dimensional control parameter space, comprising gas pressure p, gap distance d, and driving frequency f, is reduced into a two-dimensional similarity space (pd, fd). A dual-branch ML model predicts the ion density profile at the reference scale and the conditional ion velocity distribution. Taking a 1D3V argon discharge as the paradigm, we use the reconstructed ion kinetic state to initialize the PIC/MCC simulation, which then relaxes to a self-consistent periodic steady state after only a brief evolution. Compared to conventional uniform initializations, this approach achieves a maximum computational speedup of 56.8 times and a median speedup of 27.7 times. Furthermore, the physical regimes of complex nonlinear discharge transitions, including the alpha-gamma mode transition, local-to-nonlocal electron collisional heating mode transition and low-density jumps, are accurately mapped within the similarity space. Similarity transformations extend these boundaries across scales, opening a new avenue for rapid kinetic characterization and optimization of radio-frequency plasma sources.

items.title: Residual diffusion for fine-structure enhancement in low-count accelerator-based muon imaging
items.summary: Accelerator-based muon imaging combines the penetrating power of high-energy muons with selectable momentum and a controlled beam direction, offering a powerful means of probing internal structures in large, dense and heavily shielded objects. Within a fixed beam-time budget, realizing this potential requires reliable recovery of fine structures from limited muon statistics. We propose an observation-conditioned residual diffusion method with decoupled linear schedules to enhance low-count muon images through iterative restoration guided by the observed image. We evaluate a simplified VSC-24 fuel cask under an idealized 5 GeV parallel muon beam, using 500,000 accepted events per low-count image and 40 million per reference image. Simulation results show improved recovery of structural boundaries and fine details, with the mean peak signal-to-noise ratio increasing from 11.4239 to 22.1719 dB. These findings highlight the potential of diffusion models to make more effective use of limited muon data and broaden the application of accelerator-based muon imaging across scientific and industrial settings.

items.title: Kernel Design in Particle Mesh Ewald Methods: Splitting, Interpolation, and Upsampling
items.summary: For more than thirty years, particle mesh Ewald (PME) methods have dominated the computation of electrostatic interactions in molecular dynamics. A PME method uses a splitting kernel to divide the interaction into a local part, summed within a cutoff, and a smooth part, computed on a grid with a spreading and interpolation (SI) kernel. The established methods use Ewald's Gaussian split with B-spline SI kernels, and the recent Ewald summation with prolates accelerates them severalfold by using a prolate spheroidal wave function (PSWF) for both kernels. Neither choice meets two needs of molecular dynamics: a smooth energy, which long simulations need in order to conserve it, and a low-order SI kernel that stays accurate on coarse grids and gains accuracy as the grid is refined. We present a framework for designing both kernels to meet these needs. For inverse powers from the Coulomb to the dispersion interaction, our splits make the local part smooth at the cutoff to any order while keeping the Fourier concentration of the smooth part close to optimal. We show that with analytic differentiation, the force error of a continuous SI kernel of fixed shape vanishes under grid refinement only if every particle, wherever it lies, gives the grid its exact charge and dipole moment. Our SI kernel for the Coulomb interaction ensures this by construction and is twice continuously differentiable. Compared with the B-spline of the same order, it needs fewer grid points by a factor of up to nearly five; on coarse grids, it mostly needs a lower order than the PSWF kernel. In simulations of liquid water over 100 million time steps, the new kernels reduce the energy drift of both the established and the PSWF kernels by about three orders of magnitude, with a smaller force error than either. Existing PME codes can adopt them by replacing only the two kernels and the Fourier multiplier.

items.title: XANES-Guided Molecular Structure Generation via Conditional Diffusion and Forward Spectral Prediction
items.summary: Reconstructing complete molecular structures from X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra remains challenging because the spectra primarily encode local chemical environments, with overlapping contributions from multiple absorbing sites. Here, we develop an inverse-forward framework combining XANES-conditioned diffusion-based molecular structure generation with forward spectral prediction for candidate selection. The inverse model generates atomic species, bond connectivity, and three-dimensional coordinates from C, N, and O K-edge XANES, given only the total atom count without molecular formulas or element-specific atom counts. Combining all three absorption edges substantially improves structural recovery, achieving a best-of-10 exact-match rate of 56.6% across 2,888 test molecules. The generated candidates also reproduce functional groups and structural motifs, achieving a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.951 across 21 categories. Ranking candidates by agreement between input and forward-predicted spectra increases the exact-match rate from 24.3% for unranked top-1 selection to 43.9%. This spectral-consistency criterion also enables atom count estimation, identifying the correct count for 65.6% of molecules among seven tested values. Application to experimental spectra yields an exact structural match for imidazole and recovers characteristic functional groups in two additional molecules, while revealing limitations due to simulation-experiment spectral discrepancies. These findings establish an inverse-forward approach for reconstructing whole-molecule structures from complementary element-specific XANES information.

items.title: Producing $μ$Bq/m3-level low-226Ra ultrapure water for the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory
items.summary: The Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO), a 20 kton low-background liquid-scintillator (LS) detector, was designed primarily to determine the neutrino mass ordering. JUNO requires ultrapure water (UPW) with a Ra concentration < 50~$μ$Bq/m3 because of the direct liquid-liquid contact between LS and UPW during detector filling. To meet this stringent requirement, a high-sensitivity measurement system capable of detecting Ra in water down to 3.9 $μ$Bq/m3 was developed, and the 100 t/h UPW production process was optimized. By integrating selective ion-exchange resin with membrane-based separation technologies, the system consistently produced UPW with a Ra concentration of <4$μ$Bq/m3, exceeding the JUNO specification and, to our knowledge, representing one of the lowest reported levels achieved at this engineering scale. This paper describes the design and implementation of JUNO's UPW system and the high-sensitivity Ra measurement platform, together with a systematic evaluation of Ra removal efficiencies across the purification train and validation of the final water quality.

items.title: Transversal surface-code game with reconfigurable qubits
items.summary: Qubit platforms supporting flexible connectivity have opened the door to theoretical advances in fault-tolerant quantum computation (FTQC), offering a compelling alternative to lattice surgery by leveraging transversal gates. Among such systems, neutral atoms have demonstrated notable progress enabled by large-scale parallel atom transport. However, a crucial gap remains between the theory of FTQC and its practical realization with these systems. Most critically, a key theoretical requirement, that syndrome extraction must be performed frequently enough to keep error accumulation below a threshold constant, is not satisfied in a scalable manner in the existing approach due to increased transport times. In this work, we develop a theoretical framework that closes such a gap, bridging theoretical advances in fault-tolerant protocols with the latest experimental capabilities. Building on the "game of surface code" framework originally developed for superconducting qubits, we introduce an alternative game-based paradigm for transversal-gate FTQC, formulating the protocol as a transversal surface-code game governed by rules for mode transitions of code cells. The rulesets are designed to enable syndrome extraction at any intermediate step during logical gate implementation, ensuring compatibility with the threshold theorem, while fully exploiting the capabilities of the hardware to scale and accelerate FTQC. As an application, our framework offers a systematic methodology and high-level abstraction for resource estimation and optimization; an exemplary estimation for a neutral-atom system demonstrates performance competitive with a baseline lattice-surgery-based approach on superconducting qubits, even with physical operations orders of magnitude slower. These results bridge the theory and experiment of FTQC with reconfigurable qubits toward scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computers.

items.title: Assessing the enrichment of heat-producing elements in deep-mantle structures using a directional geoneutrino detector
items.summary: Determining the spatial distribution of heat-producing elements (HPEs) within the Earth is critical for understanding the planet's thermal and chemical evolution. A central debate is whether domains in the deep mantle, particularly the Large Low-Velocity Provinces (LLVP), represent anomalous, radiogenically enriched reservoirs. Variation in the surface flux of geoneutrinos provide a direct probe of Earth's internal radioactivity. However, current continental located detectors measure only the angle-integrated flux, leading to strong spatial trade-offs that substantially limit the ability of practical networks to uniquely resolve mantle compositional heterogeneity. In this study, we quantify the potential of directional geoneutrino detection to overcome this limitation. By evaluating realistic LLVP geometries in the context of the proposed Ocean Bottom Detector (OBD), we demonstrate that resolving the incoming direction of geoneutrinos can substantially improve the precision with which HPE enrichment in LLVPs can be constrained relative to the surrounding mantle, for a range of target angular resolutions envisioned for a future directional geoneutrino detector. These results indicate that future directional geoneutrino measurements could help determine whether LLVP host enhanced HPE abundances and assess their contribution to Earth's radiogenic heat budget. Such measurements would provide a new observational constraint on the chemical heterogeneity of the deep mantle and its role in Earth's long-term thermal evolution.

items.title: Brilliance: toward autonomous computational research in particle accelerator physics
items.summary: Computational research requires repeated decisions about models, calculations and the interpretation of results. We introduce Brilliance, an agent that combines large language models, reusable physics expertise and numerical simulation to construct and revise investigations in accelerator physics. Starting from a detailed expert-specified request, Brilliance develops an ideal storage-ring lattice meeting the specified emittance ceiling and sampled nonlinear-acceptance criteria after revising optics that fail particle-tracking tests. Further scientist-guided exploration produces a candidate with a natural emittance of 6.51 pm rad and millimeter-scale transverse acceptance, while exposing unresolved momentum-acceptance limitations. Using measured responses from the High Energy Photon Source, Brilliance also performs offline optics calibration consistent with an independent specialist analysis. An expert-module ablation examines how reusable domain knowledge influences research choices and outcomes. Here, we demonstrate a practical route to scientist-agent collaboration in sustained numerical research.

items.title: Simultaneous spectral measurement and programmable filtering on a universal silicon photonic chip
items.summary: Spectral measurement and spectral filtering are two fundamental operations in optics, yet they are conventionally implemented using separate optical systems, hindering their simultaneous and programmable operation on a common platform. Here, we demonstrate a universal silicon photonic chip that unifies spectral measurement and programmable filtering within a single integrated architecture. The chip comprises two 8 * 8 programmable unitary transformation circuits interconnected through optical intensity modulators, forming a universal linear optical circuit. In contrast to conventional universal circuits employing equal-length interconnections, we deliberately introduce different optical path lengths between the two unitary circuits. The resulting wavelength-dependent phase evolution provides spectral diversity while preserving the programmability of the universal circuit, enabling parallel spectral measurement and programmable filtering. The fabricated chip achieves a spectral resolution of 0.05 nm over a bandwidth exceeding 100 nm, simultaneously measures eight independent laser sources, and generates multiple programmable spectral filter functions. We further demonstrate simultaneous spectral measurement and filtering during dynamic reconfiguration of the filter functions. These results establish universal photonic circuits as a versatile platform for integrating spectral sensing and programmable optical processing on a single chip.

items.title: MAIC-2 v2.3: A Fortran program for simulating the surface temperature, atmospheric water transport and surface glaciation of the planet Mars
items.summary: The Mars Atmosphere-Ice Coupler MAIC-2 is a computationally efficient, zonally-averaged model designed to simulate Martian surface temperature, atmospheric water transport and surface glaciation over timescales of 10^5 to 10^7 years. While sophisticated General Circulation Models (GCMs) provide high-resolution simulations of the Martian atmosphere, their high computational cost makes them largely unsuitable for studies covering millions of years of orbital evolution. MAIC-2 addresses this gap by utilizing physically-based, zonally-averaged parameterizations, including a Local Insolation Temperature (LIT) scheme and a mass balance engine driven by free-convection and instantaneous mixing physics. Version 2.3 introduces a fully modularized Fortran architecture that improves maintainability and ensures that the software remains entirely self-contained, requiring no external numerical libraries or specialized data formats for execution. Demonstrated through a 20-million-year transient simulation, the model successfully reproduces the primary characteristics of the Martian polar layered deposits. MAIC-2 provides the planetary science community with a versatile, open-source tool for investigating the long-term climatic impacts of orbital variations on the Martian surface.

items.title: UNWRAP: Single-shot phase analysis of bright squeezed vacuum by Newton-ring interferometry
items.summary: The mean field of pulsed bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) vanishes, but the variance can be large, and is strongly phase-dependent. We employ ultrafast Newton-ring wavefront retrieval and analysis of phase (UNWRAP) to extract the field amplitude and phase profile of each BSV pulse, by Fourier analysis of the interference rings between the BSV and a coherent reference with different phase-front curvature. The concentric ring interference fringes are robust against pointing mismatch and drift, thereby simplifying the analysis. The measured distribution has two phase peaks separated by $π$ radians. The rings sweep the delay between the two pulses, so a single frame can capture the temporal structure of the BSV field, even when it is composed of several temporal modes.

items.title: Time-Varying Bayesian Optimization and Extremum Seekingfor Drift-Tube Linac Tuning at LANSCE
items.summary: Bayesian optimization (BO) has emerged as a promising machine learning approach to accelerator tuning. It has the advantage of being able to incorporate prior information, including simulation and historical data, and explicitly model measurement noise. However, standard implementations can produce large, abrupt parameter updates that are undesirable and potentially unsafe in accelerator operation. They may also spend excessive time exploring less promising regions of the search space. We address these limitations by imposing soft and hard step size limits. We evaluate these methods by adjusting the radio frequency settings of the drift tube linac (DTL) at the Los Alamos Neutron Science Center (LANSCE) to maximize the particle count at the end of the linac. We first test the methods in simulation with constant exogenous parameters, then repeat the tests with drifting exogenous parameters. Under drifting conditions, progressively reducing the BO step size limit improved convergence. We also find that an initial BO segment followed by extremum seeking (ES), an approach we call BO-ES, combines BO's use of prior information and sample efficiency with ES's effectiveness in local optimization and drift tracking. Finally, tests on the LANSCE accelerator with BO-ES demonstrate an approximately $25\%$ reduction in losses at the end of the linac across different configurations of historical and simulation data.

items.title: Optical Neural Networks Should Be Evaluated by Function, Not Only Physics
items.summary: Optical neural networks (ONNs) are attracting significant attention as alternative platforms for machine learning (ML). In an ONN, an optical module often takes over part of the computation inside a digital ML pipeline. How much of the task does the optical module itself perform, and how much does it contribute to any claimed system-level advantages, such as throughput or energy? This paper offers a simple, function-oriented evaluation methodology. Whatever its internal physics, the optical module appears to the surrounding digital pipeline as a mapping between real-valued tensors. We therefore evaluate it in three steps: (i) define its boundary in the pipeline, as real-valued tensors in and out; (ii) replace it with standard digital modules to identify those that match the optical system's performance on the same task and metric; and (iii) state system-level claims, such as speed or energy, per inference against the performance-matched digital module. We summarize steps (i) and (ii) in an Expressivity Card and demonstrate its use on published ONN systems. This helps isolate the optical module's contribution and provides a concrete digital reference for assessing its claimed system-level advantages, without the need to understand the physics. While we focus on optical systems as the most prominent example, the same approach applies to any physical analog computing platform used in ML, wherever a physical module takes over part of a digital pipeline.

items.title: Retinal arterial velocity-proxy waveforms from differential spectral broadening in laser Doppler holography
items.summary: Laser Doppler holography (LDH) records pulsatile spectral broadening in retinal arteries. We compare vessel and local-background measurements to extract a signed differential-broadening waveform, $Δσ$. A minimal Gaussian convolution model motivates quadratic subtraction, and Doppler scaling relates the added width to a characteristic blood velocity. Real arteries show pulsatile waveforms, whereas identically processed imaginary arteries show only low-amplitude fluctuations around zero. We interpret the empirically scaled signal as a velocity proxy for waveform shape and within-vessel changes during a single acquisition under stable conditions.

items.title: Relative periodic orbits of a free spinning loop
items.summary: A closed elastic string with no external forces can hold any shape while its material moves steadily along the curve (a steady axial motion), because its tension and the force needed to turn the material around a bend are both proportional to the curvature. I compute the periodic motions that grow from the simplest of these motions, the spinning ring, by Newton's method on a chain of masses. They include rotating waves that turn at twice the rotation rate of the material, standing "flappers" with two to five lobes, and period-doubled and period-tripled orbits. The chain only approximates the string. The orbits and their strong instabilities change little with more masses and are properties of the continuous string. Most weak instabilities change with the number of masses and are artifacts of approximating the string by a finite chain. The saddle flapper of a loop stretched 30% beyond its natural length is neutrally stable at small heights and unstable at large ones. An unstable saddle flapper trades energy back and forth with an in-plane oval, and at large amplitude the energy spreads to the shortest waves of the chain. For Keller's linear string, whose tension is proportional to the stretched length, every motion is periodic, and every knot carries an exactly periodic flapper. For a Hookean string the curvature of a knot couples a ripple to stretching waves that travel at a different speed, and in the simulations a ripple on a sliding knot does not return to its starting shape. Whether a Hookean knot carries any periodic flapper is open.

items.title: Machine-learned acceleration of earthquake sequence simulations
items.summary: Earthquake sequence simulations involve slow interseismic processes and rapid dynamic ruptures. During interseismic periods, a numerical solver can take large time steps efficiently. During seismic periods, in contrast, the solver must drastically reduce the time step, and elastodynamic wave-mediated memory effects become significant; long-term simulations are therefore computationally expensive. We investigate the use of neural operators to accelerate earthquake sequence simulations. We train a Fourier neural operator (FNO) on data from high-fidelity, fully dynamic simulations to learn a jump map that advances the system state from before a seismic rupture to after it. We propose a hybrid modeling framework in which a conventional quasi-dynamic solver simulates the slow interseismic evolution, and the trained FNO replaces the solver during the computationally intensive seismic periods with wave-mediated inertial effects. The hybrid model reproduces key long-term statistics of fully dynamic simulations, including distributions of event magnitudes and recurrence times. Furthermore, it provides a much better approximation to the fully dynamic simulations than the commonly used quasi-dynamic approximation at a reduced computational expense.

items.title: Deep-Learning-Assisted Full Waveform Inversion for Attenuation Reconstruction in Ultrasound Computed Tomography
items.summary: Acoustic attenuation is more challenging to reconstruct and has received less attention than sound speed in ultrasound computed tomography using full-waveform inversion (FWI). In this study, a deep-learning (DL)-assisted FWI framework was proposed for attenuation reconstruction based on our previous work. Some numerical experiments were conducted to investigate the strategy and the effectiveness of using DL to help accelerate and improve the reconstruction quality of attenuation imaging in FWI. The results indicated that DL saved computational cost by 28% and improved attenuation reconstruction accuracy by 70% when combined with sufficiently accurate sound speed estimates. The result supports the potential of DL initialization to improve the computational efficiency and reconstruction quality of joint SOS and attenuation FWI.

items.title: Quantitative Modeling of Action-Potential-Driven Sodium Dynamics in Neurons: From Sodium Influx to Sodium MRI
items.summary: Neuronal action potentials are accompanied by the influx of extracellular sodium ions (Na+) into axons through voltage-gated sodium channels. Repetitive neuronal firing can lead to activity-dependent increases in intracellular sodium concentration, which are subsequently reversed primarily through the Na+/K+-ATPase. Quantifying these dynamic changes provides a biophysical foundation for investigating neuronal activity using sodium (23Na) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
