items.summary: In 1997, Catanese and the first author showed that, for every $m\geq 2$, there exists a smooth closed $4m$-manifold that admits both a $λ> 0$ Einstein metric and a $λ< 0$ Einstein metric; thus, the sign of the Einstein constant $λ$ is not always determined by the differential topology of the host compact manifold. This result was later improved by Răsdeaconu and Şuvaina (2009), who showed that there are in fact at least $\binom{m + 3}{3}$ topologically distinct such examples in each dimension $4m$, $m\geq 2$. In this note, we further improve these earlier results by showing that infinitely many topologically distinct examples of this phenomenon actually occur in dimension $4m$, for each $m\geq 2$.

items.title: Sharp Partial Regularity of Weakly Pseudoholomorphic Maps Into Projective Algebraic Varieties
items.summary: For every $m\geq2$, we prove that a weakly pseudoholomorphic $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ map from a real-analytic almost complex $2m$-manifold into a projective algebraic variety has a countably $(2m-4)$-rectifiable singular set. When $m=2$, the singular set is shown to be locally finite. We first establish both conclusions on smooth almost complex domains under the additional assumption that the pullback of the Fubini--Study form is distributionally closed. We then show that this conservation law follows from the Cauchy--Riemann equation alone on real-analytic domains.

items.title: Smooth structures on polyhedral products of disks and spheres
items.summary: We prove that every polyhedral product of disks and their boundary spheres that is a topological manifold admits a stably parallelizable smooth structure. We also show that if a moment-angle complex or a real moment-angle complex admits a smooth structure for which the coordinate action is smooth, then the link of every face of the underlying simplicial complex is a simplicial sphere, and every such smooth structure is stably parallelizable.

items.title: The commutator subgroup of the Torelli group of a genus-three surface has finitely generated abelianization
items.summary: We prove that the commutator subgroup of the Torelli group of a genus-three surface with at most one boundary component has finitely generated abelianization. The proof combines Gaifullin's finite-generation sufficient condition with the explicit generating set for the Torelli commutator subgroup due to Brendle, Margalit, and Putman.

items.title: On the $L^p$-Neumann problem for divergence form elliptic equations in the upper half-space
items.summary: A central question has been whether the $L^p$-Neumann problem is solvable for some $p\in(1,\infty)$ in the upper half-space $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+:=\mathbb{R}^n\times(0,\infty)$, $n\geq2$, for second-order uniformly elliptic equations in divergence form whose coefficients are either independent of the transverse variable or satisfy the Dahlberg--Kenig--Pipher (DKP) condition. We answer this question in the negative for both classes, even for matrices whose symmetric part is the identity. The two examples have the same nonzero Neumann datum $g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ of mean zero. Although $g$ is bounded and belongs to the real Hardy space $H^1(\mathbb R^n)$, neither equation admits a weak solution with this datum whose gradient has a non-tangential maximal function in $L^p(\mathbb R^n)$ for any $1\leq p<\infty$. For the variational solution $u$ associated with either matrix $A$, the non-tangential maximal functions of $\nabla_x u$, $\partial_tu$ and $(A\nabla u)_{n+1}$ each have infinite $L^p$ norm for every $1\leq p\leq\infty$. In the example with coefficients independent of the transverse variable, the equation in the interior is the Laplace equation. The matrix in the DKP example has finite $L^2$-type Carleson discrepancy from the identity. This shows that solvability of the $L^p$-Neumann problem is not stable under arbitrary Carleson perturbations of the identity. For a suitable choice of the coefficients in the lower half-space, the $L^2$ non-tangential maximal and uniform slice estimates fail for both the tangential gradient and the transverse derivative of the associated single layer potential. The $L^2$ estimate for the tangential gradient of its boundary trace also fails. We explain the role of the coefficients below the boundary and prove the $L^2$ layer potential estimates for the reflected extension when the DKP norm is sufficiently small.

items.title: Local-global compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed (co)homology of $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields
items.summary: For each place $v \mid p$ such that $F_v \simeq \mathbf{Q}_p$, we establish a compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed homology with integral coefficients for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields $F$ with $[F:\mathbf{Q}]>2$, after localization with respect to a non-Eisenstein decomposed generic maximal ideal of a Hecke algebra.

items.title: An accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping
items.summary: In this paper, we propose an accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping for unconstrained convex multiobjective optimization problems in a real Hilbert space. The continuous flow is formulated as a system of two first-order equations involving only a single multiobjective projection operator and suitable time-scaling factors. Formally, it can also be expressed as a second-order system with explicit multiobjective Hessian-driven damping, which corresponds to the usual Hessian-driven damping introduced by Alvarez et al. [J. Math. Pures Appl., 81(8):747--779, 2002]. The first-order formulation, however, involves no Hessian term and can be regarded as an extension of the Hessian-driven Nesterov accelerated gradient flow by Chen and Luo [arXiv:1912.09276, 2019]. Assuming that the objective gradients are Lipschitz continuous on bounded sets and that the common lower level sets are bounded, we establish global existence in finite dimensions under suitable time-scaling conditions. An a priori energy estimate confines the solutions to a fixed bounded set, and a Lyapunov argument yields fast decay of a merit function and the KKT residual. Under an additional bound on the time-scaling factors, the trajectory of every global solution converges weakly to a weak Pareto point. Numerical tests illustrate the rapid residual decay and reduced oscillations.

items.title: A Poisson boundary solution to Connes' bicentralizer conjecture and Kadison's problem on MASA
items.summary: We prove that, for every inclusion $M\subset P$ of countably decomposable von Neumann algebras with a normal faithful conditional expectation, $M\subset c(P)$ has the weak Dixmier property, where $c(P)$ is the continuous core of $P$. By Haagerup's characterization, we have a completely new proof of Connes' bicentralizer conjecture, independent of the recent proof of Houdayer--Marrakchi. By Marrakchi's characterization, we also prove his relative bicentralizer conjecture. We also give a new solution to Kadison's problem after Popa and Marrakchi: further assuming that $M$ and $P$ have separable preduals and $M'\cap P=\mathcal Z(M)$, then there is a maximal abelian subalgebra of $M$ that is also maximal abelian in $P$. The proofs are based on a Poisson boundary theory for general von Neumann algebras, developed here as an extension of the theory of Das--Peterson for finite von Neumann algebras. Once this theory is established, the proofs for Connes' bicentralizer conjecture and Kadison's problem are short (around 7 pages each) and self-contained, relying only on results established by 1990. In both proofs, no separate treatment is needed for the type $\mathrm{III}_1$ case.

items.title: Fourier--Galerkin Methods for Subwavelength Resonances in two-dimensional Acoustic Metamaterials
items.summary: We present a Fourier--Galerkin asymptotic framework for the analysis and computation of subwavelength resonances in two-dimensional scattering problems in finite domains. Starting from the boundary integral formulation, we apply a Fourier--Galerkin discretization to derive an explicit finite-dimensional effective matrix whose kernel characterizes the resonant frequencies. In the subwavelength regime, we obtain asymptotic expansions of this matrix in terms of $ω$ and the material contrast, identifying the leading-order operators and their kernel structure. This reduction transforms the resonance problem into a low-dimensional nonlinear eigenvalue problem, avoiding large-scale discretizations and global root-search procedures. The entries of the effective matrix are explicitly computable and admit fast evaluation using FFT-based quadrature. The resulting approach provides an efficient and robust computational framework for resonances in general smooth geometries.

items.title: Geometric and Combinatorial Properties of the Alternating Sign Matrix Polytope
items.summary: The polytope $ASM_n$, the convex hull of the $n\times n$ alternating sign matrices, was introduced by Striker and by Behrend and Knight. A face of $ASM_n$ corresponds to an elementary flow grid defined by Striker, and each elementary flow grid determines a doubly directed graph defined by Brualdi and Dahl. We show that a face of $ASM_n$ is centrally symmetric if and only if its doubly directed graph has all vertices of even degree. We show that every face of $ASM_n$ is a 2-level polytope. We show that a $d$-dimensional face of $ASM_n$ has at most $2^d$ vertices and $4(d-1)$ facets, for $d\ge 2$. We show that a $d$-dimensional face of $ASM_n$ satisfies $vf\le d2^{d+1}$, where $v$ and $f$ are the numbers of vertices and edges of the face. If the doubly directed graph of a $d$-dimensional face is 2-connected, then $v\le 2^{d-1}+2$. We describe the facets of a face and a basis for the subspace parallel to a face in terms of the elementary flow grid of the face. We prove that no face of $ASM_n$ has the combinatorial type of the Birkhoff polytope $B_3$. We list the combinatorial types of faces of $ASM_n$ that have dimension 4 or less.

items.title: Sharpness of the Osgood threshold for anomalous dissipation and non-uniqueness in passive scalar transport
items.summary: We prove that for any concave, non-Osgood modulus of continuity $ω$, there exists a divergence-free velocity field $u\in L^\infty([0,1];C^ω(\mathbb T^2))$ and an initial data $f_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^2)$ such that the solutions of the associated advection-diffusion equation exhibit anomalous dissipation. This establishes the sharpness of the Osgood threshold for anomalous dissipation. It follows as a corollary of our main result that the Osgood condition is also sharp for the uniqueness of bounded solutions to the transport equation.

items.title: Solution of Laczkovich's Lipschitz mapping problem
items.summary: In 1991, Laczkovich asked whether every measurable set of positive measure in $\mathbb R^d$ can be mapped onto a cube with a Lipschitz map. We show that the answer is positive for every $d$. Our results also give a positive answer for Kolmogorov's problem on contractions onto polygons with small measure loss in the case of Jordan measurable sets.

items.title: A disproof of the van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk conjecture on the Davenport constant
items.summary: The Davenport constant $D(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence $S$ with terms from $G$ and with length $|S| \ge \ell$ has a nontrivial zero-sum subsequence. A long-standing conjecture, first proposed by van Emde Boas and Kruyswijk in 1969, states that $D(C_n^r)=r(n-1)+1$ for all positive integers $n$ and $r$. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture by showing that $D(C_6^r)>5r+1$ for every $r\ge23$.

items.title: Behind the equivalent descriptions of the Loewner energy
items.summary: This expository paper retells the story behind the paper "Equivalent descriptions of the Loewner energy," which uncovered the link between random fractal SLE curves and the Kähler geometry of universal Teichmüller space via the Loewner energy. It is written for the Proceedings of ICBS as the summary paper for the 2026 Frontiers of Science award.

items.title: On the Beauville Dimension of Finite Abelian Groups
items.summary: Unmixed Beauville manifolds of general type are rigid quotients of products of compact complex curves of higher genus by free diagonal actions of finite groups. Their biholomorphism classes are encoded by equivalence classes of group-theoretic data. For a finite abelian group $G$, we characterize when these data exist and determine the unmixed Beauville dimension $\mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)$, the minimum dimension of such a manifold arising from a diagonal action of $G$. We prove that $\mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)<\infty$ if and only if $\exp(G)$ is odd and greater than $3$, and the largest invariant factor of $G$ occurs at least twice. In that case, \[ \mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)=\max\{\mathrm{rk}(G),\mathrm{rk}_3(G)+2\}. \] Specializing to $\mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)=2$ recovers the classical result of Bauer, Catanese and Grunewald: the finite abelian Beauville surface groups are precisely $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^2$ with $n>1$ and $\gcd(n,6)=1$. Although the Beauville dimension has a geometric origin, our proof is entirely group-theoretic and combinatorial.

items.title: Prime Density, Kolmogorov Quotients and Homeomorphisms between Macías Spaces of Integral Domains
items.summary: For an integral domain $R$ that is not a field, the Macías space $M(R)$ is the topological space whose underlying set $R^0=R\setminus\{0\}$ is endowed with the topology generated by the basis $\{σ_k^0:k\in R^0\}$, where $σ_k^0=\{x\in R^0:\langle x\rangle+\langle k\rangle=R\}$. We characterize the openness of the unit group in $M(R)$ via semiprimitivity and, for Dedekind domains and unique factorization domains (UFDs), relate semiprimitivity and the infinitude of prime elements to the density of irreducible and prime elements. We identify the Kolmogorov quotient of $M(R)$ with a space of sets of maximal ideals and reduce the homeomorphism problem to these quotients and the cardinalities of the fibers of the quotient maps; in particular, local domains of equal cardinality have homeomorphic Macías spaces. For Dedekind domains, we solve this problem in terms of the cardinalities of their unit groups and relations among the ideal classes of their maximal ideals, thereby answering the homeomorphism problem of Macías (2024) for countable semiprimitive ones. When the class groups are torsion, as they are for principal ideal domains, the cardinalities of the unit groups and of the sets of maximal ideals suffice. For UFDs, we characterize homeomorphic Macías spaces via comaximality with prime elements and, under an additional hypothesis, obtain a solution analogous to that for Dedekind domains. We solve the problem for several classes of polynomial rings over discrete valuation rings, UFDs and fields. Finally, we characterize additive homeomorphisms between Macías spaces of certain domains of characteristic zero via ring isomorphisms, partially answering a problem of Macías and Ortiz (2025).

items.title: Finite-rank and compact Toeplitz commutators on the harmonic Bergman space
items.summary: We completely characterize finite rank and compactness of commutators of Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on the harmonic Bergman space of the unit disk. Apart from affine dependence, finite rank occurs precisely when both symbols are analytic with rational primitives, or both are coanalytic and their complex conjugates have rational primitives. For compactness, the corresponding condition is asymptotic affine dependence on hyperbolic disks of a fixed radius. This boundary behavior is characterized by three weighted vanishing conditions involving a mixed first-derivative expression and two Wronskians of first derivatives, and therefore requires derivatives of order at most two. Our proofs combine a block-matrix decomposition and explicit kernel identities with Luecking's finite-rank theorem and affine boundary rescalings to the right half-plane. Only the full harmonic symbols are assumed bounded; their analytic components need not be bounded separately. As consequences, every finite-rank commutator has square zero, and the compactness criterion yields characterizations of essential normality and compactness for analytic and mixed symbol pairs.

items.title: Euclidean interval objects in categories with finite products
items.summary: Based on the intuitive notion of convexity, we formulate a universal property defining interval objects in a category with finite products. Interval objects are structures corresponding to closed intervals of the real line, but their definition does not assume a pre-existing notion of real number. The universal property characterises such structures up to isomorphism, supports the definition of functions between intervals, and provides a means of verifying identities between functions. In the category of sets, the universal property characterises closed intervals of real numbers with nonempty interior. In the category of topological spaces, we obtain intervals with the Euclidean topology. We also prove that every elementary topos with natural numbers object contains an interval object; furthermore, we characterise interval objects as intervals of real numbers in the Cauchy completion of the rational numbers within the Dedekind reals.

items.title: High-Dimensional Canonical Correlation Analysis
items.summary: This paper studies high-dimensional canonical correlation analysis (CCA) with an emphasis on the vectors that define canonical variables. The paper shows that when two dimensions of data grow to infinity jointly and proportionally, the classical CCA procedure for estimating those vectors fails to deliver a consistent estimate. This provides the first result on the impossibility of identification of canonical variables in the CCA procedure when all dimensions are large. As a countermeasure, the paper derives the magnitude of the estimation error, which can be used in practice to assess the precision of CCA estimates. Applications of the results to cyclical vs. non-cyclical stocks and to a limestone grassland data set are provided.

items.title: A Lions lift framework for gradient and Newtonian evolutions in Wasserstein spaces
items.summary: To analyze evolutions driven by functionals over the space of probability measures, one can opt for the extrinsic Lions lift approach or the intrinsic Wasserstein viewpoint with its abstract metric structure. While the latter has been a successful playground for the study of first-order gradient flows, it classically relies on $λ$-convexity, and has eluded attempts of extensions to second-order Newtonian-like dynamics. Motivated by these obstructions, we show that the extrinsic Lions lift has the full capabilities to carry out the first-order gradient-flow program, which is classically done intrinsically in the Wasserstein space. As illustrated in an example, this paves the way for a framework of gradient evolutions beyond the $λ$-convex case, which is classically demanded for energies in the Wasserstein space. Furthermore, our interpretation of the Lions lift enables the formulation of a notion of second-order Newtonian curves in the Wasserstein phase space. Such curves can be constructed through a second-order JKO-like scheme and, when applied to linear and interacting energies, naturally lead to Vlasov kinetic equations and existence of solutions thereof.

items.title: Quadratic splitting for a weighted Monge--Ampère equation on $(0,\infty)^l\times\R^m$
items.summary: We study a Monge--Ampère equation arising from the existence problem for complete Kähler--Einstein metrics with zero Ricci curvature on divisor complements. We prove a splitting theorem for nonnegative smooth strictly convex solutions on a product of positive half lines and a Euclidean space. The potential and its first derivatives extend continuously to the boundary. The directional derivative in the equation is positive in the interior and vanishes on the boundary. After an affine change of variables, the solution is the sum of a function on the product of half lines and a positive definite quadratic form in the Euclidean variables. No growth condition or homogeneity is assumed.

items.title: fOGA: An Orthogonal Greedy Algorithm for Fractional Laplacian Problems
items.summary: We extend energy-based orthogonal greedy approximation to integral fractional Poisson problems by combining OGA with discrete fractional operators. In one dimension, order-dependent Grünwald--Letnikov stencils are paired with boundary-corrected ReLU atoms. On the unit disk, a fractional centered-difference operator is constructed on a larger periodic lattice and restricted to the interior, while boundary-weighted ReLU$^2$ atoms impose the homogeneous exterior condition. The resulting symmetric positive definite matrices provide a common energy framework for normalized atom selection and orthogonal projection. We establish the corresponding discrete projection properties and separate operator discretization from approximation in the selected spaces. One- and two-dimensional experiments assess the method through $L^2$, $H^1$, and sampled maximum errors. The results demonstrate the applicability of the OGA extension to nonlocal problems and show the influence of boundary regularity on approximation, particularly in the $H^1$ error.

items.title: Exponential boundary stabilization of the KdV--KdV system with time-varying delay: the nonlinear case
items.summary: We consider a Boussinesq system of KdV--KdV type on a bounded interval, with a boundary feedback that includes a damping term with a time-varying delayed term. Although the exponential stability of the linearized system was established in [1] by a Lyapunov approach, global existence and stabilization for the nonlinear problem remained open. Here, we prove that, for sufficiently small initial data and under a suitable restriction on the interval length, the nonlinear system admits a unique global solution whose energy decays exponentially. In particular, we provide an explicit decay rate and a quantitative smallness condition on the initial energy. Our approach combines a Lyapunov argument with well-posedness estimates that are uniform under time translations of the delay, allowing the solutions to be continued globally.

items.title: Computing $F$-Symbols from Modular Data
items.summary: We present a strategy for computing the $F$-symbols of unitary modular categories with a self-dual simple generator, starting from their modular data, which almost entirely avoids the non-linear solution of the pentagon equations. The algorithm climbs a ladder of braid group representations on successively more strands of the generator until enough $F$-symbols have been determined to propagate them to a complete solution. The strategy presented is successful in difficult cases through ranks 11 and 12, including $\operatorname{Z}(\mathrm{Haagerup}_3)$, and does not require the category to be multiplicity-free. Although the algorithm is implemented numerically, we describe a reliable means of recovering the exact $F$-symbols, assuming that in some gauge they lie in a given number field, and of certifying every pentagon and hexagon equation exactly. The exotic rank-11 anisotropic modular category B11-00119 (https://anyonatlas.org/data/B11-00119), with largest fusion coefficient 4, is used as a motivating example, for which the solve takes roughly 10 minutes on a laptop. We will continue to add $F$-symbol solutions to https://AnyonAtlas.org as they are completed.

items.title: Learning the Anyon Atlas
items.summary: We extend our previous search for the modular data of topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions from 22 to 42 anyons, identifying 150,679 new modular data. We do so by adding to our algorithm three rejection gates, two of them based on logistic regression, that discard representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ unlikely to yield modular data. We estimate that roughly 80% of the modular data between ranks 23 and 42 has been identified after closing under known constructions. With this data, we find counterexamples to a conjecture of Geiko and Moore that the reality of the higher Gauss sums suffices for time-reversal symmetry in Chern-Simons theories, and propose a refined criterion. We demonstrate the scalability of this gated implementation by identifying prime modular data at rank 100 that is not realized by any Chern-Simons theory. The identified data through rank 42 has been made available at https://AnyonAtlas.org, to which further data will be added as it is found.

items.title: Lattice Moduli and Residual Atoms
items.summary: We classify fully framed regular-singular connections on prescribed lattices for arbitrary ordered monodromy eigenvalues, including resonances. The fully framed classification has a unique triangular normal form on each fixed-residue stratum, parametrised by an affine space of dimension $r(r-1)$. We determine the connection-compatible charts of elementary lattice modifications, including resonance walls and higher-root corrections. For geometric $F$-bundles we establish a reconstruction theorem for trace-centred connections with specified horizontal pairings and determine the information lost upon forgetting the trace scalar. For a meromorphic spectral decomposition and a prescribed lattice, a defect module measures the failure of its projectors to preserve that lattice. Its annihilator exponent is the exact common pole bound and changes by at most one under an elementary modification. We compute the defect at cyclic Fano quantum boundaries and show that, whenever formal horizontal lifts of the Higgs projectors exist, their pole orders are unbounded.

items.title: On the asymmetry polynomial of Schubert varieties
items.summary: Let $W$ be a finite Weyl group with length function $\ell$ and longest element $w_0$. For $w\in W$, let $P_w(q)$ be the Poincaré polynomial of the Schubert variety $X_w$. We introduce its asymmetry polynomial $D_w(q):=q^{\ell(w)}P_w(q^{-1})-P_w(q)$. Let $n\geq4$ and $W=S_n$ or $W(B_n)$. For $w\in W$ whose Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)$ satisfies $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=2$, we prove the sharp bound $[q^k]D_w(q)\leq[q^{k-1}]P_{w_0}(q)$ for $1\leq k<\ell(w)/2$. For every $n\geq3$ and $1\leq h\leq2n-4$, we construct an element $b=b_h^n\in W(B_n)$ with $P_{\mathrm{id},b}(q)=1+q^h$, and determine the asymmetry polynomial $D_b(q)$ and all Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials $P_{x,b}(q)$ for $x\leq b$.

items.title: On Hilbert's tenth problem for number fields
items.summary: Given a quadratic number field $K$ we show that the $abc$ conjecture over $K$ implies that $\mathbb{Z}$ is Diophantine in $K$ and, hence, a negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over $K$. More generally, the same conclusions hold for an arbitrary number field $K$ provided that the $abc$ conjecture holds over $K$ and that there is an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ whose rank is positive and does not increase over $K$.

items.title: Variation bounds for averages over nondegenerate curves
items.summary: In this article, we prove sharp variational estimates for averaging operators over non-degenerate curves in $\R^3.$ The sufficiency follows from dyadic localisation, Sobolev embedding, and local smoothing estimates, and the primary novelty of this article lies in obtaining sharp necessary conditions for variational estimates.

items.title: Minimal norm of regular vectors in the root lattice of a crystallographic root system
items.summary: For a crystallographic root system $Φ$ with Weyl group $W$ and root lattice $L = \mathbb{Z}Φ$, we determine the minimum norm of a vector of $L$ having trivial stabilizer in $W$, and we prove that the vectors attaining it form a single orbit of $W$. Although this is a minimization of a quadratic function over the lattice points of a cone, the minimizer in the dominant chamber is always unique: it is $ρ+ λ$, where $ρ$ is the Weyl vector and $λ$ is $0$ or the minuscule weight in the class of $ρ$ modulo $L$. In particular, the optimal vector is the Weyl vector exactly when the Weyl vector lies in $L$. We give explicit formulas for the families $A_n$, $B_n$, $C_n$ and $D_n$, with elementary proofs, and the values for the exceptional types $E_6$, $E_7$, $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$. Finally, we explain the coincidences between the minimal norms by the folding of Dynkin diagrams.

items.title: Generalized Limits of Finitely Additive Measures on Locally Compact Groups
items.summary: Let $\mathscr{E}$ be an increasing family of Borel subsets of a locally compact topological group $G$ and let $μ$ be a nonnegative finitely additive $σ$-finite measure on the Borel $σ$-algebra of $G$ whose values on $\mathscr{E}$ are finite but unbounded. Applying a generalized limit pointwise to the net of measures $\left\{B\mapsto\frac{μ(B\cap E)}{μ(E)}\right\}_{E\in \mathscr{E}}$ yields a finitely additive measure $\varphi_μ$, which can be viewed as a generalized normalization of $μ$ to total mass one. To obtain a nontrivial necessary condition on $μ$ for the resulting measure $\varphi_μ$ to be invariant, we establish two results of independent interest: we extend the Yosida--Hewitt decomposition to finitely additive $σ$-finite measures and prove a theorem previously stated by Bingham and Ostaszewski concerning translates of sets of Haar measure zero. The first theorem yields a decomposition of $μ$ into a purely finitely additive component and two countably additive components, respectively singular and absolutely continuous with respect to Haar measure. Using the second result, we show that the invariance of $\varphi_μ$ implies that the singular component $μ_s$ is negligible relative to $μ$ and can be removed without changing $\varphi_μ$. A counterexample demonstrates that the purely finitely additive component $μ_p$ need not have these properties.

items.title: Tackling Parallelization Challenges of Randomized Preconditioners With Dependency Tracking
items.summary: Incomplete Cholesky (IC) preconditioners are the standard black-box, memory-efficient first resort for large graph Laplacian systems, but classical IC can break down on irregular graphs. Approximate Cholesky (AC) addresses this with randomized dropping that is provably breakdown-free. Its stochastic fill-in pattern, however, resists static parallelization, creating a "setup bottleneck." We present ParAC, which parallelizes the sequential rchol algorithm on CPUs and GPUs using dynamic dependency tracking and architecture-aware memory management, without altering its numerics. Total time-to-solution speedups over deterministic IC reach $57.3\times$ on CPU and $52.2\times$ on GPU. Algebraic multigrid (AMG) remains preferable on structured PDE discretizations; on irregular graph Laplacians where AMG struggles, ParAC attains up to $7.2\times$ and $6.0\times$. On 200 adversarial SDD systems, ParAC converges on every instance, whereas the AMG solvers fail on 15 and 19, on CPU and GPU, respectively.

items.title: Simultaneous analysis of approximate leave-one-out cross-validation and mean-field inference I
items.summary: Approximate Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (ALO-CV) is a method that has been proposed to estimate the generalization error of a regularized estimator in the high-dimensional regime where dimension and sample size are of the same order, the so-called ``proportional regime''. A new analysis is developed to derive the consistency of ALO-CV for non-differentiable regularizers under Gaussian covariates and strong convexity. Using a conditioning argument, the difference between the ALO-CV weights and their counterparts in mean-field inference is shown to be small. Combined with upper bounds between the mean-field inference estimate and the leave-one-out quantity, this provides a proof that ALO-CV approximates the leave-one-out quantity up to negligible error terms. Linear models with square loss, robust linear regression and single-index models are explicitly treated.

items.title: Comparing Lower and Upper Spectral Gaps of Nonnegative Symmetric Matrices
items.summary: We establish sharp estimates comparing the lower and upper spectral gaps of nonnegative symmetric matrices. Combining these comparisons with a multiplicity argument in the spirit of Li and Liu, we improve and extend earlier spectral gap comparison bounds of Saha and Li and Liu, which provide quantitative refinements of an observation of Breuillard, Green, Guralnick and Tao relating combinatorial expansion to two-sided spectral expansion. Our graph estimates hold for nonbipartite even-walk-regular graphs, which covers the classes of graphs, including vertex-transitive graphs, (twisted) Cayley graphs, and (twisted) Cayley sum graphs, investigated in previous work. Under an additional eigenmap assumption, we also establish quantitative two-sided comparisons between the lower and upper spectral gaps. In particular, these comparisons apply to walk-regular graphs.

items.title: An Upper Bound on the Proportional Choice Number of a Graph
items.summary: Proportional choosability is a list analogue of equitable coloring introduced in 2019 that imposes both upper and lower bounds on color class sizes based on the availability of each color. The proportional choice number of a graph $G$, denoted by $χ_{pc}(G)$, is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that $G$ is proportionally $k$-choosable. A recently proposed conjecture states that for any graph $G$ with at least one edge, $χ_{pc}(G) \leq Δ(G) + \text{col}(G) - 1$, where $Δ(G)$ is the maximum degree of $G$ and $\text{col}(G)$ is its coloring number. In this paper, we prove this conjecture using a generalization of Edmonds' matroid intersection theorem due to Aharoni and Berger, in which one of the matroids is replaced with an abstract simplicial complex. As a consequence, we can completely determine the proportional choice number of every path: $χ_{pc}(P_1)=1$, $χ_{pc}(P_n)=2$ for $2 \leq n \leq 5$, and $χ_{pc}(P_n)=3$ for $n \geq 6$. This resolves a question about paths that has remained open since the introduction of proportional choosability.

items.title: Noise-induced enhancement of regime lifetimes -- A data-driven approach using deterministic trajectories
items.summary: We investigate the lifetime of dynamical regimes under the impact of noise motivated by low-dimensional models of the atmosphere. One may expect that the inclusion of noise tends to make the system leave prescribed regions of the state space faster. However, for relevant systems with complexities ranging from phenomenological toy models to reduced models of atmospheric dynamics, this intuition has proven misleading. As long as the noise is sufficiently small, the noisy system stays in regimes of interest on average longer than its deterministic counterpart, an effect we call ``stochastic inertia''. This phenomenon has been observed through extensive numerical simulations for different noise levels. We propose a numerical technique for testing the occurrence of stochastic inertia, constructing, for any fixed noise level, a Markov chain on the set of points given by a sufficiently long trajectory of the system without noise. The method is shown to correctly predict the presence of stochastic inertia in simple systems, and its utility is demonstrated on a paradigm model of atmospheric dynamics.

items.title: Formal contact-line regimes in the vanishing-slip limit of the thin-film equation
items.summary: We analyze the evolution of thin liquid droplets in the lubrication approximation with different slip conditions at the liquid-solid interface. Motivated by the classical no-slip paradox which states that the Navier-Stokes equations with a no-slip boundary condition require unphysical infinite dissipation during droplet spreading, we focus on the limit of vanishing slip. We show that in the no-slip limit three fundamentally different classes of limiting solutions are approached, each of them corresponding to a different scaling of the microscopic contact angle as the regularization parameter vanishes. These findings suggest that the thin-film equation with no slip supports a rich family of physically admissible solutions, provided one interprets the no-slip thin film equation as the asymptotic limit of models which regularized slip conditions. Even though the large apparent contact angles in some of these solutions seem incompatible with the lubrication approximation, a refined analysis shows that the underlying physical variables remain consistent with the assumptions for the lubrication approximation.

items.title: Simultaneous analysis of approximate leave-one-out cross-validation and mean-field inference II: General convex penalties
items.summary: For smooth penalties and group Lasso, Part I (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.02624) analyzed approximate leave-one-out (ALO) cross-validation by comparing its weights with the trace correction used in mean-field inference. For a $C^2$ penalty $R$, the matrix entering these corrections is $A=[\nabla^2R(\widehat b)+X^TDX]^{-1}$, where $\widehat b$ is the full-data estimator and $D$ is the diagonal matrix of fitted loss curvatures; for group Lasso, the penalty and loss curvatures are first restricted to the active support before taking the pseudoinverse. The obstacle to extending this argument to general convex penalties was the lack of an explicit formula for the matrix $A$ entering these corrections. For every finite-valued strongly convex penalty, we construct such a matrix from ordinary derivatives of the penalty response at the observed subgradient. Its projection--pseudoinverse formula separates the response space and penalty curvature, fixed by conditioning, from the explicit design dependence. This supplies the missing ingredient to extend the probabilistic argument of Part~I. The construction recovers the inverse Hessian for smooth penalties and the active-group inverse for group Lasso, including inactive boundary groups. In the proportional regime, for Gaussian designs with general positive-definite covariance and covariance-scaled strong convexity, we obtain unconditional bounds comparing both ALO and mean-field predictions with exact leave-one-out predictions in regression and single-index models. The expected average squared prediction error is $O(n^{-1})$, and the expected absolute criterion error is $O(n^{-1/2})$, under bounded, 1-Lipschitz loss scores and suitable test functions. The matrix and ALO weights use only observed data; the mean-field correction additionally uses the design covariance. The proofs are formalized in Lean~4.

items.title: A disproof of the El-Zahar--Erdős conjecture
items.summary: El-Zahar and Erdős asked whether every graph of bounded clique number and sufficiently large chromatic number contains two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs, each of large chromatic number, with no edge between them. We give a negative answer even for triangle-free graphs. For every integer $g \ge 4$, we show by a probabilistic argument that there exist graphs of girth at least $g$ and arbitrarily large chromatic number in which any two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs that each require at least seven colors are joined by an edge.

items.title: On the dynamics of composition operators: supercyclicity, odometers and translations
items.summary: We study the dynamical properties of composition operators acting on Banach spaces of measurable functions. In particular, we study in some detail the composition operators induced by odometers, which allows us to give a variety of new examples and counter-examples. We also get general statements about supercyclicity and frequent hypercyclicity of composition operators on $L\_p$-spaces.

items.title: Slope stability for normal varieties
items.summary: In this expository paper, we review the theory of slope stability of torsion-free sheaves with respect to nef curve classes and extend it to normal varieties.

items.title: Large deviation principles for component counts in the dense regime
items.summary: This paper develops large deviation principles for component counts in dense random geometric graphs. We consider a homogeneous Poisson point process on the flat \(d\)-dimensional torus and study the number of isolated components of fixed order \(k\) at connection radii above the connectivity scale. Two types of large deviation behaviour are investigated. First, we prove a Donsker--Varadhan large deviation principle in the regime where the expected number of such components tends to infinity. Second, we study the opposite extreme regime, where this expectation tends to zero, and establish fixed order tail measure limits for the associated \(k\)-component isolation-volume point process. As a consequence, we obtain functional large deviations for the moving threshold component count process.

items.title: Random Sequential Adsorption versus the Uniform Ensemble of Jammed Configurations: Stochastic Dominance on Graphs
items.summary: Random sequential adsorption with nearest-neighbor exclusion on a graph, also known as the discrete parking process, ends in a jammed configuration, that is, a maximal independent set of the graph. We compare the number of occupied sites in two models: the sequential model generated by this dynamics, and the static model, in which all jammed configurations are equiprobable. In a recent study of the one-dimensional case, it was stated that the sequential occupancy first-order stochastically dominates the static one on every path graph; the proof was subsequently withdrawn and the statement left as a conjecture. We prove this conjecture for all path graphs. The dominance extends to all cycle graphs, and exact computations confirm it for all 31 connected graphs with fewer than 6 vertices. It is not universal: we construct graphs with 6 or more vertices and maximum degree at least 4 on which the static model dominates the sequential one, and although the two models are comparable on all connected graphs with up to 7 vertices, stochastic comparability fails starting at 8 vertices. We also prove that dominance is inherited by disjoint unions whose components share the same dominance direction, and we exhibit mixed unions in which comparability is either preserved or lost. Finally, supported by exhaustive computations, we conjecture that the sequential model dominates the static one on every graph with maximum degree at most 3, a class that includes paths, cycles, and ladder graphs.

items.title: An Atiyah--Hirzebruch to Adams map and the hastened Adams spectral sequence for supercohomology
items.summary: We construct a map of filtered spectra inducing a map from the Atiyah--Hirzebruch spectral sequence (AHSS) to the Baker--Lazarev Adams spectral sequence of a $\mathit{ko}$-module $M$. Using this and a theorem of Bruner--Rognes, we construct a hastened Adams spectral sequence (HASS) for the Postnikov truncations of $\mathit{ko}$ and the connective Adams summand. Then, motivated by questions in quantum field theory, topological phases of matter, and tensor category theory, we apply the HASS to supercohomology, the cohomology theory $I_{\mathbb{C}^\times}(τ_{\le 2}\mathit{ko})$, and observe that in examples of interest it is easier to calculate with than either the AHSS or the usual Adams spectral sequence. We include a User's Guide to the HASS and several worked examples, as well as hastened Adams charts for many commonly encountered $\mathcal{A}(1)$-modules.

items.title: On a Secretary Problem with Two Equal-Sized Pools of Candidates
items.summary: This paper presents the solution of a secretary type problem where the decision maker observes a sequence of offers of two types. There are N objects of both types and these objects appear to the decision maker in random order. Objects can only be compared when they are of the same type. The objects of a given type that have already appeared can be ranked according to a complete order. Objects of different types are not comparable. On the appearance of an object, the decision maker must decide whether to accept that object (and thus stop searching) or irrevocably reject it (and thus continue searching). The goal of the decision maker is to accept an object that is the best of its type. The authors present the general form of the optimal policy and the asymptotical solution. The authors give a strong result describing whether an object of relative rank one should be accepted when the same number of objects of both types have been seen.

items.title: Pretty good state transfer in Grover walks on abelian Cayley graphs
items.summary: In this paper, we study pretty good state transfer (PGST) between vertex states in Grover walks on graphs. Using Chebyshev polynomials, we obtain a spectral and number-theoretic characterization for the occurrence of PGST on general graphs and on Cayley graphs over finite abelian groups. This approach yields complete classifications of hypercubes, the prisms $K_m\square K_2$, and unitary Cayley graphs. In particular, the hypercube $Q_d$ exhibits PGST if and only if $d$ is odd, $d\equiv2\pmod4$, or $d\equiv8\pmod{16}$, extending the known result for only prime $d$ (Chan and Zhan~\cite{pgst1}). We show that the independent-set blow-up $G[\overline K_2]$ exhibits PGST if discriminant eigenvalues of $G$ are reciprocals of nonzero integers. Using techniques from algebraic number theory, we obtain several infinite families of graphs exhibiting PGST, including examples with rationally dependent spectral angles not covered by earlier constructions based on linear independence over $\mathbb Q$.

items.title: Balanced Simplicial Complexes for the $γ$-Vectors of Zig-Zag Eulerian Polynomials
items.summary: In this paper, we construct a simplicial complex whose $f$-vector equals the $γ$-vector of the descent polynomial of an arbitrary canonically labeled rank-one poset. As an application, we prove Petersen and Zhuang's conjecture that the $γ$-vector of the normalized zig-zag Eulerian polynomial is the $f$-vector of a balanced simplicial complex.

items.title: On automorphisms of symplectic varieties acting trivially on the second cohomology group
items.summary: We prove that the group of automorphisms acting trivially on the torsion-free part of the integral second cohomology on a primitive symplectic variety is a locally trivial deformation invariant. We exhibit some examples of this invariant.

items.title: The Lyapunov and uniform spectra
items.summary: The \textit{Lyapunov spectrum} of a linear cocycle (or vector bundle) is the set of Lyapunov vectors with respect to all ergodic probability measures for the base topological dynamical system. This spectrum disregards trajectories that are atypical from the measure-theoretic viewpoint, and so it is in general insufficient to determine important properties of the cocycle, such as existence of dominated splittings. We resolve this deficiency by introducing a larger set which we call the \textit{uniform spectrum} of the cocycle. This definition is akin to Misiurewicz and Ziemian's rotation set. We prove several properties of the Lyapunov and uniform spectra, including relations between them. Motivated by a theorem of DeWitt and Gogolev, we consider Hölder-continuous cocycles over hyperbolic homeomorphisms and then provide bounds for the uniform spectrum in terms of the Lyapunov spectrum. We exhibit additional connections to the literature.

items.title: Foliations by constant spacetime mean curvature surfaces for asymptotically hyperboloidal initial data sets
items.summary: We construct an exhaustive family of constant spacetime mean curvature (STCMC) surfaces for initial data sets close to the anti-de Sitter-Schwarzschild hyperboloid. In particular, we obtain such a foliation as the long time limit of the volume preserving spacetime mean curvature flow starting from the constant mean curvature foliation constructed by Neves-Tian (Geom. Funct. Anal., 2009). As an application, inspired by the definition of STCMC center of mass for initial data sets proposed in the asymptotically Euclidean setting by Cederbaum-Sakovich (Calc. Var. PDE, 2021), we study the center of mass of an asymptotically hyperboloidal initial data set.

items.title: Low-dimensional optimal stopping with rank-dependent loss
items.summary: Sequential selection problems with independent observable scores and rank-dependent objectives are not reducible, in general, to dynamic optimisation over a state space of fixed dimension. We consider optimal stopping problems with truncated loss structures through the lens of the planar Poisson process, where self-similarity removes the time variable and the state is reduced to the $m$ lowest scores observed so far, rescaled to the initial time. For $m=1$ the optimal rule stops at the first record below a hyperbola, which is found by a sliding-window argument. For $m=2$ we derive the equations for the boundaries of the stopping sets of $1$-records and $2$-records, solve them explicitly on a part of the state space, and express the optimal values by quadratures. The value function and the optimal strategy are characterised by a static integro-differential equation. The optimal strategies are compared with simple low-parameter rules, which are close to optimality.

items.title: Flexibility for the Monge-Ampere system implies flexibility for isometric immersions into Riemannian manifolds
items.summary: We prove that any flexibility result for the Monge-Ampère system implies the corresponding flexibility result for the isometric immersion system, with the same Hölder regularity. We treat the general isometric immersion system, in which both the source and the ambient metrics are arbitrary Hölder regular, in arbitrary dimension and codimension. Combining this implication with existing results for the Monge-Ampère system, we obtain new ${C}^{1,α}$ flexibility statement for isometric immersions with arbitrary source and ambient metrics. To our knowledge, these are the first such results for non-Euclidean ambient metrics.

items.title: A weighted restriction estimate in $\mathbb R^2$
items.summary: We establish a weighted restriction estimate in $\mathbb{R}^2$. Our proof combines new two-ends Furstenberg estimates with refined decoupling.As an application, our result yields decay estimates for the circular $L^p$-means of the Fourier transforms of fractal measures in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

items.title: The computational complexity of Undirected Vertex Geography with maximum height 3
items.summary: The impartial game Undirected Vertex Geography is known to be polynomial time solvable. The variant in which vertices are assigned heights with maximum value m that reduce by 1 whenever the token is moved from that vertex, denoted UIRm, is known to be polynomial time solvable when m=2 and PSPACE-complete when m=4. We solve the open question of the computational complexity of UIR3 by a reduction from Directed vertex geography, and show that the complexity holds when the underlying graph is planar and (a) has degree at most 3, (b) is bipartite with maximum degree 4, or (c) is bipartite with maximum degree 5 and only has heights of 1 and 3.

items.title: Efficient orders for reciprocal matrices with block structure
items.summary: We consider block partitioned reciprocal matrices. For these matrices, we characterize the efficient vectors whose subvectors, corresponding to principal blocks, are positive multiples of given efficient vectors for those blocks. This generalizes a prior, scalar oriented, extension theorem. Conditions are presented that guarantee the existence of efficient vectors that preserve ordinal relations associated with cross-block comparisons. The notion of order transitivity is also generalized to block reciprocal matrices. For such matrices, it is then shown that efficient vectors, with no rank reversals in positions corresponding to off-diagonal blocks, exist. The notion of uniformly ordered reciprocal matrices (all efficent vectors exhibit the same order) is also generalized in the block reciprocal setting. This class is characterized via known matrix bounds for the consistent matrices associated with efficient vectors. We also provide a graph-theoretic characterization of the existence of a positive vector that is efficient for all completions of a given partial reciprocal matrix. Based on this, we apply some of our results on ordering to such matrices.

items.title: Torsion cycles on Fermat varieties
items.summary: A theorem of Manin and Drinfeld states that any divisor of degree $0$ on the cusps of a modular curve is torsion in the Jacobian. An elegant proof of this result was provided by Elkik using mixed Hodge theory. Rohrlich proved a generalization of this to Fermat curves. In this paper we reprove his results along the lines of the work of Elkik. We then use the same methods to generalize it to higher Chow cycles. We introduce a notion of `ambient decomposability' - essentially cycles coming from the ambient ${\mathbb P}^{n+1}$ and the base field - and show that higher Chow cycles determined by coordinate sections are necessarily of this type. This is a revised and accepted version of the earlier manuscript of the same name and is to appear in Indagationes Mathematicae. The results are stronger than the results in the earlier manuscript.

items.title: A simplicial model for manifold calculus through the configuration category
items.summary: Let $M$ be a closed $d$-dimensional smooth manifold and $X:Δ^{op}\rightarrow\operatorname{Fin}$ a finite simplicial set whose geometric realization is homeomorphic to $M$. Given the $\infty$-category $\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}_{/M}$ of disks embedded in $M$ and the path components functor $π_0:\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}_{/M}\rightarrow\operatorname{Fin}$, we construct a cofinal functor $Γ_X:Δ^{op}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}_{/M}$ such that $X=π_0\circΓ_X$. This result provides an alternative construction of a simplicial model developed by Boavida de Brito, Lambrechts, Pryor and Songhafouo Tsopméné to compute the space-valued presheaf $\operatorname{Emb}(-,M):\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}^{op}\rightarrow\mathcal{S}$. We also extend the result to manifolds with a $G$-structure and discuss applications to manifold calculus, factorization homology, and a possible generalization to manifolds with boundary.

items.title: Polar director structure of SmAP$_\text{F}$ phase of bent-core liquid crystals in thin planar cells with bias electric field
items.summary: We study the polar director structure in thin planar cells filled with bent-core liquid crystals in the ferroelectric smectic-A phase (SmAP$_\text{F}$). We analyze a continuum phenomenological model proposed in the physics literature and present proofs establishing the existence of weak solutions and conditional uniqueness of nonconstant solutions. We further investigate the qualitative properties of nontrivial solutions and examine the effects of a bias electric field, surface anchoring, and cell thickness on the polar director configuration. Our results are consistent with previous experimental and numerical simulations reported in the physics literature. In addition, our analysis reveals new parameter-dependent behaviors supported by our numerical simulations and extends results reported from previous literature.

items.title: Vector metrics with values in pre-Riesz spaces I: transfer of order convergence along vector lattice covers
items.summary: Vector metric spaces in the sense of Çevik and Altun take values in a vector lattice, but their axioms use only the order of the value space. We develop the theory for vector metrics with values in an Archimedean pre-Riesz space $E$, i.e.\ an ordered vector space admitting a bipositive order dense embedding $i$ into a vector lattice $Y$. We ask when an $E$-valued vector metric $d$ and the vector-lattice-valued metric $i\circ d$ have the same convergent and Cauchy nets and sequences. Relatively uniform convergence transfers along every cover. For nets, $\mathrm{o}_3$-convergence transfers if and only if the cover has an intrinsic domination property. This property holds for pervasive covers, by a result of Kalauch and van Gaans, for uniformly dense covers and in finite dimensions; it fails for an example of Kalauch and van Gaans. Sequential convergence transfers under a countable domination property implied by uniform density, but not under pervasiveness. For uncountable $Γ$, the vector lattice $\mathbb{R}\mathbf 1\oplus c_{00}(Γ)$ is pervasive in its Dedekind completion $\ell^\infty(Γ)$ without the transfer, while for countable $Γ$ the transfer holds; the difference is explained by order separability. In finite dimensions, with a closed generating cone, all these convergences coincide with norm convergence in every cover. For $C^1[0,1]$-valued integral metrics, positivity of the kernel on the diagonal forces all order convergences to coincide with $L^1$-convergence. For the Volterra kernel $(t-s)_+$, by contrast, $L^1$-convergence, relatively uniform convergence and order convergence are pairwise different, and we describe each explicitly.

items.title: Singularities of ideals with minimal tangent space dimension in the Hilbert scheme of points on a threefold
items.summary: We classify all singular monomial ideals in the Hilbert scheme of $d$ points on $\mathbb{A}^3$ whose tangent spaces have the minimal dimension $3d+6$. There are two families called the opera houses and rotating staircases, and we give their combinatorial and algebraic descriptions. All the opera houses are in one linkage class, and their singularities are smoothly equivalent to the vertex of a cone over the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(2,6) \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^{14}$ in its Plücker embedding. The rotating staircases split into many linkage classes and we give some examples.

items.title: Combinatorial Bloch-Gieseker inequalities on toric surfaces
items.summary: We give a combinatorial proof of the Bloch-Gieseker inequalities in the special case of ample toric vector bundles on toric surfaces via a new rearrangement inequality for planar curves. Using this we establish the Hodge package for combinatorial analogues of cohomology rings of ample projective bundles over toric surfaces which don't appear to arise from matroidal constructions.

items.title: An $\infty$-category approach to $A_\infty$-algebras and $A_\infty$-categories
items.summary: $A_\infty$-algebras over a commutative ring $R$ are generalizations of $R$-algebras in which multiplication is only associative up to higher homotopies. Similarly, $A_\infty$-categories over $R$ are generalizations of $R$-linear categories in which composition of morphisms is only associative up to higher homotopies. They are important in the definition of Fukaya categories in Symplectic Geometry, and in other areas of mathematics. By $\infty$-categories we mean quasicategories, a class of simplicial sets which are a model for $(\infty,1)$-categories, used in the work of Jacob Lurie. We define and study $\infty$-categories of $A_\infty$-algebras and $A_\infty$-categories. Our approach is unusual in that rather than defining them by localization, we construct our $\infty$-categories completely explicitly as simplicial sets. Our $\infty$-categories are intended for applications to Fukaya categories in Symplectic Geometry. Given a suitable symplectic manifold $(X,ω)$, one should construct its Fukaya category ${\mathscr F}(X,ω)$, a (filtered) $A_\infty$-category, and its derived Fukaya category $D^b{\mathscr F}(X,ω)$, a triangulated category (or better, a stable $\infty$-category). Typically ${\mathscr F}(X,ω)$ depends on many arbitrary choices. Our $\infty$-categories give a clean way to explain in what sense ${\mathscr F}(X,ω)$ and $D^b{\mathscr F}(X,ω)$ are independent of these choices.

items.title: All Serrin bands are unduloidal
items.summary: A Serrin domain is a smooth domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ where Serrin's overdetermined problem for $Δu+2=0$ admits a positive solution $u$. In the plane, Fall-Minlend-Weth and Dávila-del Pino-Musso-Wheeler constructed periodic Serrin bands close to a flat strip and a singular chain of tangent disks, respectively. More recently, Cerezo-Fernández-Mira constructed a real-analytic $1$-parameter family of unduloidal Serrin bands interpolating between these two limiting geometries. In this work, we prove that every Serrin band in $\mathbb{R}^2$ belongs to this canonical unduloidal family.

items.title: Moment approximations in optimal transport: geometric estimates and a semiclassical limit
items.summary: We study finite moment approximations of linear optimization problems over measures. Under suitable assumptions, we establish the existence of discrete minimizers with a controlled number of support points, duality and $Γ$-convergence as the moment approximation is refined. This framework accommodates several transport problems, in which marginal constraints are replaced by finitely many moment constraints. For moment functions localized at scale $r_n$, we prove an estimate controlling $W_\infty$ by $W_p$ up to an additive error of order $r_n$, which also applies to discrete measures. For repulsive costs, we show that minimizers remain separated from the diagonal, uniformly in the number of moments, and we derive consequences for dual potentials. Finally, under a moment-correction assumption, we prove that the fermionic minimum energies converge in the semiclassical limit to the moment-constrained Coulomb transport value for a fixed family of moment functions.

items.title: Regularity and stabilization of integral closures of powers of homogeneous ideals
items.summary: In this paper, we establish explicit polynomial bounds for the regularity defect and the stabilization index of integral closures of powers of arbitrary homogeneous ideals over fields of any characteristic. Specifically, let $I \subseteq K[x_{1}, \dots, x_{n}]$ be a nonzero proper homogeneous ideal generated in degrees at most $d$. We prove that $\reg \overline{I^{s}} \le ρ(I)s + d^{(n-1)2^{n}}$ for every $s \ge 1$, where $ρ(I) \le d$ denotes the eventual slope of $\reg \overline{I^{s}}$. Furthermore, the stabilization bound is polynomial in $d$ for a fixed number of variables $n$. In characteristic zero, an upper bound for the first Hilbert coefficient yields a significantly sharper exponent. Our approach relies on exact equigenerated reductions, free lattice constructions within normalized Rees algebras, monic Frobenius presentations, and Tor-module regularity controls, complemented by generic source hyperplanes that reduce the stabilization behavior to the eventual nonvanishing of graded components.

items.title: Endpoint behaviour of vertical and horizontal Riesz transforms for the flow Laplacian on homogeneous trees
items.summary: We study endpoint estimates of Riesz transforms on a homogeneous tree equipped with its canonical flow measure $μ$. We prove that the known boundedness from $H^1_{\mathrm{at}}(μ)$ to $L^1(μ)$ of the vertical Riesz transform can not be strengthened to boundedness on $H^1_{\mathrm{at}}(μ)$ itself. We also prove that the adjoint vertical Riesz transform is not of weak type $(1,1)$. For the scalar horizontal transforms defined by nonzero bounded coefficients with zero sum on each child set, we establish $H^1_{\mathrm{at}}(μ)\to L^1(μ)$ boundedness and show that failure to preserve cancellation on atoms prevents boundedness on $H^1_{\mathrm{at}}(μ)$. We then introduce a horizontal derivative based on deviations from sibling averages. Its associated Riesz transform retains the $L^p(μ)$ bounds for $1<p<\infty$ and the weak type $(1,1)$ estimate, and is bounded on $H^1_{\mathrm{at}}(μ)$ itself. These mapping properties parallel those of horizontal Riesz transforms in the continuous setting, supporting our construction as a natural discrete analogue. These results distinguish vertical and horizontal behaviour at the endpoint and identify cancellation on sibling sets as a mechanism for Hardy-space boundedness.

items.title: A stratified version of geometric realizations
items.summary: Given a simplicial set $X$, let $\operatorname{B}({X})$ denote its poset of nondegenerate simplices. We define a natural stratification $\left\vert{X}\right\vert\rightarrow\operatorname{B}({X})$. When $X$ is locally finite, we prove that this stratification is conical. Moreover, if $X$ is finite, we prove that the exit path category $\operatorname{Exit}^{\operatorname{B}({X})}(\left\vert{X}\right\vert)$ satisfies the geometric realization formula $\mathop{\operatorname{colim}}\limits_{σ:Δ[p]\rightarrow X} \operatorname{Exit}^{\operatorname{B}({p})}(Δ^p)\simeq\operatorname{Exit}^{\operatorname{B}({X})}(\left\vert{X}\right\vert)$ where the colimit is indexed by the category of simplices of $X$.

items.title: Unbounded traces, Connes' index theorem for measured foliations, and the Godbillon-Vey invariant in KK-theory
items.summary: We prove that unbounded positive traces define KK-elements with real coefficients. Such traces naturally arise from invariant transverse measures on foliations (Connes, 1979) and, more generally, on Lie groupoids (Crainic--Mestre, 2019). As an application, we build a canonical KK-element with real coefficients whose associated map of K-groups is the Godbillon-Vey invariant as constructed by Connes. In the process, we show how Connes' index theorem for measured foliations can be deduced from the Connes-Skandalis longitudinal index theorem, using cyclic cohomology.

items.title: Relationship between quandle shadow cocycle invariants and Vassiliev invariants
items.summary: As one of the problems in his list [20], T. Ohtsuki proposed to study relations between quandle cocycle invariants and quantum invariants. The aim of this paper is to answer one of those questions. We prove that the coefficient of the finite perturbative expansion of the quandle shadow cocycle invariant defined by $(\Z /p\Z)$-Laurent polynomial quandle is Vassiliev invariant for any braids.

items.title: Completions of vector metric spaces and the diagonal property of order convergence
items.summary: A vector metric space carries a distance with values in an ordered vector space $E$; a sequence converges if its distances to the limit are dominated by a sequence decreasing to zero in $E$. We show that, for Archimedean $E$, every $E$-valued vector metric space has a completion if and only if order Cauchy sequences in $E$ converge and $E$ has the diagonal property of order convergence (SDP): for every double sequence $(a^k_n)$ with $a^k_n\downarrow_n0$ there are indices $n_k$ and $e_k\downarrow 0$ with $a^k_{n_k}\le e_k$. In vector lattices this is the classical diagonal property of Kantorovich, equivalently the strong Egoroff property. We show that its standard characterisations remain valid in Archimedean ordered vector spaces, and that it holds if and only if convergence in every $E$-valued vector metric space satisfies the iterated limit axiom. For an ordered Banach space with a closed normal cone, all completions exist if and only if the norm is $σ$-order continuous; if the cone has an interior point, all vector metrics are then scalar. By a theorem of Veksler and of Hager and van Mill, for compact Hausdorff $K$ either $K$ is an almost $P$-space and $C(K)$-valued vector metrics are scalar, or there are countable $C(K)$-valued vector metric spaces without completion. A product of ordered vector spaces with (SDP) and nonzero cones has (SDP) if and only if there are fewer than $\mathfrak b$ factors, extending a result of Hager and van Mill for $\mathbb{R}^A$. We also prove permanence results for direct summands and uniformly dense vector lattice covers of pre-Riesz spaces.

items.title: A variational approach to an anisotropic nonlocal porous medium equation with drift
items.summary: We study nonlocal porous-medium equations driven by anisotropic Riesz-type repulsive interactions and an external confining potential. The pressure is determined by convolution with an interaction potential of the form $$ W(x)=|x|^{-s}Ω\left(\frac{x}{|x|}\right), \qquad d-2<s<d, $$ where $Ω$ is a smooth, even, and strictly positive angular profile. For quadratic confinement and $s\in(d-2,d)\cap(0,5]$, under suitable positivity assumptions on the anisotropic kernels, we prove that the unique energy minimizer is the only steady state among bounded continuous probability densities. We then establish the long-time convergence of global weak solutions to this equilibrium, both locally and globally in Hölder norms. To obtain these results, we derive uniform $L^p$, $L^\infty$, and Hölder estimates, adapting the regularity theory for fractional porous-medium equations to the anisotropic setting. We also construct global weak solutions through a minimizing-movement scheme in Wasserstein space, establish the corresponding energy-dissipation inequality, and prove a Talagrand-type transport inequality.

items.title: Dual Gauss-Thakur sums for Drinfeld modules
items.summary: We define dual Gauss-Thakur sums for Drinfeld modules, building on constructions of Gauss-Thakur sums due to Thakur, in the case of the Carlitz module, and Gazda and Maurischat, for general Anderson $t$-modules. Using results of Ferraro, we demonstrate that these sums can be obtained by evaluations of dual special functions at elements of finite fields. Our main results are matrix identities assembled from Gauss-Thakur sums and dual Gauss-Thakur sums in terms of multiplication coefficients for the Drinfeld module and its adjoint. We further prove determinant identities and explore connections with special Goss $L$-values and Drinfeld modular forms.

items.title: Real Frøyshov invariants and lattice homology
items.summary: For a class of almost rational plumbing 4-manifolds equipped with smooth involutions, we give a description of the Real Frøyshov invariants of their boundaries in terms of lattice homology. Our approach uses the $S^1$-stable equivalence between Seiberg-Witten Floer spectra and lattice spectra constructed by Dai-Sasahira-Stoffregen, and the $\operatorname{O}(2)$-equivariant versions of these spectra developed by Kang-Park-Taniguchi. As applications, we derive a formula for these invariants for every $\operatorname{spin}^c$ structure on the double branched covers of even torus knots $T_{2p,q}$, and determine the smooth nonorientable $4$-genus of an infinite family of torus knots $T_{4,q}$.

items.title: Multiplicity of positive solutions for degenerate nonlocal $p$-Laplacian problems without monotonicity of the normalized reaction
items.summary: We study degenerate nonlocal Dirichlet problems driven by the $p$-Laplacian, with diffusion depending on weighted sums of integral powers of the solution. Under explicit sign, spectral and size conditions, we obtain two positive solutions for each bounded positivity interval of the diffusion coefficient with zero endpoint values. Neither monotonicity of the normalized reaction $f(x,t)/t^{p-1}$ nor uniqueness of the frozen problem is required. The proof combines Schauder's theorem on a product space of a scalar parameter and a function with subsolution bounds and an energy estimate. The multiplicity result also persists under uniformly small continuous perturbations of the nonlocal functional, including perturbations that do not preserve order.

items.title: On Tiling and Spectral Sets in $\mathbb Z_{p^2}\times\mathbb Z_{p^2}$
items.summary: Let $p$ be a prime number, it is shown that tiling sets are spectral in $\mathbb Z_{p^2}\times\mathbb Z_{p^2}$ and spectral sets of sizes $p^k (k=0,1,2,3,4)$ are tiling in $\mathbb Z_{p^2}\times\mathbb Z_{p^2}$. The main arguments are based on analysis of the zero set of the Fourier transform as well as the tree structure of subgroups in $\mathbb Z_{p^2}\times\mathbb Z_{p^2}$. Some auxiliary results concerning tiling sets and spectral sets of sizes $p$ and $p^{2m-1}$ in $\mathbb Z_{p^m}\times \mathbb Z_{p^m}$ ($m\in\mathbb N$) are also presented.

items.title: Uniformly positive entropy and mixing in minimal systems
items.summary: Every minimal system with uniformly positive entropy of order two is topologically mixing. In a minimal system, mixing along an infinite set $A\subset\N_0$ is equivalent to $\dist(T^nU,T^nV)\to0$ along $A$ for all nonempty open $U,V$, and to unbounded complexity of each standard binary open cover along every infinite subset of $A$. For $A=\N_0$ it is also equivalent to $Δ^*$-transitivity. A local distance condition characterizes finite cyclic decompositions with mixing return maps. Such a decomposition exists precisely when, for each infinite $S\subset\N_0$, the closure of some proximal cell along $S$ has positive measure for some invariant probability. In a minimal weakly mixing system, for fixed infinite $S$, these cells are either all dense or all have closures of measure zero for every invariant probability. We also give proximal-cell criteria for Furstenberg families and mild mixing.

items.title: Base-extension Semantics for Intuitionistic Predicate Logic
items.summary: Sandqvist's base-extension semantics explains the logical constants of intuitionistic propositional logic by inference in bases: collections of rules over atomic sentences that record the inferential content of a state of affairs. We extend it to intuitionistic predicate logic, first- and second-order, reading the quantifiers substitutionally, and prove natural deduction sound and complete. Two ideas carry the extension. First, a rule of a base may require a premiss to be established for a fresh name, one about which neither the assumptions nor the base say anything. With such rules, Sandqvist's completeness proof extends to first-order logic, whether validity is taken over all bases or over finite ones. Second, the second-order quantifier ranges over the atomic predicates, and validity is support in comprehensive bases, where every expressible condition has a definitional proxy. This yields intuitionistic Henkin second-order logic with full comprehension, not full second-order semantics.

items.title: On integral and $p$-adic Bost-Connes systems
items.summary: Using Borger and de Smit's theory of periodic Witt vectors, we construct integral models of Bost-Connes systems for general number fields, generalizing Connes, Consani and Marcolli's construction over $\mathbb Q$. As an application, for totally real number fields other than $\mathbb Q$, we construct $p$-adic Bost-Connes systems whose $p$-adic KMS states are described in terms of Deligne-Ribet's theory of $p$-adic $L$-functions, extending the work of Connes and Consani for $\mathbb Q$.

items.title: Half-Line Hardy-Szegő Point Processes: Fisher-Hartwig Asymptotics and Sparse Conditioning
items.summary: A horizontal window extending from a fixed positive height to infinity has infinite area but a finite expected number of Hardy-Szegő zeros. We study its zero count as the horizontal length $L$ grows. Unlike for fixed bounded-height windows, the logarithmic moment generating function has a new $θ^2\log L/(2π^2)$ term; we also identify its holomorphic order-one correction. The logarithmic term has two equal contributions: a Fisher-Hartwig jump in a canonical Wiener-Hopf model and an endpoint effect in the original Fourier-Laplace operator. This yields precise point and tail probabilities at positive count densities. We also determine the transition when a moving upper height is comparable to $L$. For sparse exact counts $n_L\to\infty$ with $n_L=o(L)$, we obtain logarithmic probability asymptotics relative to the exact void probability. We determine the void exponent and sharp asymptotics relative to the void probability for counts up to order $\log L$. Under sparse exact-count conditioning, the empirical distribution of rescaled horizontal positions and logarithmic heights converges to the uniform law on the unit square. Near distinct interior horizontal locations, the rescaled configurations converge to independent Poisson processes with uniform logarithmic-height marks.

items.title: Infinite-dimensional invariant tori for the perturbed modified KdV equation
items.summary: In this paper, we consider the perturbed modified KdV equation $u_t=-u_{xxx}+6u^2u_x+\partial_x(u^5)$ on the circle, without external parameters. We prove that it admits plenty of almost periodic solutions.

items.title: When Does Reallocating a Sampling Budget Pay? Instance-wise Allocation for Neural Routing Solvers
items.summary: Neural routing solvers sample many solutions per instance and keep the best, with the same number of samples for every instance. We measure how much a non-uniform split of the same total budget is worth and which property of a workload decides it. Best-of-k curves estimated by averaging random orderings of stored samples overstate the gain, and deciding on one half of the samples while evaluating on the other understates it; we use exact best-of-k curves, a U-statistic over all orderings. For three pretrained solvers (POMO, the Attention Model and Sym-NCO) on the traveling salesman problem, reallocation reduces the total optimality gap by at most 2.5% on the training distribution, so uniform allocation is close to optimal there. On workloads that mix in out-of-distribution instances it reduces the gap by 11.8-13.3% (1.1-1.8% of tour length) for the two solvers that degrade under the shift, and almost nothing for the one that does not. Across two heterogeneity mechanisms, three solvers, two confirmation collections and budgets of 25 to 200 samples per instance, the gain is predicted by the spread of difficulty within a workload, not its average. Allocating on a power-law curve fitted to twenty charged probe samples per instance recovers 88-93% of the uncharged optimum; successive halving does worse. A 2-opt local search, however, removes most of the gap at negligible cost, after which reallocation adds a few hundredths of a percent of tour length.

items.title: Supersingular Ekedahl-Oort strata and Oort's conjecture
items.summary: Let $\mathcal{A}_g$ be the moduli space over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ of $g$-dimensional principally polarised abelian varieties, where $p$ is a prime. We show that if $g$ is even and $p\geq 5$, then every geometric generic member in the maximal supersingular Ekedahl-Oort stratum in $\mathcal{A}_g$ has automorphism group $\{ \pm 1\}$. This confirms Oort's conjecture in the case of $p\geq 5$ and even $g$. We also separately prove Oort's conjecture for $g=4$ and $p >2$.

items.title: Broximal Gradient Descent in General Norms: Convergence without Fejér Monotonicity
items.summary: We study Broximal Gradient Descent in a general norm for smooth optimization over a closed convex set. Each update minimizes the linear model over the intersection of the feasible set and a norm ball. Unlike the Euclidean case with suitably restricted radii, the distance to a solution can increase, even when the squared norm is strongly convex. We instead use a comparator inequality and an observable stationarity certificate. For convex objectives, prescribed radii yield value convergence, including escape when the infimum is unattained, and a last-iterate $O(K^{-1/3})$ bound without a distance-bound assumption. A level-set distance bound gives an all-iteration $O(1/K)$ rate with calibrated radii and an asymptotic $O(\log K/K)$ rate with radii using no problem constant. Strong convexity and power growth give explicit faster envelopes and convergence of the iterates.
