Without convexity, a constrained Polyak--Łojasiewicz inequality gives linear convergence with prescribed radii. An observable radius-halving rule needs a valid smoothness constant but neither the PL modulus nor an initial gap bound; warm starting gives logarithmic total oracle complexity in inverse accuracy. The analysis separates established local-oracle ingredients from the control of level sets, radius calibration, and accuracy-based oracle counts.

items.title: Structure-Preserving PHS RBF-FD Methods for Schrodinger Equations
items.summary: We develop and analyze a structure-preserving polyharmonic-spline radial-basis-function finite-difference (PHS RBF-FD) method for the two-dimensional Schrödinger equation with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. The method combines a 29-point complete-shell stencil with odd boundary reflection to construct a symmetric discrete Laplacian. Unlike conventional nearest-neighbor RBF-FD discretizations, whose independently selected stencils do not generally preserve global symmetry, the proposed construction admits an exact discrete sine eigenbasis. We derive a Fourier-symbol representation and establish a sufficient criterion for strict negative definiteness, verified for the \(r^7+\mathbb P_4\) and \(r^{11}+\mathbb P_5\) formulations using validated coefficient calculations. The resulting symmetric spatial operator preserves discrete mass and energy under exact semidiscrete evolution, while fully discrete conservation depends on the time integrator. Numerical experiments examine kernel selection, dispersion, convergence, symmetry defects, and computational cost. Comparisons with conventional RBF-FD and fourth-order finite differences include exact Fourier modes and a variable-potential Schrödinger problem with an independently refined spectral reference. The \(r^{11}+\mathbb P_5\) formulation provides favorable accuracy in the tested problems while maintaining the desired spatial structure. The analysis establishes a connection between boundary treatment, global operator symmetry, and structure preservation in localized PHS discretizations.

items.title: From Consensus-Based Optimization to Evolution Strategies: Proof of Global Convergence
items.summary: Consensus-based optimization (CBO) is a powerful and versatile zero-order multi-particle method designed to provably solve high-dimensional global optimization problems, including those that are genuinely nonconvex or nonsmooth. The method relies on a balance between stochastic exploration and contraction toward a consensus point, which is defined via the Laplace principle as a proxy for the global minimizer. In this paper, we introduce new CBO variants that address practical and theoretical limitations of the original formulation of this novel optimization methodology. First, we propose a model called $δ$-CBO}, which incorporates nonvanishing diffusion to prevent premature collapse to suboptimal states. We also develop a numerically stable implementation, the Consensus Freezing scheme, that remains robust even for arbitrarily large time steps by freezing the consensus point over time intervals. We connect these models through appropriate asymptotic limits. Furthermore, we derive from the Consensus Freezing scheme by suitable time rescaling and asymptotics a further algorithm, the Consensus Hopping scheme, which can be interpreted as a form of $(1,λ)$-Evolution Strategy. For all these schemes, we characterize for the first time the invariant measures and establish global convergence results, including exponential convergence rates.

items.title: Exact Algorithms for Computing Generalized Eigenspaces of Matrices via Jordan-Krylov Basis
items.summary: An effective exact method is proposed for computing generalized eigenspaces of a matrix of integers or rational numbers. The key of our approach is the concept of the Jordan-Krylov basis. A new method, called Jordan-Krylov elimination, is introduced to design an algorithm for computing the Jordan-Krylov basis. The resulting algorithm outputs generalized eigenspaces as a form of Jordan chains. Notably, in the output, components of generalized eigenvectors are expressed as polynomials in the associated eigenvalue as a variable

items.title: Capacity-Aware Redistribution Control for Mitigation of Cascading Failures in Networks
items.summary: This paper studies the control of irreversible cascading failures in networks with finite node capacities. Each node carries a nonnegative divisible quantity, referred to as load, and fails irreversibly when its load exceeds its capacity. The network dynamics are represented by topology-dependent row-stochastic matrices. When nodes fail, these matrices must be updated. However, directly deleting rows and columns corresponding to failed nodes can reduce the total load in the network. We therefore introduce a topology update that preserves unit row sums and quantifies any unserved load explicitly. We derive the resulting load-balance relation and a necessary and sufficient condition for lossless redistribution after simultaneous failures. Based on these results, we formulate a two-stage optimization problem: the first stage minimizes unserved load, and the second stage minimizes the highest capacity utilization among the surviving nodes. Simulations on grid and Barabasi-Albert networks show that, unlike the standard equal and residual-capacity redistribution approaches, the proposed method prevents secondary failures in all tested cases, with a tradeoff against served load on scale-free networks.

items.title: Tiling of Hyperbolic Surface by Maximal Number of Tiles
items.summary: Tilings of a closed hyperbolic surface by congruent $n$-gons with $n\ge 7$ is a finite problem. One extreme of the finite problem is that the number of tiles is maximal. The problem is related to edge-to-edge tilings of the Poincaré disk ${\bb H}^2$ by congruent $n$-gons, such that all vertices have degree 3 and the vertex sets satisfy certain balance condition. For the special case $n=7$, we show that the heptagon in any such tiling belongs to one of the four families, and tilings of ${\bb H}^2$ by generic heptagons in each family is unique. As a consequence, for any closed hyperbolic surface of Euler characteristic $χ$, we may classify all tilings of the surface by maximal number $-6χ$ of congruent generic heptagons in the four families.

items.title: Small Prime Primitive Roots in Arithmetic Progressions
items.summary: Let $p>1$ be a large prime number, let $q=O(\log\log p)$ and let $1\leq a<q$ be a pair of relatively prime integers. It is proved that there is a prime primitive root $u\ll (\log p)(\log \log p)^5$ such that $u\equiv a\bmod q$ in the prime finite field $\mathbb{F}_p$.

items.title: Rates of convergence for extremal spacings in Kakutani's random interval-splitting process
items.summary: Kakutani's random interval-splitting process iteratively divides, via a uniformly random splitting point, the largest sub-interval in a partition of the unit interval. The length of the longest sub-interval after $n$ steps, suitably centred and scaled, is known to satisfy a central limit theorem as $n \to \infty$. We provide a quantitative (Berry-Esseen) upper bound for the finite-$n$ approximation in the central limit theorem, with conjecturally optimal rates in $n$. We also prove convergence to an exponential distribution for the length of the smallest sub-interval, with quantitative bounds. The Kakutani process can be embedded in certain branching and fragmentation processes, and we translate our results into that context also. Our proof uses conditioning on an intermediate time, a conditional independence structure for statistics involving small sub-intervals, an Hermite-Edgeworth expansion, and moments estimates with quantitative error bounds.

items.title: Towards sparse optimization over convex loops: Equivalence of Square Root Velocity distance and Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao
items.summary: The Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) distance on $S^{2}$ has recently been shown to coincide with a classical elastic distance between $S^{2}$-immersions in the theory of Riemannian shape analysis. While this correspondence holds in dimension $2$, the analogous statement fails in general on $S^{1}$ and, in the case of convex curves, it cannot be derived from existing two-dimensional arguments. In this paper, we establish that for convex absolutely continuous immersions of $S^{1}$ in the plane, the shape distance induced by the square root velocity transformation (SRVT) is indeed equivalent to the WFR distance acting on their associated length measures. The proof exploits a monotonicity principle for optimal transport on the universal cover of the circle, which in turn guarantees the existence of an optimal reparametrization achieving the SRVT infimum and enables a one-dimensional unbalanced optimal transport reformulation. Motivated by this equivalence, we further investigate the role of sparsity in shape optimization problems formulated in terms of length measures and regularized by the WFR distance. We study linear optimization over the corresponding balls, for which we prove a finiteness result when the reference measure is discrete, and propose a convex, positively one-homogeneous regularizer suitable for conditional gradient algorithms.

items.title: Gravitational Illumination Bodies
items.summary: For a given convex body $K$ in $\mathbb R ^n$ and $δ>0$, we introduce a new class of bodies, the {\em gravitational illumination bodies} $I^δ(K)$. We show some of their properties and explore their relation to floating bodies, illumination bodies and Ulam floating bodies. Unexpected phenomena happen and the gravitational illumination bodies exhibit very different behavior than the floating bodies, illumination bodies and Ulam floating bodies. While the classical bodies are all convex and either contained in $K$ or containing $K$, this is no longer the case for the new bodies. They need not be convex, but they are star shaped and it may happen that $I^δ(K)$ has non-empty intersection with both, $K$ and its complement. Moreover, the containment behavior may change with the dimension. Most surprising is the behavior of a volume derivative, $$ \lim_{δ\to 0} \frac{ |\vol_n(K)-\vol_n(I^δ(K)) |}{δ^\frac{2}{n+1}}. $$ In all dimensions the corresponding volume derivative for the classical bodies results in the equi-affine invariant affine surface area of the body $K$. In the case of the gravitational illumination body, this is also the case in all dimensions, except in dimension $3$. In dimension $3$ the limit is equal to $0$ for all convex bodies. A non-zero derivative is obtained in dimension $3$ if one normalizes by $δ$ instead of $δ^\frac{1}{2}$. The non-zero limit is a new affine invariant involving the {\em affine mean curvature } and the {\em Pick invariant} of the convex body.

items.title: Sharp potential and Brenier map $W_2$-stability for log-concave sources
items.summary: We study quantitative stability of Brenier potentials and maps under changes of the target measure. Let $κ>0$, for a $κ$-strongly log-concave source $ρ$, possibly with a non-smooth potential, the normalized transport potentials satisfy \[ \left\Vert u_μ-u_ν\right\Vert _{L^{2}(ρ)}\leqslant\left( 1/κ\right) ^{1/2}W_{2}\left( μ,ν\right) \] for arbitrary targets with finite second moments. This readily yields a Poincaré inequality for $κ$-strongly log-concave sources. The coefficient $(1/κ)^{1/2}$ is shown to be optimal. The proof relies on a probabilistic interpretation of cell energies and the subsequent variance decomposition. Interpolation from potential to map then yields the map stability for targets in a common compact set, \[ \left\Vert T_μ-T_ν\right\Vert _{L^{2}(ρ)}\leqslant \operatorname{Const} \cdot W_{2}\left( μ,ν\right) ^{1/3}. \] Sharpness of the order for both the potential and map stability are established. This clarifies a long- standing limitation in topological embedding: representing distributions by their Brenier maps preserves convergence, but it need not preserve local distances.

items.title: On the Principle of Localization on Quasi-Orbits in Crossed Products
items.summary: Quasi-regular $C^*$-dynamical systems with locally closed quasi-orbits are considered. For the corresponding crossed products, a localization principle on quasi-orbits is proven. This principle reduces the study of the primitive spectrum of the original crossed product to the study of the primitive spectra of crossed products, each corresponding to its own $C^*$-dynamical system with a single quasi-orbit. Assuming that the group action on the primitive spectrum of the $C^*$-algebra in the crossed product is free, except for some fixed subset, a characterization of the spectrum of the crossed product is provided, which allows for a description of the Jacobson topology on it.

items.title: Dessins d'Enfants as a Topological Lens on Temporal Hypergraphs
items.summary: Hypergraphs are the natural language for group interactions, and topological data analysis has given us several ways to look at them: simplicial and cell complexes, persistent homology, and sheaves. All of these treat a hyperedge as an unordered set. In this paper, we introduce a different and, to our knowledge, new viewpoint that comes from Grothendieck's theory of dessins d'enfants and, unlike these approaches, takes into account the order in which vertices appear in each hyperedge and hyperedges appear around each vertex. A dessin is a bipartite graph drawn on a closed orientable surface. Through Walsh's classical correspondence between hypermaps and bipartite maps, every hypergraph equipped with a cyclic order of incidences at each vertex and inside each hyperedge is a dessin, and therefore determines a surface with faces and a genus. We develop this idea for temporal hypergraphs and build the surface by replaying history: incidences are added in the order in which they occurred, and each new incidence is inserted into the cyclic orders built so far, next to the earlier incidence to which it is related. We prove that every insertion either grows the hypergraph without creating a cycle, closes a cycle locally by splitting a face, or closes it globally by adding a handle; the number of independent cycles equals the number of local plus handle events, and the genus equals the number of handle events. These counts give interpretable, size-controlled measures of how a temporal hypergraph's cycles organize on a surface as it grows. We apply our method to five Stack Exchange communities and show that it separates communities that standard statistics cannot tell apart and quantifies how much the real order of interactions matters. We further discuss what the surface viewpoint adds to existing higher-order network analysis and how it opens a path toward dessin-based learning on hypergraphs.

items.title: Recent developments in stochastic systems with singular dynamics -- a brief survey --
items.summary: Diffusions with singular drifts appear naturally in the study of certain classes of interesting particle systems. Due to the singularities involved in the equations describing them, studying their dynamics is both interesting and challenging as they fall outside of the usual regularity assumptions on the vector fields in the literature. One needs to introduce and study them with different methods, with the use of symmetric polynomials being a particularly promising approach. In this expository work, we give an overview of some models and methods, and we further explore their interactions with the areas of Multiple Loewner chains (in particular, multiple Schramm-Loewner Evolutions), the new links with Random Matrices, and the novel area of Machine Learning for Singular Dynamics.

items.title: Combinatorial Properties of The Giant Under Supercritical Percolation
items.summary: We study combinatorial properties, such as diameter and long paths and cycles, of the giant component of percolated graphs. Such combinatorial properties are well studied for classical graphs such as pseudo-random graphs and the hypercube. We aim to obtain similar results for extensive families of $d$-regular $n$-vertex graphs. Specifically, assuming expansion properties of the host graph, we show a typical vertex expansion by a factor of $1/d\log d$ in the giant component of the percolated subgraph. As a consequence, we obtain bounds on various combinatorial properties of the giant component. For example, a bound of $O\left(d\log^2 d+\log n\right)$ on the typical diameter of the giant component of the percolated subgraph. In addition, we construct graphs with very good vertex and edge expansion, but having large diameter, showing that the diameter of the percolated subgraph is not necessarily typically logarithmic in the number of the vertices of the graph. We also present good expanders such that their percolated subgraph typically contains a bad expanding set.

items.title: Polynomial $\mathcal{Z}$-contraction: A unified approach with Application
items.summary: In this paper, we introduce polynomial $\mathcal{Z}$-contraction by unifying the ideas of polynomial contraction and $\mathcal{Z}$-contraction and also provide demonstrative examples to show the effectiveness and novelty. Chiefly, we prove two fixed point results for polynomial $\mathcal{Z}$-contraction employing simulation functions. Lastly, we utilize our main result to discuss the existence and uniqueness of solution for boundary value problem with a concrete example in $L^p(0,π)$ under suitable assumptions.

items.title: Diffusion Models are Provably Efficient Priors for Sparse Recovery
items.summary: Diffusion models have transformed generative modeling through their ability to capture and generate samples from complex data distributions. This success has spurred substantial interest in using pretrained diffusion models as expressive priors for highly ill-posed inverse problems in imaging and sensing. Despite strong empirical performance, theoretical understanding of this approach remains limited: existing guarantees are often asymptotic or entail prohibitive computational costs in the worst case. In this paper, we address this gap by studying sparse recovery from a small number of linear measurements, a classical problem in compressed sensing. We show that, given an accurate diffusion model capturing a sparsity-promoting Bernoulli-Gaussian prior, a likelihood-guided annealed Langevin sampler provably recovers the sparse signal in polynomial time with near-optimal sample complexity for a broad family of random and deterministic sensing matrices. When the signal is indeed drawn from the postulated prior, we further establish total variation guarantees for posterior sampling after a final denoising step. These results lay a theoretical foundation for statistically and computationally efficient inverse solvers with diffusion priors.

items.title: Duality for Cohen--Macaulay Complexes through Combinatorial Sheaves
items.summary: We prove a duality theorem for Cohen--Macaulay simplicial complexes. This is a generalisation of Poincaré Duality, framed in the language of combinatorial sheaves. Our treatment is self-contained and accessible for readers with a working knowledge of simplicial complexes and (co)homology. The main motivation is a link with Bieri-Eckmann duality for discrete groups, which is explored in a companion paper.

items.title: Boundedness of the Riesz potential associated to diffusion operators in Lebesgue spaces
items.summary: We revisit boundedness of the Riesz potential associated to a diffusion operator both in fixed and variable exponent Lebesgue spaces. We obtain optimal asymptotics in the former setting and we provide new tools to establish boundedness in the latter.

items.title: Data-driven control of polynomial systems using implicit methods
items.summary: While conventional behavioral data-driven control represents linear time-invariant (LTI) systems directly from data, extending these data representations to nonlinear systems remains an open challenge. We address this gap for general polynomial systems, characterizing their finite-length trajectories as a real algebraic variety defined by implicit polynomial relations rather than explicit equations. First, we provide conditions on measured data under which these data can be used to represent the system. Building on this representation, we formulate data-driven simulation and predictive control problems that are equivalent to their model-based counterparts, and solve the resulting polynomial systems globally using homotopy continuation. Numerical case studies confirm the effectiveness of this approach by successfully simulating a stiff Van der Pol oscillator in situations where explicit models fail. Furthermore, these data-driven simulation and control methods are illustrated on a Duffing oscillator, demonstrating that our method outperforms Koopman-based approaches in predicting long trajectories.

items.title: Asymptotics for generalized integer partitions
items.summary: We study the asymptotic behavior of weighted partition functions $p_f(n)$, defined by the generating function $\prod_{n \geq 1} (1 - q^{n})^{-f(n)}$ with non-negative real weights $f(n)$. We assume that the associated Dirichlet series $D(s) = \sum_{n \geq 1} f(n) n^{-s}$ admits a meromorphic continuation to a half-plane $\Re(s) \geq -\varepsilon$, with finitely many real poles of arbitrary orders, the largest of which is a positive pole $α$ of order $k$, and a possibly infinite collection of complex poles lying strictly to the left of $α$, with some additional conditions. We extend the saddle-point method of Debruyne and Tenenbaum, and show that the pole $α$ dominates the contribution of all other poles. As a result, we give an explicit asymptotic formula for $p_f(n)$ described via generalized Lambert functions. Furthermore, we show that for $k \geq 2$ no finite combination of powers of $n$, $\log n$, $\log \log n, \ldots$ approximates the saddle point well enough to give an asymptotic formula for $p_f(n)$. We also discuss a number of applications related to algebra, number theory, and combinatorics.

items.title: A Cubic Obstruction to Sums of Tripotent and Square-Zero Matrices
items.summary: Let $R$ be a nonzero unital ring of characteristic $2$, and let $λ$ be a central unit of $R$. We prove that an element $a\in R$ satisfying $a^3+a^2+λ=0$ cannot be expressed as the sum of a tripotent element and a square-zero element. The proof does not require the summands to commute. Over $\F_2$, this gives counterexamples in every order divisible by three, including order twelve, and proves the optimality of the known uniform exponent four in those orders. We also give constructive proofs that every matrix of order four or five over $\F_2$ is a sum of a tripotent and a square-zero matrix, and deduce a complete criterion in order three. Combining the cubic obstruction with the quartic obstruction for idempotent-plus-cube-zero decompositions, we obtain two-way incomparability of the corresponding decomposition classes in every positive order divisible by twelve.

items.title: The number of $k$-factors of a random regular graph
items.summary: Let $Z_k(G)$ be the number of $k$-factors ($k$-regular spanning subgraphs) of a uniformly random simple $d$-regular graph $G\sim G(n,d)$, where $d\ge 3$ and $1\le k\le d-1$ are fixed integers such that $dn$ and $kn$ are even. We determine the asymptotic second moment of $Z_k(G)$ and show that $Z_k(G)/\mathbb{E} Z_k(G)$ converges in distribution to an explicit random variable $W$ that depends on the short-cycle counts of $G$ but not on $k$. Moreover, for any $1\le k,\ell\le d-1$, the normalised counts on the same graph satisfy $Z_k(G)/\mathbb{E} Z_k(G) - Z_\ell(G)/\mathbb{E} Z_\ell(G) \to 0$ in probability, and, since $W>0$ almost surely, their ratio converges to $1$ in probability. This extends results of Bollobás--McKay and Janson for $k=1$ and Robalewska for $k=2$ to all $1\le k\le d-1$. In the pairing model, the second moment reduces to a one-dimensional lattice sum over the overlap of two $k$-factors. We evaluate this sum using the Poisson-binomial representation of the hypergeometric distribution, exponential tilting, and a uniform local limit theorem.

items.title: Lagrangian slice disks with symplectomorphic exteriors
items.summary: By modifying a construction of Abe and Tange, we exhibit arbitrarily large families of Lagrangian slice disks with Weinstein deformation equivalent exteriors. This answers a Lagrangian version of a question of Hitt and Sumners. We raise other open questions related to Lagrangian slice disks and their exteriors.

items.title: Quasimonomial Monge--Ampère equations for big classes
items.summary: Let X be a normal projective variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We describe an alternative approach to a differentiability result of volumes of norms defined by finitely many quasimonomial valuations. As a consequence, we prove the non-Archimedean Calabi--Yau theorem for quasimonomial measures on $X$ with respect to big classes, in the trivially valued case. We also obtain continuity of solutions as numerical classes vary in the big cone. This extends previous results of Boucksom--Jonsson and Dervan--Reboulet, and gives the first uniqueness results in the big case. Our approach relies on convex geometry and Okounkov bodies, without involving non-Archimedean pluripotential theory or test configurations.

items.title: A limit theorem for deviation of ergodic integrals on a class of flows on the two-torus
items.summary: We study the fluctuations of ergodic integrals for locally Hamiltonian flows on the two-torus with a single non-degenerate saddle (Arnol'd flows). We sample a flow from a suitably random family, together with a base point $p$ chosen uniformly at random on that flow's domain. For a smooth observable $f$, we show that the centered Birkhoff integral $\int_{0}^t f(φ_s p)\,ds-t\bar f$, where $\bar f$ is the spatial mean of $f$, normalized by $(\log t)^2$, converges in distribution to the product of two independent random variables. Using special representation of locally Hamiltonian flows, we reduce the problem to studying ergodic sums of functions with logarithmic singularities over circle rotations. Then, we prove a Cauchy limit theorem for such ergodic sums, which is a result of independent interest.

items.title: Cwikel and Kato-Seiler-Simon estimates for commutators
items.summary:
We prove that the commutator $[a(X),b(-\mathrm{i}
abla)]$ belongs to the weak Schatten class $\mathcal{S}^p_{m weak}$ provided $
abla a\in L^p$ and $
abla b\in L^p_{m weak}$ for $\max\{1,2d/(d+2)\}<p<\infty$. This is an analogue of Cwikel's estimate, with a larger range of exponents. We also prove analogues of the Kato-Seiler-Simon and Birman-Solomyak-Simon estimates. Counterexamples show the necessity of the lower thresholds and the failure of the Lipschitz endpoint estimate.

items.title: On metric multiplicative Diophantine approximation
items.summary: Gallagher's theorem (1962) gives a Khintchine-type dichotomy for the Lebesgue measure of the set of multiplicatively $ψ$-approximable points in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \geq 2$, for monotonic functions $ψ$. We establish this dichotomy for arbitrary functions $ψ$, proving a conjecture of Beresnevich, Haynes, and Velani (2013).

items.title: Trickle groups on a complete graph are linear
items.summary: Trickle groups were recently introduced by Bellingeri, Godelle and Paris, as generalizations of both cactus groups and right-angled Coxeter and Artin groups. We construct a representation of any trickle group $\mathrm{Tr}(Γ)$ with complete graph $Γ$ on a space having a basis in bijection with the vertex set $V(Γ)$, and show that it is faithful. This in particular shows that trickle Garside groups are linear. It also allows one to realize every finite trickle group as a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_{|V(Γ)|}(\mathbb{C})$. We do not use the results of Bellingeri, Godelle and Paris; instead we rather show that several properties of trickle groups that they obtained (and also some new ones) can easily be proven in the particular case of a complete graph using our representation. This includes the normal forms, the embedding of the trickle monoid inside the group in the case where $μ(x)=\infty$ for all $x\in V(Γ)$, and the absence of torsion of the latter. In this last case we give a second proof of faithfulness in the spirit of Krammer-Hée, which explains how to read Garside-theoretic information from the representation.

items.title: Stafford's conjecture on cyclicity of torsion modules
items.summary: We prove that over a Weyl algebra over a field of characteristic zero $A_n(k)$, every nonzero $d\in A_n(k)$ admits $F,R,S\in A_n(k)$ such that $1=dR+FdS$, a conjecture Stafford proposed in 1978. As a consequence, every finitely generated torsion right $A_n(k)$-module is cyclic. The proof maps $d$, by a symplectic change of variables, to a normal form $\tilde d$ and shows that the cyclic module $Q=A_n(k)/(\tilde dA_n(k)+x_1^N\tilde dA_n(k))$ vanishes. We first show that right multiplication by $x_1$ is surjective on $Q$. A comparison of lengths of localized modules over the associated graded ring then gives $\operatorname{gr}Q=x_1\operatorname{gr}Q$, so that the characteristic variety of $Q$ is disjoint from the hyperplane $\{x_1=0\}$. Finally, Gabber's involutivity theorem together with an argument about conormal directions at infinity from algebraic geometry shows that such a characteristic variety must be empty and therefore, $Q = 0$.

items.title: Volume growth and gap Theorem for manifolds with non-negative complex sectional curvature
items.summary: The combined work of Liu, Ni, and Ni-Tam established that a complete Kähler manifold with positive bisectional curvature has Euclidean volume growth if and only if its curvature decays quadratically on average. In this work, we use the approximation scheme developed by Cabezas-Rivas and Wilking to establish the Riemannian analogue under the assumption of nonnegative complex sectional curvature. As an application, we prove an optimal gap theorem for manifolds with nonnegative complex sectional curvature. These results generalize the authors' earlier work.

items.title: The number of cycles in a random 2-factor of a random regular graph
items.summary: We study the number of cycles $X$ in a uniformly random 2-factor $F$ of a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices (in the pairing model) for any fixed $d\ge 3$. When the pairing $P$ and the 2-factor $F\subseteq P$ are chosen uniformly at random together, the probability generating function of $X$ is $Γ(n+\tfrac u2)Γ(\tfrac12)/\bigl(Γ(n+\tfrac12)Γ(\tfrac u2)\bigr)$, which does not depend on $d$. Consequently, $X$ has mean $\tfrac12\log n+O(1)$ and variance $\tfrac12\log n+O(1)$, satisfies a central limit theorem, and equals $1$ (so that $F$ is a Hamilton cycle) with probability $Θ(n^{-1/2})$. Using an exact formula for the second moment of the cycle generating polynomial together with small subgraph conditioning, we transfer these results to a uniformly random 2-factor of a fixed random regular graph.

items.title: Proof of the polygonal Saint-Venant inequality conjectured by Pólya--Szegö
items.summary: We prove the polygonal Saint--Venant inequality conjectured by Pólya and Szegö: for every $n\geq 3$, among (possibly non--convex) polygons of prescribed area with at most $n$ sides, the regular $n$-gon uniquely maximizes torsional rigidity. The proof is purely analytic and stems from the local version of the result given in our previous paper: it combines an area--angle proportional partition of a polygon, inspired by Solynin and Zalgaller, with a sharp comparison for the mixed torsional rigidity of the partition cells, and with an angular concavity property of this functional on the class of isosceles triangles.

items.title: An asymptotic ball algebra with countably determined spectra and a nonseparable character space
items.summary: Let $X=\partial\mathbb B_2\subset\mathbb C^2$ and let $\mathcal R$ be the restrictions to $X$ of functions in the ball algebra $A(\overline{\mathbb B_2})$. The unital uniform Banach algebra \[ \mathcal A=\{(f_n)\in\ell^\infty(\mathbb N,C(X)):\mathrm{dist}_{C(X)}(f_n,\mathcal R)\longrightarrow0\} \] is inverse-closed in $\ell^\infty(\mathbb N,C(X))$. Consequently one countable family of evaluation characters generates the spectrum of every element of $\mathcal A$. Nevertheless $Δ(\mathcal A)$ contains continuum many pairwise disjoint nonempty open subsets and is therefore nonseparable. This gives a negative answer to a problem posed by Ohrysko, Wojciechowski and Graham.

items.title: Cox rings of Jacobian elliptic surfaces of Kodaira dimension one
items.summary: We study Cox rings of relatively minimal semistable Jacobian elliptic surfaces over $\mathbb P^1$ with $χ=χ(\mathcal O_X)\ge3$ and finite Mordell--Weil group. When the Mori cone is generated by the zero section and the reducible-fiber components, we give a finite criterion for Cox-ring generation: a numerically determined set of nef classes must admit sections nonvanishing along the zero section. The criterion supplies a minimal homogeneous generating set without assuming finite generation in advance. We prove that its nonvanishing condition holds whenever $\sum_i n_i\le2χ+4$, where $I_{n_i}$ are the reducible fibers; hence every such surface is a Mori dream surface. Independently of this condition, we exclude ample generator degrees throughout the stated cone range. We also determine the section--fiber subring and give minimal complete-intersection presentations when all $s$ reducible fibers have type $I_2$ and $s\le2χ+1$, including the endpoint beyond that cone range.

items.title: The Capillary Dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
items.summary:
We study a capillary dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski problem on a spherical cap. For $2\le k\le n$, $1<p<k+1$, and $0<θ<π/2$, we consider \[ σ_k(
abla^2h+hσ) = f(ξ)h^{p-1} rac{ρ^{k+1}}{\varphi(ρ)}, \qquad ρ=(h^2+|
abla h|^2)^{1/2}, \] with the capillary Robin condition $
abla_μh=\cotθ\,h$. Assuming that $f$ is positive, smooth and horizontally even, $g=f^{-1/(p+k-1)}$ satisfies the capillary spherical-convexity and boundary compatibility conditions, and $H(r)=\varphi(r)/r^p$ is strictly increasing and proper with $Q_\varphi(r)\le k+1$, we prove the existence of a smooth, positive, horizontally even solution that is strictly capillary convex. The proof uses an Orlicz homotopy, uniform a priori estimates, a viscosity constant-rank argument when $k<n$, global oblique regularity, and degree theory.

items.title: Quaternionic Torus Actions on Manifolds
items.summary: We study smooth actions of quaternionic tori $\operatorname{SU}(2)^r$ on closed, connected smooth manifolds, establishing sharp bounds for $r$ in terms of the dimension of the manifold when the action is either effective, effective almost-free, or almost-effective. In particular, we prove that an almost-effective $\operatorname{SU}(2)^r$-action on an $n$-dimensional manifold satisfies $r\leq \lfloor2n/3\rfloor$, and we classify up to diffeomorphism all simply connected manifolds attaining the maximal possible rank. This gives a quaternionic counterpart of the maximal symmetry rank conjecture without any curvature assumption. We also establish the bounds $r\leq n/3$ for effective and effective almost-free quaternionic torus actions, and we compute the exact value for spheres, quoric manifolds, or manifolds of the form $(S^3)^a\times (S^1)^b$.

items.title: Asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares
items.summary: We introduce some new general techniques for studying asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares. Using these techniques, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the probability that a given 'small' partial Latin square $H$ is present in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (as conjectured by Divoux-Kelly-Kennedy-Sidhu). As applications, we determine which configurations are likely to appear in random Latin squares (resolving a conjecture of Allsop-Morris), we determine the asymptotic distribution of the number of $3\times 3$ Latin subsquares in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (resolving conjectures of McKay-Wanless and Kwan-Sah-Sawhney), and we show that the first two rows of a random $n\times n$ Latin square are statistically indistinguishable from a random derangement (answering a conjecture of Cameron and Cavenagh-Greenhill-Wanless).

items.title: Positivity and uniform log-concavity for rank-two Chern coefficients
items.summary: We study the binomial-basis coefficients in the Schur expansion of the Chern classes of symmetric powers of a rank-two bundle. Bérczi and Fehér conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative and log-concave in the Newton index. An inverse-series formula yields an integral gamma-positive refinement with exact support and a positive expression for the derivatives of the shifted Chern quotient. We prove that generalized Bernoulli polynomials of real order at least their degree have simple real zeros. Applied to the shifted quotient, this gives strict ultra-log-concavity in the Schur index at every positive shift. For the original Newton coefficients, we establish strict log-concavity with an explicit multiplicative margin in two uniform regions. A Hahn projection gives a square-root band about the balanced Schur index; a complex saddle estimate extends this to a band of linear width. Uniform estimates for the cumulants of a normalized Schur functional give a terminal Newton region of linear width. Polynomial coefficient identities also establish every row with Schur index at most six or imbalance at most nine. The argument separates log-concavity in the Schur, derivative and Newton indices and identifies the factorial factors in the transfer between the latter two. The unrestricted Newton log-concavity conjecture remains open.

items.title: Complete Intersection Semigroups and End Curves on Singularities of Splice Type
items.summary: We prove that any complete intersection numerical semigroup can be realized as the value semigroup of an end curve in a splice quotient singularity. Therefore, providing a converse to the semigroup-theoretic statement of the End Curve Theorem of Neumann and Wahl for integral homology sphere links. For a certain family of curves embedded on splice quotient singularities with $\mathbb{Z}HS^3$ link, we show the coincidence between the Alexander polynomial of the knot cutted out by the curve and its Poincaré series. Hence providing a generalization of the result due to Campillo, Delgado and Gusein-Zade for plane curve singularities. Moreover, for any complete-intersection numerical semigroup, we define a family of knots such that the Alexander polynomial of the knots coincides with the generating series of the semigroup.

items.title: Taming the Tails of Stochastic Gradient Descent in the Interpolation Regime
items.summary: In this paper, we study stochastic gradient descent in the smooth interpolation regime, where the population objective shares a common minimizer with the sample losses. In contrast to prior work, which has largely focused on in-expectation analysis, we obtain high-probability convergence guarantees under the same assumptions. In the convex case, we prove a fast rate of order $\log(β^{-1}) \cdot n^{-1}$ after $n$ iterations, with failure probability at most $β$. In the strongly convex case, we derive a family of moment-based bounds of order $β^{-p} \cdot \exp(-\mathcal{O}(p \cdot n))$ for $p \in (0,1]$, and complement them with a matching lower bound showing that the corresponding deterioration in the exponential rate is essentially unavoidable. In both settings, our theoretical results are unified across a broad class of step-size schedules. Building on this analysis, we extend our results to a low-noise regime and to nonconvex objectives satisfying the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition.

items.title: A Cheng-type Eigenvalue-Comparison Theorem for the Hodge Laplacian
items.summary: We consider the class of closed Riemannian $n$-manifolds with Ricci curvature and injectivity radius bounded below by uniform constants, and an upper bound on the diameter. We establish a uniform upper bound for the eigenvalues of the Hodge Laplacian acting on differential forms on Riemannian manifolds in this class, similar to the classical eigenvalue comparison theorem proved by Cheng for the Laplace-Beltrami operator acting on smooth functions. This extends earlier work of Dodziuk and Lott, which required sectional curvature bounds in addition to bounds on other geometric quantities. As an application, we obtain uniform eigenvalue estimates for the connection Laplacian acting on $1$-forms.

items.title: Adelic points and unmramified Brauer approximation for classifying stacks
items.summary: Let $k$ be a number field. We study adelic topologies and strong approximation for classifying stacks. For a connected linear algebraic group $G$, we relate the Brauer-Manin obstruction on $BG$ to Kottwitz's localisation sequence and identify the quotient of the unramified Brauer group of $BG$ by the Brauer group of $k$ with the cyclic Tate-Shafarevich group of the character module of $G$. This yields a local criterion for strong approximation with respect to the unramified Brauer group. Finally, for an abelian variety $A$, we compute the cohomological Brauer group of $BA$ and show that, when the group of $k$-rational points on the dual abelian variety has positive rank, strong approximation with respect to the full Brauer group fails off every finite set of places.

items.title: A Trajectory-Based Mathematical Framework for Wildfire Front Propagation in Heterogeneous Landscapes
items.summary: We present a mathematical formulation based on trajectories for modeling the propagation of wildfire fronts in heterogeneous landscapes and apply it to the Brazilian Pantanal. The formulation is made up of a direction-dependent propagation law and Finsler orthogonality along a moving boundary. This results in a nonlinear local system for outward fire front trajectories. We provide a strictly convex translated ellipse representation at each point of the evolving boundary which guaranties uniqueness and existence of the chosen outward velocity. The effective propagation coefficients that are dependent on space and the hourly wind forcing permit the perimeter to evolve irregularly without imposing a fixed global front geometry. Computed trajectories were georeferenced and isotropically spatially registered with VIIRS active-fire observations. ERA5 wind and ERA5-Land vegetation data were used to describe the environmental forcing and landscape heterogeneity. The full-run Dice coefficients for the observation-guided spatial comparisons for the exploratory experiments for September 3-5, 2020 are 0.578, 0.571, and 0.467 respectively. One-at-a-time sensitivity perturbations of the spatial propagation coefficient, wind speed magnitude and rate-law exponents quantify the governing influence of the environmental forcing and parameter variations on the spatial extent of the calculated fire advance. These observed patterns also guided calibration and, in the absence of exact timestamps of satellite acquisition, the results show within-event spatial agreement rather than independent predictive validation. The framework provides a mathematically rigorous basis for subsequent uncertainty quantification, independent validation over multiple events and prospective sector-wise assessments of simulated fire spread.

items.title: Further simulations between tropical and linear programming
items.summary: Propositional proof systems that apply various kinds of cuts to linear inequalities (such as Cutting Planes [CCT87] and Lift&Project [BCC93,Pud99,Das05]) or operate with disjunctions of linear inequalities (such as Res(CP) [Kra98] and Res(LP) [HK06]) have been in the focus of research for the past 30 years. Recently, tropical proof systems were introduced [AGH25]; they resemble the latter systems but differ from them in important respects. The relations between the traditional systems and the new tropical systems have remained largely unknown, and exponential lower bounds for tropical systems were limited to non-CNF examples. In this paper we prove several new polynomial simulations between these systems. To this end, we introduce Thr-Res (Threshold Resolution), a new natural daglike proof system operating on threshold conditions over the Boolean literals: lines asserting that at least s literals of a given multiset are true. Its main difference from CP is that the rounding rule (without it CP is incomplete) is replaced by a weaker rule that allows one to perform "resolution" steps with linear combinations beyond Boolean clauses; also, in its addition rules, Thr-Res resembles input resolution [Cha70]: a derived line is combined with an input clause or an axiom, whereas CP can add up any two derived lines. By varying the maximum value of s, one obtains systems ranging in strength from Resolution to MP-NSR, the static tropical (min-plus) proof system introduced in [AGH25]. As a consequence, we prove that MP-NSR is polynomially simulated by CP and L&P (even by their unary versions), which automatically yields exponential lower bounds on the size of MP-NSR proofs for formulas in CNF. We complement it with simulations in the converse direction: binary daglike MP-PCR (a dynamic version of MP-NSR) polynomially simulates L&P; it also polynomially simulates CP when division axioms are added.

items.title: Polynomials from tilings of rectangles
items.summary: We study tilings of rectangular boards using unit squares together with a single type of big tile shaped as a Ferrers diagram. We derive generating functions for these tilings, prove real-rootedness and interlacing properties of associated independence polynomials, and establish connections with several sequences in the OEIS. Our results touch on tilings involving L-shaped polyominoes, fault-free tilings, and cylindric variants. For rectangular tiles of shape $(k,k)$, we prove real-rootedness and interlacing in the range $d\leq k$.

items.title: The Suspension of the Milnor Fiber as a Local Conley Index
items.summary: Let $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C},0)$ be a holomorphic germ with an isolated critical point at the origin, and let $\varphi_f$ be the local negative gradient flow of $\operatorname{Re}f$ for a smooth Riemannian metric. We compute the pointed homotopy Conley index $h(\varphi_f,\{0\})\simeqΣF_f\simeq\bigvee_{j=1}^{μ(f)}S^n$, where $F_f$ is the Milnor fiber and $Σ$ denotes reduced suspension. The index is independent of the metric, and its reduced integral homology has rank $μ(f)$ in degree $n$ and vanishes otherwise. The proof uses continuation to a holomorphic morsification. Conservation of the imaginary part for a Hermitian metric allows a target rotation to exclude connecting orbits, so the homotopy-level sum property applies. We also give spherical index pairs for homogeneous and weighted homogeneous functions, describe quadratic splitting, and recover the Poincaré--Hopf index through McCord's theorem.

items.title: Subword enumeration up to stack-sorting equivalence
items.summary: Defant and Kravitz introduced generalizations of West's stack-sorting map $s$ from permutations to finite words. This raises questions as to how such generalizations could be applied in the field of combinatorics on words. The Defant-Kravitz generalizations of $s$ depend on how repeated occurrences of the same character within a word may be repositioned, according to their $\textsf{tortoise}$ and $\textsf{hare}$ operations. As demonstrated in this paper, these operations provide a natural way of extending abelian complexity functions for infinite sequences, in a way that gives light to structural properties associated with infinite words. We apply these new ideas to two famous infinite words: the paperfolding word and the Thue-Morse word. In the case of the Thue-Morse word, we discover an interesting connection to the previous work of several authors, such as de Luca and Varricchio, on the ``special'' factors of the Thue-Morse word. This may be seen as providing a basis for a new and interdisciplinary area linking the combinatorics about the stack-sorting of permutations with the field of combinatorics on words.

items.title: Treewidth 3 in the Product Structure Theorem for Bounded Degree Graphs in Minor-Closed Classes
items.summary: We show that, for all positive integers $t$ and $Δ$, there exists an integer $c$ such that, for every $K_t$-minor-free graph $G$ with maximum degree at most $Δ$, there exists a graph $H$ of treewidth at most $3$ and a path $P$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of the strong product $H\boxtimes P\boxtimes K_c$. This improves on a previous result of Dujumović, Esperet, Micek, Walczak, and Wood (2022) by bounding the treewidth of $H$ independently of $t$ and $Δ$. As an immediate consequence we obtain a bound of $O(r^4)$ on the $r$-weak colouring number of bounded-degree graphs from any proper minor-closed graph class.

items.title: Restoring Power Fairly: Equitable Resource Allocation in Post-Disaster Grid Recovery
items.summary: Post-disaster power restoration requires allocating limited repair and power resources across affected communities, creating a fundamental tension between restoring service efficiently and providing equitable access to electricity. We develop an optimization framework incorporating horizontal fairness, which promotes comparable service across affected communities, and vertical fairness, which accounts for differences in community vulnerability. The framework integrates repair-crew scheduling with an approximation of power-system operations, including distributed generation and solar-plus-storage resources. It supports vulnerability-aware prioritization while protecting specified fractions of bus-level service under a horizontal-fairness reference plan and limiting the increase in restoration cost. Structural results characterize when the two fairness benchmarks can be attained simultaneously in an aggregate allocation model and provide a sufficient condition under which improving vertical fairness requires changing discrete decisions in the full restoration model. Using the IEEE 33-bus test system, we show that equitable restoration operates through two interconnected mechanisms: reconnecting isolated areas and allocating limited power within connected areas. In the tested setting, selected vulnerability-aware solutions attain both fairness benchmarks at a lower cost than their horizontal-fairness reference plan. The results also show that stronger emphasis on horizontal fairness can yield lower efficiency losses than intermediate fairness settings, with an identical-demand comparison illustrating the role of demand heterogeneity. The framework helps decision makers identify the operational sources of service disparities and evaluate how repair priorities, power allocation, and allowable cost increases affect the opportunities to reduce them.

items.title: Assessing model calibration with boosting trees
items.summary: The main goal in regression modelling consists in approximating the conditional mean of a response given a set of features. A regression function is said to be strongly calibrated if the resulting mean estimates match the true conditional means for almost every set of features. Aiming for strong calibration seems not achievable in practice as one typically deals with finite samples of noisy observations. A weaker notion of calibration is auto-calibration, and it means that the conditional expectation of the response, given a mean estimate, matches this estimate. This notion is important, e.g., in insurance pricing as it ensures no cross-subsidization between different price cohorts. In this paper, we show that boosting trees can be used to test necessary conditions for strong calibration and auto-calibration, respectively. The practical relevance of our approach is supported by a numerical example, in which the proposed tests achieve high empirical power.

items.title: Torsion order and the next-to-top term of knot Floer homology
items.summary: Sivek conjectured that, for every nontrivial knot $K\subset S^3$, the dimension of the next-to-top term of $\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(K)$ is at least that of the top term. We show that this inequality holds for knots with $U$-torsion order one in either the minus theory $\mathrm{HFK}^-$ or the unoriented theory $\mathrm{HFK}'$. Combined with Eftekhary's work, this implies that knots with rational unknotting number one satisfy the conjecture. In particular, the result applies to every nontrivial satellite knot whose pattern can be unknotted in the solid torus by a single rational tangle replacement.

items.title: A unified Sobolev framework for long-wave limits of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation
items.summary: We present a unified justification of the KdV, Airy, inviscid Burgers, and Whitham approximations for the one-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii equation in Sobolev spaces. Using energy estimates for its Madelung formulation, we establish quantitative error bounds on the natural time scales of the respective approximations. The analysis covers different long-wave scaling regimes within a single framework.

items.title: Cosmetic crossings and the knot complement problem
items.summary: We prove the cosmetic crossing conjecture, Problem 1.58 in Kirby's list, and the generalized cosmetic crossing conjecture for every knot whose branched double cover is an L-space; in particular, both hold for all alternating and all quasi-alternating knots. We also prove the oriented knot complement conjecture, Problem 1.81(D), for all closed 3-manifolds with finite fundamental group, in particular for all lens spaces: in such a manifold, every knot whose exterior is irreducible and not a solid torus is determined by its complement. Both results rest on a monotonicity theorem for Heegaard Floer correction terms: if a knot in a rational homology sphere has an isotropic, nonzero homology class, then the sum of all correction terms strictly increases along its surgeries with coefficients -1/j relative to the rational longitude, so no nontrivial surgery yields the original oriented manifold. We also show that every purely cosmetic band surgery on a knot with an L-space branched double cover is weakly nugatory, which answers a question of Rogers for these knots.

items.title: New Heuristics for Large-Scale Joint Order Selection, Allocation, Batching, and Picking
items.summary: Manual order picking in warehouses plays an important role in modern e-commerce fulfillment. In this work, we consider a warehouse fulfillment model recently introduced by researchers at Zalando, a leading fashion e-commerce company. It simultaneously models the hierarchy of decision stages in a very large-scale setting with a semi-online order set, where only a certain number of items have to be fulfilled in each time interval. For their base model, we present both new and improved algorithms together with comprehensive performance evaluation. We further extend the model to a setting with multiple phases, which more closely represents the situation observed in real warehouses, and adapt the algorithms to this setting, including new variants that incorporate multi-phase specific features. We demonstrate that this extension allows us to model, control, and optimize for certain parameters such as order age which play an important role in managerial considerations with the growing importance of next or even same day delivery.

items.title: Free Products of Vector Lattices
items.summary: We study free products of vector lattices and their relation to free products of Banach lattices. We characterize the Archimedean vector lattices whose vector lattice free product with every Archimedean vector lattice is again Archimedean: these are precisely those whose finitely generated sublattices are projective. For finitely generated lattices, this connects the free-product property with polyhedral geometry through Baker--Beynon duality. We also show that the Banach lattice free product is the completion of the Archimedean vector lattice free product under the largest lattice norm making the canonical maps contractive. For finitely many factors, the Archimedean vector lattice free product is order dense in the Banach lattice free product. Moreover, it is shown that bounded families of injective lattice homomorphisms also induce injective homomorphisms between Banach lattice free products. Finally, in analogy with the theory of separably injective Banach lattices, we study relative injectivity and universal disposition for the class of vector lattices with countably many proper prime ideals. Every vector lattice embeds into one of universal disposition for this class, while ordered ultrapowers of the real line provide relatively injective examples of cardinality continuum.

items.title: A counterexample to Molchan's orthant persistence conjecture
items.summary: We refute Molchan's conjecture that the persistence probability of the isotropic fractional Brownian field on $[0,R]^d$ satisfies $p_{d,H}(R)=R^{-d(1-H)+o(1)}$ as $R\to\infty$. We prove $$ \limsup_{d\to\infty}\limsup_{R\to\infty} \frac{-\log p_{d,H}(R)}{d\log R} \le 1-\frac{49}{48}H+o(H), \qquad H\downarrow 0. $$ Thus the conjecture fails for every sufficiently small fixed Hurst parameter in all sufficiently large dimensions. A finite-step Gaussian interpolation inequality on the exact positive sphere is proved in an appendix.

items.title: Failure of the $L^p$ Neumann problem in bi-Lipschitz images of a ball
items.summary: For every $n\geq 2$ we construct a bounded domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^{n+1}$, which is the image of the unit ball under a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism of $\mathbb R^{n+1}$, and a bounded Neumann datum $g$ with zero mean such that the variational solution $u$ of the Neumann problem with datum $g$ satisfies $\mathcal N(\nabla u)\notin L^1(\partialΩ)$. In particular, the $L^p$ Neumann problem is not solvable in $Ω$ for any $1<p<\infty$, although $Ω$ is a two-sided chord-arc domain whose boundary supports a weak $(1,1)$-Poincaré inequality, and although in this class of domains the Dirichlet and the regularity problems are solvable for some exponents. This answers in the negative a question of C. Kenig, and it also shows that, unlike the solvability of the Dirichlet problem, the solvability of the $L^p$ Neumann problem for some $p\in (1,\infty)$ is not invariant under bi-Lipschitz homeomorphisms of $\mathbb R^{n+1}$.

items.title: Nine-Colored Partition Components Modulo 19
items.summary: Let $p_{m}(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$ into parts of $m$ colors, and let $y=q^{19}$. Starting from Winquist's identity, as Hirschhorn did for the modulus $11$, we express each of the nineteen components of $(q;q)_{\infty}^{10}$ modulo $19$ as a sum of two quartic products of the theta functions $(y^{a};y^{19})_{\infty}(y^{19-a};y^{19})_{\infty}$, and deduce all nineteen generating functions $\sum_{n} p_{9}(19n+r)y^{n}$ modulo $19$ in closed form. The vanishing class $p_{9}(19n+17)$ is the one known previously. For seventeen colors, the residue class singled out by Kiming and Olsson carries no congruence, and we show that its generating function is $y f(y^{19})^{2}/f(y)$ modulo $19$. Along the way, we recall, with proofs, such exact relationships known for all these congruences. O'Brien's cubic relation is a Weierstrass equation for $X_{0}(19)$ in Kolberg's coordinates; we prove the existence of a doubling automorphism of the theta functions, fixing the cubic, which acts on both dissections by explicit scalars. All proofs are by hand.

items.title: About the occurrence of Akhmediev breathers in dispersive systems
items.summary: Akhmediev breathers are spatially periodic solutions of the NLS equation which are localized in time. We prove a new NLS approximation result for dispersive wave systems, showing that there are solutions to these systems where Akhmediev breathers in the lowest order approximately modulate the underlying wave packet. Since the solutions of the original wave system are quasi-periodic in space, the main challenge is to find an appropriate function space to estimate the approximation error.

items.title: Axiomatic Sectional category, Topological complexity, and Homotopic distance
items.summary: Many of the properties of sectional category, topological complexity and homotopic distance are in fact derived from a small number of basic properties, which, once established, lead to all the others without further recourse to topology. On the other hand, there are several variants of these notions: with open covers or else Whitehead-Ganea constructions, also with spaces and maps that are unpointed or else pointed, fibrewise, equivariant, etc. or even with algebraic models of spaces and maps. These are two reasons why we build an axiomatic approach to all these notions, based on just three simple axioms. We also introduce the notion of `lifting category' which unifies the notions of sectional category, topological complexity, and homotopic distance, all of which are special cases of lifting category.

items.title: Koopman Observability of Nonlinear Systems and Data-Driven Koopman--Luenberger Observer
items.summary: While nonlinear systems can be generally described as infinite-dimensional linear systems via their Koopman semigroups, the direct synthesis of state observers on the premise of learned Koopman operator models, in an analogous manner to finite-dimensional linear systems, remains an open problem. In this paper, the concepts of Koopman observability, Koopman detectability, and Koopman--Luenberger observer of nonlinear systems are provided. By defining the Koopman semigroup on a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), the conditions for Koopman exponential detectability are established, which involves solving an operator Lyapunov inequality that only implicitly involves the infinitesimal generator of the Koopman semigroup. Through the use of a finite-horizon Yosida approximation of the Koopman generator and an empirical sampling operator, the data-driven solution of the observer gain can be reduced to a finite-dimensional subspace specified by the sample and hence fulfilled by convex semidefinite programming (SDP). The state observation error is guaranteed to be bounded in a mean-squares sense, under closed-loop dissipation conditions on the sampling operator and its empirical operator.

items.title: Holomorphic Vector Bundles on the Quantum Projective Line
items.summary: We study Birkhoff--Grothendieck splitting for holomorphic vector bundles on the quantum projective line in the Dolbeault-module framework. We prove that every polynomial holomorphic bundle admitting a finite filtration by standard line objects is a direct sum of standard lines, with uniquely determined splitting integers. The proof uses a Dolbeault differential graded category and the two-arrow Kronecker quiver. For a three-parameter rank-two extension family, we determine the splitting types and distinguish the nonzero splitting strata by the determinant of a quantum connecting map. For general non-diagonal rank-two connections, we derive noncommutative Riccati equations for invariant graph submodules and formulate the global splitting problem in terms of holomorphic projectors. We also discuss twisted positive Hochschild cocycles and formulate a variational principle and a conformal-stability conjecture. On the algebraic side, we explain why both the bare sheaf category of the quantum projective line and the Artin--Zhang category of the quantum plane inherit classical Birkhoff--Grothendieck splitting. We distinguish these results from unrestricted standard-line splitting, which fails for polynomial gauges, and outline a differential quantum GAGA programme with explicit attention to regularity and equivariance.

items.title: Finite-Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes with Smooth Forcing, Part I: Construction of Self-Similar Solutions with Admissible Stress and Flat Remainder
items.summary: This paper gives a readable and accessible version of the profile-construction part of OpenAI's manuscript "Finite Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes". We regard OpenAI's work as a major advance on the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem. We construct an axisymmetric leading flow that is regular at the axis and sum its lower-order corrections to obtain an approximately self-similar background field. Its Navier-Stokes residual consists of a divergence-form term and a remainder vanishing to infinite order in $1-t$ on fixed similarity sectors. The associated stress and radial shear satisfy the admissible cone condition. The stress need not be small. We introduce a new linear model that provides a clearer explanation of the inner core construction. The cancellation of the divergence-form residual by oscillatory pulses is treated in the companion paper "Finite-Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes with Smooth Forcing, Part II: Residual Correction via Oscillatory Pulses" (arXiv:2611.06869). We claim no original mathematical contribution.

items.title: On the Order of Products of Coprime Elements in Finite Groups
items.summary: In this work, we introduce the subgroups $D_m(G)$ and $D_{m,n}(G)$ for a group $G$ with finite exponent. We show that both subgroups are characteristic, that $D_{m,n}(G)$ is always nilpotent, and that their nilpotent structure provides a characterization of Frobenius group decompositions. Furthermore, we define the $E_{m,n}$-series, which extends this framework to the study of an important class of solvable groups of Fitting height at most $4$. In this sense, we say that a group is $E_{m,n}$-nilpotent if it possesses a finite, strictly increasing $E_{m,n}$-series, and we prove that the maximum length of such a series in an $E_{m,n}$-nilpotent group is 4.

items.title: Katona's Shadow Equality Persists under Bounded VC-Dimension
items.summary: Katona's intersecting-shadow theorem states that every $t$-intersecting $r$-uniform family has size at most that of its $(r-t)$-shadow, with equality precisely for complete $r$-uniform families on $2r-t$ points. We prove that both the shadow inequality and its equality classification remain valid under the substantially weaker assumption that the VC-dimension is at most $r-t$. By contrast, bounded VC-dimension and $t$-intersection do not, in general, yield the same extremal bounds in the corresponding cardinality problem.

items.title: A combinatorial proof of a symmetric joint distribution on strict binary trees
items.summary: Nonplanar strict binary trees on $2n+1$ vertices are enumerated by the reduced tangent numbers $T_{2n+1}/2^n$, whose entries are refined by Poupard's triangle. Poupard defined the end of the minimal chain ($\mathrm{eoc}$) and the parent of the maximum leaf ($\mathrm{pom}$) on these trees, proving that $\mathrm{eoc}$ and $\mathrm{pom}+1$ share this triangular distribution. Foata and Han subsequently showed via tree calculus and partial difference equations that the joint distribution of $(\mathrm{eoc}, 2n+1-\mathrm{pom})$ is symmetric. By introducing an auxiliary tree statistic dual to $\mathrm{eoc}$, we give a bijective proof of this symmetry. Our proof composes a recursive bijection on strict binary trees, a bijection to alternating André permutations, and the reverse-complement involution on permutations.

items.title: Graph structure via local occupancy
items.summary: The first author together with Jenssen, Perkins and Roberts (2017) recently showed how local properties of the hard-core model on triangle-free graphs guarantee the existence of large independent sets, of size matching the best-known asymptotics due to Shearer (1983). The present work strengthens this in two ways: first, by guaranteeing stronger graph structure in terms of colourings through applications of the Lovász local lemma; and second, by extending beyond triangle-free graphs in terms of local sparsity, treating for example graphs of bounded local edge density, of bounded local Hall ratio, and of bounded clique number. This generalises and improves upon much other earlier work, including that of Shearer (1995), Alon (1996) and Alon, Krivelevich and Sudakov (1999), and more recent results of Molloy (2019), Bernshteyn (2019) and Achlioptas, Iliopoulos and Sinclair (2019). Our results derive from a common framework built around the hard-core model. It pivots on a property we call local occupancy, giving a clean separation between the methods for deriving graph structure with probabilistic information and verifying the requisite probabilistic information itself.

items.title: Sampling Density for Gabor Phase Retrieval
items.summary: We study sampling density and geometry for Gaussian Gabor phase retrieval on the full space $L^2(\mathbb R)$. We classify the power lattices $a\mathbb Z^ν\times b\mathbb Z^ν$ that determine every function up to a global phase. For $0<ν<1$ with $ν\ne1/2$, uniqueness holds for every $a,b>0$, whereas it fails for every pair when $ν\ge1$. At the square root scale, uniqueness holds whenever $a^2/b^2$ is irrational. If $a^2=κp$ and $b^2=κq$ with coprime positive integers $p,q$, it holds precisely when $κ\le1$. The critical case follows from a sharp quadratic growth bound, classification of its equality case, and Fock integrability. For $1/2<ν<1$, we prove the stronger modulus-uniqueness statement for all entire functions of finite quadratic type using only first-quadrant samples. We also give uniqueness and nonuniqueness conditions for samples on two intersecting or three parallel lines, relating the sampling scale to the geometry of the lines. The lattice classification extends coordinatewise to Gaussian Gabor measurements on $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$.

items.title: Distributionally robust chance-constrained standard quadratic optimization with Wasserstein ambiguity
items.summary: The standard quadratic optimization problem consists of minimizing a quadratic form over the standard simplex. It has highly relevant applications ranging from portfolio optimization to machine learning. However, if the quadratic form is neither convex nor concave, this problem is NP-hard. We study a distributionally robust chance-constrained variant whose ambiguity set is a Wasserstein ball around the sampled distribution and make four contributions. First, although the problem is nonconvex in the decision variable, we exploit its linear dependence on the uncertain matrix to reduce the problem to a mixed-integer nonlinear optimization problem. Second, we show that a judicious choice of matrix norm---the entrywise maximum norm---makes this reformulation both exact and tractable, and we describe the induced worst-case distribution. Third, our formulation is, by construction, the minimization of the worst-case Value-at-Risk of the random quadratic form; this unifies it with existing frameworks for uncertain standard quadratic optimization problems, in particular under chance constraints, and we identify natural settings in which it collapses to a single deterministic instance. Finally, we report numerical experiments on positive definite and indefinite instances which quantify how the model parameters drive the optimal value and solution time, and expose the computational cost of indefiniteness.

items.title: Open Homomorphisms between $m$-step Solvable Galois Groups of Number Fields
items.summary: Let $K,L$ be number fields, and let $m \geq 2$ be an integer. In this paper, we prove that an open homomorphism $φ_{m+2}: G_K^{m+2} \to G_L^{m+2}$ induces an open homomorphism $φ_m$ that arises uniquely from a field embedding $τ_m:L_m \hookrightarrow K_m$. We first establish a sharper version of the $m$-step solvable cyclotomic compatibility criterion by Mao and Saïdi: if $φ_{m+2}:G_K^{m+2}\to G_L^{m+2}$ is compatible with the cyclotomic characters, then the induced map $φ_m:G_K^m \to G_L^m$ arises uniquely from a field embedding $L_m \hookrightarrow K_m$. Then we apply the strategy of OpenAI's (together with Tsujimura's recent explanation of OpenAI's work) proposed proof of Uchida's conjecture to show that every open homomorphism $φ_4:G_K^4 \to G_L^4$ is automatically compatible with the cyclotomic characters.

items.title: On the parametric and semiparametric Fisher information matrix for non-zero mean stationary spherical invariant random processes
items.summary: The classical Whittle formula provides a closed-form expression for the asymptotic Fisher information matrix (FIM) rate of multidimensional, real-valued, zero-mean, purely nondeterministic stationary Gaussian processes (GPs), expressed in terms of their parameterized spectra within a maximum-likelihood framework. However, the Gaussian assumption underlying this result restricts its applicability to many real-world signals exhibiting heavy-tailed or non-Gaussian behavior. In this paper, we extend Whittle's result to multidimensional, real-valued stationary compound Gaussian processes (CGPs) with arbitrary mean, under a unified framework encompassing fully known, parameterized, and completely unknown density generators. Building upon the Slepian-Bangs formula for $n$ consecutive observations and extending it to the semiparametric setting, we leverage the asymptotic properties of block Toeplitz matrices to obtain a closed-form spectral-domain expression for the asymptotic FIM rate. The resulting expression, common to all density generator families, generalizes the standard zero-mean Gaussian formula by incorporating a distribution-dependent contribution associated with the nonzero mean, and an additional covariance term that is invariant to the choice of non-Gaussian distribution. This extension enables efficient and theoretically grounded performance analysis for heavy-tailed signal processing applications.

items.title: Word length, Morse theory, and Vietoris-Rips complexes
items.summary: We present a discrete Morse theoretic approach to proving high connectivity or contractibility of a Vietoris-Rips complex using distance to a fixed point as an initial measurement. In particular we focus on the case of a finitely generated group using word length. As a proof-of-concept application we prove that $\mathcal{VR}_2(A_Γ)$ is contractible for $A_Γ$ a right-angled Artin group on a triangle-free graph $Γ$. We also prove an interesting sufficient condition for a group to be finitely presented that only requires checking connectivity of certain finite complexes.

items.title: On a Fuzzy Landau Equation: I. A Variational Approach
items.summary: In this paper, we introduce a fuzzy Landau equation, where particles interact through delocalised collisions. We establish a variational characterisation that recasts the fuzzy Landau equation within the framework of GENERIC systems (General Equations for Non-Equilibrium Reversible-Irreversible Coupling), obtaining an equivalent characterisation of H-solutions.

items.title: Shape-Derivative Moment Approximation for a Reduced Time-Harmonic Biot Poroelastic System with Random Interfaces
items.summary: We develop first- and second-moment approximations for a reduced time-harmonic Biot poroelastic interface system with random material interfaces. The model retains mixture inertia, quasi-static Darcy discharge, and explicit storage and coupling coefficients. The interface separates two media, each with constant Lamé parameters and hydraulic mobility. We use shape calculus to analyze random perturbations normal to the interface. We derive the first shape derivative in a total-traction and normal-flux formulation, establish a Taylor expansion on a fixed function space under a non-resonance assumption, and prove error bounds on fixed observation regions. The mean approximation is second-order accurate, and the covariance and variance approximations are third-order accurate. We estimate the variance error directly. Applying pivoted Cholesky compression to the covariance matrix of the coefficients in a fixed basis of smooth interface modes reduces the computation of the leading covariance to deterministic sensitivity solves. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions examine perturbation rates, low-rank truncation, coupled statistics, and computational cost.

items.title: A Cohen--Macaulay Analogue of the Brodmann--Rotthaus Theorem
items.summary: We prove a Cohen--Macaulay analogue of the theorem of Brodmann and Rotthaus on the lifting of quasi-excellence. More precisely, let $A$ be a Noetherian ring and let $I$ be an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$. We show that if $A/I$ is $\mathsf{CM}$-Q0 and $A$ is a $\mathsf{CM}$\textnormal{-G-}ring, then $A$ is $\mathsf{CM}$-quasi-excellent. Our proof follows the strategy of Kurano and Shimomoto and makes essential use of Česnavičius' Macaulayfication theorem.

items.title: The isolation number of uniform hypertrees
items.summary: An isolating set of a hypergraph $H$ is a vertex set whose closed neighbourhood intersects every edge of $H$. The isolation number $ι(H)$ is the minimum cardinality of such a set. Let $r\ge3$, and let $T$ be an $r$-uniform hypergraph whose incidence graph is a tree. We prove that, if $T$ has order $n$ and at least two edges, then $ι(T)\le\lfloor n/(2r-1)\rfloor$. The bound is attained at every admissible order. We characterize all hypertrees attaining it by a construction using six types of marked hypertrees of orders $2r-1$, $3r-2$ and $4r-3$. The proof uses a packing formula for the isolation number and an exact identity for the difference $n-(2r-1)ι(T)$. For connected graphs of order $n$ with at least two blocks, all of which are triangles, we obtain the sharp bound $\lfloor n/5\rfloor$ on the cycle isolation number and characterize the graphs attaining it.

items.title: A Java Math.BigDecimal Implementation of Core Mathematical Functions
items.summary: The mathematical functions log(x), exp(x), root[n]x, sin(x), cos(x), tan(x), arcsin(x), arctan(x), x^y, sinh(x), cosh(x), tanh(x) and Gamma(x) have been implemented for arguments x in the real domain in a native Java library on top of the multi-precision BigDecimal representation of floating point numbers. This supports scientific applications where more than the double precision accuracy of the library of the Standard Edition is desired. The full source code is made available under the LGPL v3.0.

items.title: Convergence of replicator-mutator particle systems via bounded Wasserstein distance
items.summary: Interacting particle systems with selection and mutation mechanisms arise in biological modeling, evolutionary optimization, and particle filtering methods. In this work we will consider the paradigmatic replicator-mutator PDE, which combines a diffusive component with a source term that depends on an external potential. We derive quantitative error estimates for the distance between the empirical measure of an unweighted particle system and the solution of the PDE. The proof uses a Wasserstein-1 distance with a bounded ground cost, which allows us to treat unbounded potentials on an unbounded state space. The key tools are the optimal coupling of newly resampled particles and, for the time-continuous limit, the use of a discrete-time killing resampling.

items.title: Semi-exact functors and the conjecture of Coulembier and Flake
items.summary: We introduce the notion of semi-exact functors between abelian categories, which are characterised by either preserving or breaking exactness of sequences.
