We prove semi-exact functors are always exact with respect to a canonically determined exact structure. For a symmetric tensor category $\Cs$, we define a support theory by considering all $\Bbbk$-linear symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors $\mathscr{C}\to\operatorname{Ver}_{p^\infty}$ up to equivalence, and conjecture that it agrees with the Balmer spectrum of the stable category when $\mathscr{C}$ is finite. We prove a weak form of this conjecture and other results for Tannakian categories and in characteristic 0. Critical to the positive characteristic case is a functor constructed by Coulembier and Flake who were interested in higher Frobenius functors. We show that their construction, which relies on the theory of abelian envelopes, gives a natural source for semi-exact functors, and at least in the Tannakian setting gives all $\Bbbk$-linear, symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors.

items.title: Asymptotic Error of the Euler--Maruyama Scheme for McKean--Vlasov SDEs Driven by $α$-Stable Processes
items.summary: We study the continuous-time Euler--Maruyama error for McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations (SDEs) driven by symmetric $α$-stable noise, $1<α<2$. We assume globally Lipschitz coefficients, a bounded jump coefficient, and bounded Lipschitz state derivatives and law-derivative kernels. The error normalized by $(n/\log n)^{1/α}$ converges jointly with the original driver in the multivariate Skorokhod $J_1$ topology, and hence stably relative to the driver's path. The limit solves a linear SDE driven by the original noise and an independent symmetric $α$-stable process. Conditional centering removes both law-derivative terms from the limiting equation. For $1\leqslant p<α$, the Euler schemes based on the numerical and exact marginal laws differ by $o((\log n/n)^{1/α})$ in the $L^p$ norm of the path supremum. Their normalized errors have the same limiting $p$th moment of the path supremum, which is positive if $σ(x_0,δ_{x_0})\partial_xσ(x_0,δ_{x_0})\ne 0$. For test functions in $C_b^2(\mathbb{R})$, the fixed-time weak error is $o((\log n/n)^{1/α})$.

items.title: Computer-assisted proofs for the fourth algebraic transfer in certain generic degrees
items.summary: This paper restructures the author's earlier article in Journal of Homotopy and Related Structures to correct its erroneous invariant-dimension calculations for the fourth Singer algebraic transfer and is written as a replacement for that article. More precisely, we determine the domain and image of the transfer in the degree families $2^{s+t+1}+2^{s+1}-3$ with $t\ne3$ and $2^{s+t}+2^s-2$ with $t\notin\{2,3,4\}$, where $s,t$ are positive integers. Divided-power spikes are basis elements dual to polynomial monomials whose exponents have the form $2^j-1$ for nonnegative integers $j$. Their translates under ${\rm GL}_4(\mathbb F_2)$, the group of invertible $4\times4$ matrices over the field with two elements, generate submodules of the Steenrod kernel, the subspace annihilated by all positive Steenrod squares. We present these submodules as quotients of sums of permutation modules on complete flags, which are chains in $\mathbb F_2^4$ containing one subspace of each dimension $0,1,2,3,4$. Identifying the relation spaces in these presentations gives explicit equivariant comparison isomorphisms. A recursion obtained by separating even and odd exponents in each variable reduces the comparisons to specified identities of finite-dimensional subspaces. These comparisons apply to both complete degree families, including the parameter values omitted from the transfer theorem. Duplication and partial flag embeddings also give theoretical comparisons in specified parameter ranges. As a consequence, Singer's injectivity conjecture holds in rank four in both degree families under the stated parameter restrictions. The cokernel is one-dimensional in homological degree $256$ and zero in every other degree in those ranges.

items.title: Tropical Geometry of $G_2$
items.summary: We tropicalize the Grassmannian and the flag variety of the algebraic group of type $G_2$. The two tropical varieties are strictly contained in the associated Dressians. Their points are trees in the $G_2$-forest and decorated trees in the $G_2$-orchard. These form hexagons in incidence geometry. We classify all toric degenerations and their Newton-Okounkov polytopes. Mukai theory leads us to tropical canonical curves of genus 10. This article serves as a blueprint for studies of reductive groups in tropical geometry.

items.title: Conditional Mean-Field Type Linear Quadratic Optimal Control Problem for Regime-Switching Diffusions with Indefinite Coefficients
items.summary: We study a conditional mean-field type linear quadratic optimal control problem for regime-switching diffusions with indefinite weights. The dynamics and cost depend on conditional expectations of the state and control given the history of the Markov chain. Under standard definiteness conditions, we establish the existence and uniqueness of the optimal control and derive its feedback representation and optimal cost through two sets of coupled Riccati equations and a linear backward stochastic differential equation driven by the Markov chain. To treat the case of indefinite weights, we extend the equivalent cost functional approach to this setting using regime-dependent quadratic adjustments for the conditional mean of the state and its deviation from that mean. When the transformed weights in the equivalent cost functional satisfy standard definiteness conditions, this construction yields unique solvability of the original Hamiltonian system and a feedback representation of the unique optimal control. The proposed results also provide an effective method for establishing the solvability of fully coupled linear conditional mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equations that do not satisfy certain existing monotonicity conditions. We further apply the results to conditional mean-variance portfolio selection with exogenous liability in an incomplete regime-switching market and derive the optimal investment strategy.

items.title: An Explicit Uniform Connectivity Bound for Generalized Markoff Graphs
items.summary: Let $X_D$ be the surface $x^2+y^2+z^2-xyz=D$ over $\mathbb F_p$. For every prime $p>10^{320}$ and every $D\in\mathbb F_p\setminus\{4\}$, we prove that the three Vieta involutions act transitively on the trace triples of generating pairs of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_p)$. The proof combines an explicit primitive-fiber argument, Chen's orbit-size lower bound, and a weighted maximal-divisor estimate. We also give an explicit descent from Nielsen transitivity to transitivity under the Vieta involutions alone.

items.title: (Non-)existence of complex structures on $2$-step nilpotent Lie algebras
items.summary: In this paper we determine which $8$-dimensional $2$-step nilpotent real Lie algebras admit (integrable) complex structures. We construct explicit examples on $40$ out of the $43$ isomorphism classes, and show that there are obstructions to the existence of complex structures on the remaining three isomorphism classes. These obstructions are related to the set of elements of rank $2$ in the pencil defining the Lie algebra structure. We also show that for any even-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{h}$, the direct sum $\mathfrak{g}:=\mathbb{R}^2\oplus \mathfrak{h}$ (and also some other, more general, extensions of $\mathbb{R}^2$ by $\mathfrak{h}$) admits a complex structure if and only if $\mathfrak{h}$ admits a complex structure. In particular, this allows us to construct the first examples of $2$-step nilpotent Lie algebras in every even dimension $2n\geq8$ which do not admit complex structures. Finally, we show that every even-dimensional $2$-step nilpotent Lie algebra with $2$-dimensional center admits a complex structure.

items.title: Finite-dimensional Hopf algebras generated by the coradical
items.summary: Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra over a field $k$. The paper is concerned with the question of when $H$ is generated by the coradical $H_0$. We give several characterizations of this property, involving the largest Hopf ideal contained in the Jacobson radical $J(H^*)$ and the coefficient coalgebra of the injective hull of the trivial comodule. If the canonical map $H_0\to H/J(H)$ is surjective, then $H$ is generated by $H_0$ if and only if $H=H_0^3+J(H)^2$, where $H_0^3$ is the span of products of three elements of $H_0$. For finite locally free Hopf algebras of constant rank over a $k$-scheme in characteristic zero, including duals of liftings of a given Nichols algebra, the locus where this property holds is Zariski open and compatible with arbitrary base change. For a finite-dimensional pointed Hopf algebra $K$ with abelian coradical over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the largest Hopf ideal contained in $J(K)$ is determined. $K^*$ is generated by its coradical if and only if $J(K)$ contains no nonzero skew-primitive elements. For liftings of quantum linear spaces and standard liftings of finite Cartan type, this condition is expressed in terms of the deformation parameters of $K$.

items.title: Asymptotics of linear normal lambda terms: WKB structure, Airy turning point and a positive recurrence
items.summary: Let a n be the number of closed linear $λ$-terms in $β$-normal form with n variable occurrences. We prove is the large-order constant of the Riccati-Airy sequence K m attached to the turning point of the WKB expansion. We show that the K m are exactly rescaled coefficients of the formal logarithmic derivative of the Airy asymptotic series, and deduce $κ$ $\infty$ = 1/(2$π$) from the explicit Airy coefficients. Hence The proof combines four further ingredients: (i) the WKB coefficients are polynomials with nonnegative coefficients in v = (1 -4w) -1/2 and satisfy an explicit positive recurrence; (ii) the linearisation of the WKB equation has a combinatorial meaning ($λ$-chain terms) and is a translation in the action coordinate s, whose singularity sits at the instanton action A 0 = ln 2 -1 2\,; (iii) an exact identity shows that, after conjugation by the transported WKB prefactor $μ$ = r/(1+r) 2 , the remaining non-linear terms are either negative or of relative size O(m -2 ); (iv) under the conjugated linear dynamics the depth profile is dominated by its top coefficient. A finite bound on an explicit ratio sequence is obtained by exact computer arithmetic (the program is given in an appendix); it also yields a n $\le$ 1.14736 f '' n (1) for all n, with f '' n (1) $\sim$ 5 144 (n -1)!$λ$ n .

items.title: An additive-square-free word over an alphabet of size 6
items.summary: An additive square over $\mathbb{N}$ is two consecutive nonempty blocks of the same length and same sum. For example, 1423 is an additive square, since 14 and 23 both have length 2 and sum 5. Solving a problem that has been open for more than 50 years, we give an example of an infinite word over a 6-letter subset of N that avoids additive squares.

items.title: From Multirelations to Meet-Relations: A Relational Duality for Semilattices with Adjunctions
items.summary: We develop a relational duality for semilattices with adjunctions (SLatas) based on binary meet-relations. First, we introduce the category of MoS-spaces and establish a dual equivalence with modal semilattices. Then, by means of A-relations, we define the category RelSP and prove a dual equivalence between SLata and RelSP. To compare this framework with the multirelational semantics previously developed for SLatas, we introduce the notion of normal mS-space and show that, under this condition, the multirelational structure can be canonically recovered from a meet-relation, and conversely. As a consequence, we prove that the categories RelSP and SLataSp are isomorphic.

items.title: Worst-case bias of the independence assumption for functions of two ordinal variables
items.summary: Let ordinal grades $X$ and $Y$ be obtained by cutting a pair of random variables with copula $C$ at arbitrary thresholds, and let $g$ be a function of the grades. We study the largest error $S_C(g)$, over all thresholds, that is, over all marginal laws, made when the mean of $g(X,Y)$ is computed as if the grades were independent. This is the counterpart of the classical dependence-uncertainty problem: the copula is fixed and the discretisation is free. The error is caused entirely by the interaction of the inputs, measured by an index $ρ(g)$, the largest absolute $g$-volume of a rectangle of grades, which vanishes if and only if $g$ is additive. For every copula, $S_C(g)$ lies between $ρ(g)$ times the largest deviation of $C$ from the independence copula and $ρ(g)$ times half the total variation of their difference, and the factor one half cannot be improved. For the Gaussian copula with correlation $λ$ we prove that $S_C(g)$ equals $|λ|ρ(g)/(2π)$ to first order, with a sharp constant and an explicit remainder. The same first-order law holds for copula families whose first-order departure from independence is a product of unimodal factors, including the Farlie-Gumbel-Morgenstern, Ali-Mikhail-Haq, Frank, Clayton and Plackett families, and we characterise the Archimedean families with this property. An application to the TNM staging of colon cancer, with data from a clinical trial, compares the bounds with the actual error of the independence computation.

items.title: Global well-posedness and decay estimates of strong solutions to a non-conservative compressible two-fluid model in $L^p$ critical framework
items.summary: We investigate the global existence and long-time behavior of solutions to a general multidimensional non-conservative compressible two-fluid model satisfying the algebraic capillary pressure relation \(P^{+}(ρ^+)-P^{-}(ρ^-)=f(α^{-}ρ^{-})\) in the $L^p$ critical framework. Our main contributions are twofold. First, under the sharp stability condition \(-\frac{s_{-}^{2}(1,1)}{α^{-}(1,1)}<f^{\prime}(1)<0,\) we establish the global existence and uniqueness of solutions for small perturbations around a linearly stable constant equilibrium. In particular, our result removes the additional negativity assumption required in Evje--Wang--Wen [Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 221:1285--1316, 2016]. Second, assuming in addition that the low-frequency of the initial perturbation is small in a lower-regularity Besov space, we derive optimal decay rates for the solution.

items.title: Induced matching treewidth in classes with a forbidden structure
items.summary: Induced matching treewidth is a tree-decomposition based parameter where we bound the size of an induced matching whose every edge intersects a single bag of the decomposition. It is known that many computational problems can be solved efficiently in graphs of bounded induced matching treewidth. In this paper we are interested in understanding what classes of graphs have bounded induced matching treewidth. We provide dichotomy theorems for all classes defined by excluding a single graph with respect to six basic containment relations: (induced) subgraph, (induced) topological minor, and (induced) minor. Furthermore, we study the case where the input graph has minimum degree at least 2, as well as the more restrictive case where it is 2-connected. This can be assumed without loss of generality for many computational problems. It turns out that for classes excluding some graph as an induced minor, this restrictions yield some new cases of bounded induced matching treewidth. As a consequence, our results imply new algorithmic results, as well as the existence of balanced separators dominated by a constant number of vertices in the considered classes. This confirms some special cases of two conjectures of Gartland and Lokshtanov.

items.title: Signature Approach for Contextual Bandits with Nonlinear and Path-dependent Rewards: Regret Bound and Statistical Inference
items.summary: We study contextual bandits with nonlinear and path-dependent rewards through a novel signature-transform-based approach. Leveraging the universal nonlinearity property of signatures, we approximate continuous path-dependent reward functionals by linear functionals in the signature space. This representation enables the use of efficient linear contextual bandit methods while preserving expressive sequential structure. Building on this framework, we propose \texttt{DisSigUCB}, a signature-based disjoint upper confidence bound (UCB) algorithm. Under boundedness and non-degeneracy assumptions, we establish a high-probability regret bound of order \(\tilde\mathcal{O}\bigl(d_{\text{Sig}} \sqrt{KT} + \ varepsilon_N T \sqrt{d_\Sig}\bigr)\) with \(K\) being the number of actions, \(d_{\text{Sig}} \) the signature feature dimension, and \(\varepsilon_N\) the finite-depth approximation error. We further introduce $ζ$-\texttt{DisSigUCB}, a randomized variant that ensures persistent exploration for statistical inference. Under additional margin and long-run design conditions, we prove consistency and asymptotic normality of the action-specific ridge estimators. Both the synthetic experiments and the numerical studies on temperature sensor monitoring, sleep-stage classification, and hospital nurse staffing demonstrate the effectiveness of \texttt{DisSigUCB} over linear and kernelized contextual bandit baselines in nonlinear and path-dependent settings.

items.title: The Schoen-Yau-Schick Obstruction in All Dimensions
items.summary: We prove that closed Schoen--Yau--Schick manifolds admit no metric of positive scalar curvature in all dimensions. Building on the singular dimension descent of Bi--Zhu, we extend their topological argument from overtorical manifolds to the Schoen--Yau--Schick setting. The key is to detect a non-spherical two-dimensional homology class by a cohomology class with finite coefficients and preserve the resulting nonzero degree throughout the descent, leading to a contradiction on the terminal surface.

items.title: Short quadratic exponential sums with primes in major arcs
items.summary: Using the second moment of Dirichlet $L$-functions on the critical line over the major arcs ${\mathfrak M}({\mathscr L}^b)$, with $τ=y^3x^{-1}{\mathscr L}^{-b_1}$, and excluding a small neighborhood of the centers of these arcs, i.e., those $α$ satisfying $|α-\frac{a}{q}|>(8πy^2)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{1-\frac{\scriptstyle1}{\scriptstyle{9-4\sqrt{2}}}}{\mathscr L}^{c_2}$, where $c_2=\frac{2A+24+(\sqrt{2}-1)b_1}{2\sqrt{2}-1}$, we obtain the estimate $$ S_2(α;x,y)=\sum_{x-y<n\le x}Λ(n)e(αn^2)\ll y\,{\mathscr L}^{-A}. $$ Moreover, in a small neighborhood of the center of the major arcs, defined by $|α-\frac{a}{q}|\le(8πy^2)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{\frac{\scriptstyle5}{\scriptstyle8}}{\mathscr L}^{1,5A+0,25b+18}$, an asymptotic formula with a remainder term is obtained for $S_2(α;x,y)$, where $A$, $b_1$, and $b$ are arbitrary fixed positive constants, and ${\mathscr L}=\ln xq$.

items.title: Dyson's Tenfold Way, Revisited
items.summary: In this work, we study semilinear representations of groups acting on degree two Galois extensions. Our results include a classification of irreducible semilinear representations, which generalises Dyson's Tenfold Way. Using this, we completely describe the semilinear representation theory of certain groups, such as symmetric groups, and of finite groups over cyclotomic fields. We also prove many results concerning semilinear representations over $\mathbb{C}$, which includes an induction theorem which simultaneously generalises Brauer's Induction Theorem and Serre's Induction Theorem. We are also interested in applications of our classification theorem to crystallography, and include a detailed study of the semilinear representation theory of magnetic wallpaper groups.

items.title: Optimal Stability for Bivariate Weighted Fourth-Order Inequalities
items.summary: In this paper, we prove sharp stability estimates for a two-component radial weighted fourth-order Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg inequality in the two radial regimes for which the scalar optimizers are explicitly known and the corresponding spectral non-degeneracy holds. These regimes are \(4-N<α<2,\ \ell=-α\), and \(2<α<N,\ \ell=4(α-2)(N-2)/(N-α)-α\). Let $N\ge 3$, $p=2(N+\ell)/(N-4+α)>2$, \(μ_1,μ_2\geq0\), \(κ>0\), and $r,s>1$ satisfy $r+s=p$. For radial pairs $(u,v)\in X_{\mathrm{rad}}\times X_{\mathrm{rad}}$, we determine the sharp constant $S_{r,s,μ_1,μ_2,κ}$ in the coupled inequality \[ S_{r,s,μ_1,μ_2,κ} \left(\int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^\ell\big(μ_1|u|^p+μ_2|v|^p+pκ|u|^r|v|^s\big)dx\right)^{2/p} \le \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^α\big(|Δu|^2+|Δv|^2\big)dx . \] The sharp constant is expressed through the scalar sharp constant and the minimum of an explicit one-dimensional ratio function. We also characterize all extremals and prove sharp quantitative stability estimates. The stability exponent is determined by the degeneracy of the ratio minimizers: it is quadratic in the non-degenerate case and becomes square-root type in the degenerate case.

items.title: On a conjecture of Elie Cartan concerning the Gauss equation of a flat submanifold
items.summary: We study exteriorly orthogonal (or flat) symmetric bilinear forms on $\R^n$ with values in $\R^p$, continuing the work initiated by Élie Cartan in 1919 and 1920. In particular, we describe the second fundamental form of an $n$-dimensional flat manifold isometrically immersed in $\E^{n+p}$. Depending on the values of $n$ and $p$, Cartan's results either can be extended to this setting or fail.

items.title: Universal operators on Banach spaces
items.summary: The paper studies universal operators and $n$-tuples of operators on Banach spaces. In the Hilbert-space setting, sufficient criteria for universality, concrete examples, and spectral properties are well established. We investigate extensions of these results to Banach spaces. In particular, we discuss the link between universality and the invariant subspace problem: this leads us to define a stronger notion of universality which is the notion of hereditarily universal operators. We give sufficient conditions for an operator to be hereditarily universal and provide some examples. We also study $n$-tuples of operators by generalizing Vladimir Müller's results to the Banach setting. Finally, we obtain a result on the essential spectrum of a universal $n$-tuple of operators on $\ell_p$.

items.title: On vacuum static foliations
items.summary: We study the compact vacuum static foliation, a Riemannian foliation which generalizes the compact vacuum static space. In particular, we investigate the relations between the tautness of a compact vacuum static foliation and the bound of transverse curvatures.

items.title: Multiplicity criteria for the absolutely continuous spectrum of finite hopping Hermitian operators
items.summary: We consider locally finite-hopping Hermitian operators that admit radial-type transfer matrix sets in the sense of Sadel. We extend his spectral averaging formula from scalar spectral measures to matrix-valued spectral measures associated to a root matrix. This extension yields criteria for lower bounds on the multiplicity of absolutely continuous spectrum. As applications, we consider random decaying shell-matrix potentials on stair-like graphs with increasing-width wires and operators on the Bethe lattice. In both cases, we establish that absolutely continuous spectrum has almost surely infinite multiplicity.

items.title: On the self-extensions of the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence over $\mathbb{Q}_p$
items.summary: Let $p\ge5$ and $D$ be the unique nonsplit quaternion algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We compute, in the category of smooth representations with a fixed central character, the self-extension groups of the $D^{\times}$-representations occurring in the mod $p$ Jacquet-Langlands correspondence in the generic case. The main ingredient is a new weighted filtration on the relevant ring and module. The associated graded module preserves the first nontrivial extension relation, which is not detected by the $\mathfrak{m}_D$-adic filtration.

items.title: Nonparametric Regression on Fixed-Cardinality Subsets:Minimax Risk and Random-Design Effects
items.summary: We study regression from noisy evaluations of uniformly sampled subsets containing exactly \(k\) items from a ground set of size \(d\), a setting motivated by combination screening. The fixed-cardinality constraint couples membership coordinates and prevents a direct use of product-domain notions of interaction and smoothness. Using the harmonic decomposition of the Johnson graph, we define an intrinsic Johnson--Sobolev scale and determine the exact dimensions of low-order interaction spaces. We establish finite-sample risk bounds for harmonic projection and a nonasymptotic minimax characterization when the Sobolev energy budget is bounded relative to the noise variance proxy. We also study sparsity when responses depend on few items, quantifying the reduced interaction dimension and the effects of unknown support and rare configurations. When the empirical Gram matrix is well conditioned, stable least squares removes the design fluctuation of the component already in the fitted space. A rank-deficiency analysis identifies the components left unresolved by random sampling. Combined with a centered completion estimator, it yields minimax bounds matching up to constants whenever \(\min(k,d-k)\) and the smoothness order are fixed, without restricting the signal-to-noise ratio. Numerical experiments distinguish observation noise, design fluctuation, and incomplete coverage; NCI-ALMANAC drug-pair scores provide a real-data illustration.

items.title: A Counterexample to Voiculescu's Normal Dilation Conjecture
items.summary: We construct a compact operator $T$ with trace class self-commutator and vanishing Helton-Howe measure such that $T\oplus S-M\notin \mathcal{S}_2$ for every bounded operator $S$ and every bounded normal operator $M$. This gives counterexamples to Voiculescu's normal dilation and stable classification conjectures. The construction uses magnetic shifts on finite square tori. Their real parts have commutators of uniformly bounded trace norm, while their frame errors admit logarithmic lower bounds in the lattice size. A summability criterion for frame error turns these finite-dimensional estimates into a compact counterexample. The same operator inequalities yield a rank profile invariant under Hilbert-Schmidt perturbations and normal stabilization, which distinguishes the example from zero.

items.title: Global nonsolvability of the leafwise $\dbar$-equation on foliations with Stein leaves
items.summary: Motivated by our previous work on $q$-convexity and global solvability for Levi flat structures, we study the complex foliation associated with the non-tame family of Stein structures constructed by Forstneri\v c and Sigurðardóttir. Although every leaf is closed and biholomorphic to $\C^2$ and the foliation admits a complete bundle-like Riemannian metric, there exists a smooth leafwise $\dbar$-closed $(0,1)$-form for which the leafwise $\dbar$-equation admits no global $L^r_{\loc}$ solution for any $0<r\le\infty$. This result also suggests a modification of Questions~2.10.4--2.10.6 in \emph{Foliations: Dynamics, Geometry and Topology}.

items.title: Soft g-frames in soft Hilbert spaces
items.summary: In this paper, we introduce and analyze soft $g$-frames in soft Hilbert spaces, extending generalized frame theory to parameterized uncertainty models. We establish the completeness of the direct sum of soft Hilbert spaces and prove that the associated soft pre-$g$-frame operator $T_Λ$ is well-defined and bounded with unconditionally convergent series representations. Furthermore, we show that the soft $g$-frame operator $S_Λ$ is a bounded, self-adjoint, and strictly positive element of the unital soft Banach algebra $\mathcal{B}(\tilde{\mathcal{U}})$, and we prove its invertibility via the soft Neumann series and derive two-sided operator bounds for its inverse. We characterize the canonical dual soft $g$-frame, establish the unconditional soft $g$-frame decomposition theorem, and construct induced pairs of dual soft frames from dual soft $g$-frames. Finally, an analytical example with parameter-dependent metrics illustrates the matrix representations, verifies the optimality of the frame bounds via Rayleigh quotients, and confirms the reconstruction formula.

items.title: Phase factors and optimal seminorms for polynomial averages of commuting transformations
items.summary: For invertible commuting measure-preserving transformations $T_1, \ldots, T_\ell$ on a standard probability space, we study polynomial averages along both integers and primes. We provide a rank-based criterion ensuring that, even when the polynomials are linearly dependent, finite-order phase factors are characteristic factors. For polynomials with integer coefficients and zero constant terms, it suffices that the dimension of the space spanned (over $\mathbb{Q}$) by any nonempty subfamily of $k$ polynomials exceeds $k/2$. These phase factors are generated by polynomial phases associated with positive integer powers of the individual transformations and may be strictly smaller than the corresponding Host-Kra factors of the same order. The required order depends only on the number of polynomials and their maximum degree. A four-term example involving a totally ergodic Heisenberg nilsystem shows that this criterion may fail if the equality $k/2$ is permitted. For a family of three polynomials, this criterion is equivalent to the condition that the polynomials are pairwise linearly independent. Consequently, it applies to the family $t, t^2, t^2+t$, where the third polynomial is the sum of the first two. For this specific family, we prove that the optimal orders for the phase factors and the Host-Kra factors are $4, 2, 2$, respectively--a result that holds for both integers and primes. The corresponding optimal seminorms are $U^5(T_1)$, $U^3(T_2)$, and $U^3(T_3)$, which provides an answer to a question posed by Kuca.

items.title: $k-$Absorbing factorization in multiplicative lattices
items.summary: We study the multiplicative $C-$lattices generated by principal elements in which every proper element is a finite product of $k-$absorbing elements. We prove that such lattices have Krull dimension at most one. In the modular case, a finite direct product decomposition theorem is obtained.

items.title: Rademacher and Enflo types in Banach spaces: sharp comparison and orthogonality
items.summary: For every \(1<p\le2\), we prove that the optimal universal factor relating the Enflo type \(p\) constant to the Rademacher type \(p\) constant is \(p\), already among finite-dimensional real or complex Banach spaces. Ivanisvili, van Handel, and Volberg [Ann.\ of Math.\ (2) \textbf{192} (2020), 665--678] proved the equivalence with factor \(π/\sqrt{2}\). Areshidze [arXiv:2609.32666v1 (2026)] improved the upper bound to \(p\). Our matching lower bound settles the optimality question posed in that preprint. We also obtain two results for a real Banach space \(X\). \begin{list}{}{\setlength{\leftmargin}{\dimexpr24pt+1.8em\relax}\setlength{\rightmargin}{24pt}\setlength{\labelwidth}{1.4em}\setlength{\labelsep}{0.4em}\setlength{\topsep}{2pt}\setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}} \item[(a)] For \(1<p<2\), \(X\) has Enflo type \(p\) if and only if the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality holds uniformly over ordered families \((v_i)\) satisfying \[ v_i\perp_B v_j \qquad \text{for all } i<j, \] where \(\perp_B\) denotes Birkhoff--James orthogonality (that is, \(\|v_i+t v_j\|\ge\|v_i\|\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\)). \item[(b)] For \(1<p\le2\), uniform validity of the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality on pairwise isosceles orthogonal families implies that \(X\) has Enflo type \(2p/(p+1)\). \end{list} These results show how Birkhoff--James and isosceles orthogonality reduce the linear estimates needed to establish a metric type property of the whole space.

items.title: Every group is the automorphism group of a set-theoretic solution of the Yang-Baxter equation
items.summary: We give an affirmative answer to the abstract group problem for the category $\YB$ of all set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter (YB) equation: every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a YB-solution, which can be chosen on a finite set if the group is finite. In the terminology of László Babai, this means that the category $\YB$ is universal and finitely universal, which is an analogue of Frucht's classical theorem for graphs. Furthermore, the YB-solutions can be chosen within three very small classes: the solutions of the Frobenius-Separability equation, the solutions of the Baaj--Long--Skandalis equation and the recently introduced bipartite solutions. The proof is based on new constructions which associate to any graph a YB-solution in each of these classes, with the same automorphism group as the graph. Explicit YB-solutions with automorphism groups $C_n$, $S_n$, $D_n$ and $Q_8$ are given, as well as a unitary YB-solution, constructed directly from a field $K$, whose automorphism group is ${\rm Aut} (K)$.

items.title: Energy decay and asymptotic profile for a system of damped wave equations
items.summary: We consider a system of two wave or Klein-Gordon equations on the Euclidean space. One is damped, while the second is only indirectly damped via a coupling term. We are interested in the large time behavior of the solutions. More precisely, we prove energy decay for both components and, when possible, we give their asymptotic profiles. Our proofs are based on spectral analysis. We will see that in our setting the contribution of high frequencies always decays exponentially, so the results depend on the contribution of low frequencies. We observe a diffusive phenomenon as for a single wave equation, but the coupling between the two components gives completely different behaviors, depending on the nature of the equations and the strengths of the damping and coupling.

items.title: Martingale Transforms and Subsequence Estimates in Noncommutative \(L_p\)-Spaces
items.summary: We establish a transference principle from martingale transform inequalities to subsequence estimates for weakly null sequences. As applications, for every von Neumann algebra $\M$, (1) we show that, every bounded sequence in the Haagerup space $L_1(\M)=\M_*$ has either a norm-convergent subsequence or a $2$-co-lacunary subsequence, answering an open problem of Parcet and Randrianantoanina; (2) we prove that every UMD Banach space has the uniform USP, which in particular yields uniform USP for $L_p(\M)$, $1<p<\infty$, answering a question posed by Oikhberg and Spinu; (3) we answer an open problem of Haagerup, Rosenthal and Sukochev for the upper $\ell_p$ estimates for $L_p(\M)$, $1<p<2$, in the affirmative; (4) we also answer the problem of whether every $2$-strictly singular operator on a noncommutative $L_1$-space is automatically Dunford--Pettis.

items.title: On models of affine arithmetic
items.summary: By affine arithmetic is meant the set of affine consequences of Peano arithmetic. This is a continuous theory which is studied in the framework of affine logic, a sublogic of continuous logic. Affine arithmetic is undecidable. Also, its models are generally lattice ordered and carry a nontrivial metric. Classical models are then characterized as those which are linearly ordered. In this paper, the affine variants of several classical results in Peano arithmetic are proved. In particular, an affine form of Gaifman's splitting theorem is proved.

items.title: Cellular Algebra of A2 webs
items.summary: We introduce a diagram algebra $\mathcal{K}_L$ based on Kuperberg's $A_2$-webs and prove a Schur--Weyl duality $\mathcal{K}_L \cong \operatorname{End}_{U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)}((V^+ \oplus V^-)^{\otimes L})$, where $V^\pm$ are the fundamental representations of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$. By self-duality of $V^+\oplus V^-$, $\mathcal{K}_L$ is a natural $A_2$ analogue of the Temperley--Lieb algebra. We construct an explicit cellular structure for $\mathcal{K}_L$, with the web basis as its cellular basis and cell modules indexed by dominant $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$-weights. The bases of these modules are parametrized by dominant lattice paths via a recursive growth algorithm. Using this structure, we determine local generators of $\mathcal{K}_L$ and establish web formulations of the first and second fundamental theorems of invariant theory. In particular, we show that the braid-group image, augmented by local idempotents, does not generate $\mathcal{K}_L$, and identify an additional local generator. Finally, we derive a bimodule decomposition of $(V^+ \oplus V^-)^{\otimes L}$, yielding a complete set of irreducible $\mathcal{K}_L$-modules for formal or generic $q$.

items.title: Lelong Numbers Above an Arbitrary Bound and Plane Curves
items.summary: Let $T$ be a positive closed current of bidimension $(1,1)$ with unit mass on $\mathbb P^2$ and $E^+_α(T)$ be the upper level sets of Lelong numbers $ν(T,x)$ of $T$. For any $α\geq \frac{3}{d+5}$, $d\in \mathbb Z^+$ we show that $|E^+_α(T)\setminus C|\leq 2$ for a curve $C$ of degree $d$. As a corollary of this result, we obtain a quantative lower bound for the integrability exponent at any point away from the curve $C$ and a two point set $P$.

items.title: Logarithmic Stability for an Inverse Source Problem in a Coupled Nonlinear Helmholtz System
items.summary: We consider an inverse source problem for a coupled nonlinear Helmholtz system motivated by second-harmonic generation. For a known susceptibility bounded away from zero, we prove that small real-valued sources are uniquely determined by the full first Fréchet derivative of the nonlinear Dirichlet-to-Neumann map at a fixed small real boundary value. Under an a priori Sobolev bound, we derive a conditional logarithmic stability estimate. The proof uses linearization, complex geometric optics solutions for a matrix Schrödinger equation, and interpolation.

items.title: The effect of policy cancellation on the risk of an insurance portfolio
items.summary: For an insurance portfolio modelled by a large number of i.i.d. losses, the average loss converges to its expected value by the law of large numbers, reflecting the diversification effect of pooling risks. Policy cancellations reduce the portfolio size and thereby weaken this effect. We quantify the resulting increase in risk by applying risk measures to the average loss before and after the cancellation of policies. For a portfolio of size $n$, we show that the impact of cancelling a single contract is of order $n^{-3/2}$, while the cancellation of a fixed proportion of contracts has an effect of order $n^{-1/2}$. We further extend the proportional cancellation regime to heterogeneous portfolios with different cancellation rates and risk characteristics across segments. These asymptotic results provide a quantitative basis for assessing surrender fees and cancellation costs from the insurer's perspective. We complement the theoretical analysis with numerical results for representative life insurance products, illustrating the magnitude of cancellation costs and the effect of portfolio aggregation. The two regimes require different techniques. For the cancellation of a fixed proportion of contracts, we employ central limit theorems in Wasserstein distance. For the cancellation of a single contract, we combine Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality with higher-order distributional approximations based on the Edgeworth and Cornish-Fisher expansions.

items.title: Generic vanishing and singularities of theta divisors
items.summary: We study the connection between the generic vanishing conjecture for subvarieties of principally polarized abelian varieties and various predictions about the singularities of theta divisors. We deduce new cases of a conjecture on the multiplicities of points on irreducible theta divisors, as well as Beauville's conjecture characterizing Jacobians by the size of their theta singularity loci.

items.title: A remark on the AI proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
items.summary: We give a geometric interpretation of the projection and reconstruction underlying the Open AI's characteristic-two proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture. Using the double covering and filling a puncture, we construct a morphism on normalized level-two associators with an explicit inverse on its image. We compute the restricted tangent reconstruction in the pro-2 realization and identify the leading coefficient maps with those of the OpenAI proof, making its implicit reconstruction explicit.

items.title: Isometrically greedy renormings of bidemocratic unconditional bases of Banach spaces
items.summary: We show that if a greedy basis of a Banach space has the additional property that its dual basis is also greedy, then the space admits an equivalent norm under which the basis is isometrically greedy. This solves in the positive a question posed by Dilworth, Kutzarova, Odell, Schlumprecht and Zsák in 2014. As an application, we resolve a long-standing problem explicitly posed by Albiac, Ansorena and Wallis in 2017 by proving that any subsymmetric basis of a Banach space is isometrically greedy under a suitable renorming of the ambient space.

items.title: Isometric classification of the $L^{p}$-spaces of infinite dimensional Lebesgue measure
items.summary: We investigate the isometric structure of $L^{p}$-spaces for the infinite-dimensional Lebesgue measure $(\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}},μ)$. Under the continuum hypothesis (CH) we prove $L^{p}(μ)\cong \ell^{p}(\mathfrak{c},L^{p}[0,1])$, where $\mathfrak{c}$ denotes the cardinality of the continuum, and without CH we obtain an isometric, complemented copy of $\ell^{p}(\mathfrak{c},L^{p}[0,1])$ inside $L^{p}(μ)$. In a general framework, we characterize precisely when $L^{p}(ν)\cong \ell^{p}(κ,L^{p}[0,1])$ and classify all such isometries.

items.title: Sharp Sobolev thresholds and rapid rotation for Navier--Stokes equations with fractional horizontal dissipation
items.summary: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with fractional horizontal dissipation $νΛ_h^{2α}$, $0<α\le1$, and a Coriolis force. There is no vertical dissipation. The scaling-critical Sobolev index is $s_c=5/2-2α$. For $0<α<1$, we prove local Hadamard well-posedness in $H^s$ for $s\ge s_c$; for $α=1$, the range is $s>1/2$. At every prescribed finite rotation rate, norm inflation holds in all remaining positive-order Sobolev spaces for classical solutions with smooth compactly supported divergence-free initial data, starting from arbitrarily small $H^s$ data in arbitrarily short time. Thus $H^{s_c}$ is a well-posedness space for $0<α<1$, whereas $H^{1/2}$ exhibits norm inflation for $α=1$. These results give sharp Sobolev thresholds for each finite rotation rate. Throughout the well-posedness range, small data yield global solutions with a rotation-independent smallness threshold, and every fixed datum yields a global solution for sufficiently rapid rotation. The nonlinear solution converges to the linear Stokes--Coriolis evolution uniformly on $[0,\infty)$ and in the global dissipation norm as $|Ω|\to\infty$. For spectrally localized data separated from the vertical frequency axis, the convergence rate is $O(|Ω|^{-γ})$ for every $0<γ<1/2$. For $0<α<1$, the energy estimates close at $s=s_c$ without loss of derivatives in isotropic Sobolev spaces, using Littlewood--Paley decomposition, Sobolev trace inequalities, and localized horizontal product estimates. Below $s_c$, norm inflation follows from an approximation by a fixed smooth Euler solution after rescaling. At $(α,s)=(1,1/2)$, viscosity remains fixed under critical rescaling; the construction instead uses a localized scalar shear and conormal analytic stability estimates uniform in the vertical concentration parameters.

items.title: Stable admissible neural classes and convergent physics-informed neural networks
items.summary: Residual-based methods, including physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), physics-informed Kolmogorov--Arnold networks, and some physics-informed neural operator architectures, approximate PDE solutions by minimizing a discrete least-squares loss formed from the PDE and boundary residuals over a prescribed trial class. This structure is shared by classical least-squares Kansa collocation, whose kernel trial spaces admit an established convergence theory. For neural trial classes, approximation power alone does not ensure that discrete residuals control the continuous solution error. For linear elliptic Dirichlet problems, we extend the kernel-based collocation framework to neural trial classes through elliptic regularity, discrete stability, and consistency. Elliptic regularity supplies the PDE estimate relating solution error to continuous residuals. Discrete stability identifies admissible trial subclasses in which continuous residuals are controlled by a computable discrete loss. This step also quantifies the required number of collocation points. Furthermore, the stability analysis naturally demands a scale-dependent, physics-balanced boundary weight. For the constrained problem, consistency requires accurate comparison functions within the same admissible subclass, a requirement not supplied by neural approximation estimates alone. Specializing to multilayer perceptrons with tanh activations (tanh-MLPs), we construct admissible comparison networks and establish convergence for the constrained residual minimization problem. We further obtain conditional convergence of unconstrained physics-balanced PINNs based on tanh-MLPs under joint network and sampling refinement.

items.title: Topological aspects of generalized Sklyanin algebras
items.summary: We are concerned with the topology of Casimir foliations of Sklyanin algebras and their certain generalizations. In particular, we give a complete description of the topological types and bifurcations of Casimir leaves of the original Sklyanin algebras, which improves and extends analogous results from the original papers of E. Sklyanin. Our approach is based on the so-called signature formula for the Euler characteristic of real algebraic varieties. Moreover, we show that the same approach yields similar results for certain generalizations of the original Sklyanin algebras known as Jacobian Poisson structures. Keywords: Poisson structure, Sklyanin algebra, Casimir function, Casimir foliation, Nambu bracket, Jacobian Poisson structure, Euler characteristic, algebraic formula for the Euler characteristic, bifurcation diagram, isolated singularity of complete intersection, Milnor number

items.title: Complete monotonicity of Laplace transform ratios: Density criteria for self-decomposability and additive decomposition
items.summary: We prove a complete monotonicity (CM) theorem for ratios of Laplace transforms: if the denominator function is logarithmically convex and the quotient of the two functions is monotone, then the corresponding quotient of Laplace transforms (or, in the opposite monotonicity case, its derivative) is CM. As probabilistic consequences, we obtain density-level criteria for self-decomposability (SD) and additive decomposition (AD) of positive distributions, together with a short proof of the classical Steutel theorem concerning infinite divisibility (ID). These criteria reduce problems typically tackled via special function quotients or Lévy measures to elementary checks on the underlying densities. The main application is to the beta prime distribution and Tricomi's confluent hypergeometric function. In the log-convex range $a\le1$, we prove new cross-parameter additive decompositions and self-convolution additive factorizations for beta prime laws. Equivalently, we establish the complete monotonicity of several quotients of Tricomi functions, providing partial affirmative solutions to a problem of Ismail and Kelker (SIAM J. Math. Anal., 1979) and to two conjectures of Ferreira and Simon (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 2023). We also obtain additive factorizations for generalized inverse Gaussian (GIG) laws, expressed as complete monotonicity of ratios of modified Bessel functions. Further examples, including Whittaker-type and logarithmic beta families, illustrate the scope and limitations of the method.

items.title: On Word Representations and Embeddings in Complex Matrices
items.summary: Embeddings of word structures into matrix semigroups provide a natural bridge between combinatorics on words and linear algebra. However, low-dimensional matrix semigroups impose strong structural restrictions on possible embeddings. Certain finitely generated groups admit faithful representations in SL(2, C) and other similar matrix groups. On the other hand, it is known that the product of two free semigroups on two generators cannot be embedded into the 2x2 complex matrices. In this paper we study embeddings of word structures into low-dimensional matrix semigroups over the complex numbers and develop new techniques for constructing word representations of the Euclidean Bianchi groups. These representations provide a symbolic framework and a natural first step towards analysing fundamental decision problems in 2x2 matrix semigroups.

items.title: A description of the space with no separable quotient presented by OpenAI
items.summary: OpenAI recently presented a remarkable solution to the longstanding separable quotient problem in Banach space theory. The result establishes its independence from ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC with a measurable cardinal. Under the continuum hypothesis, the paper constructs a nonseparable Banach space $X$ with no separable infinite-dimensional quotient. The present paper offers an alternative exposition of the mechanism leading to $X$ and its properties. Our aim is to make the methods and results more accessible and to offer a clearer understanding of this exotic space.

items.title: Intersections of Odd Polygons Revisited
items.summary: It is shown that the maximum number of intersection points between the boundaries of a simple $m$-gon and a simple $n$-gon is $mn-(m+n)+3$ for any odd integers $m,n \ge 3$. The previous best upper bound was $mn-(m+n)+C$, for some huge constant $C$.

items.title: Sharp integral condition for linear growth of greedy lattice animals
items.summary: We show that the necessary and sufficient condition for linear growth of greedy lattice animals with nonnegative i.i.d. vertex weights in every dimension $q\ge2$ is the same criterion for linear growth of directed last-passage times. We also obtain two-sided finite-size estimates, up to dimension-dependent constants, for the mean maximal weights of directed paths, lattice animals, valid for every nonnegative weights. These estimates determine the order of mean growth even when growth is superlinear. Since every up-right path from the origin is a lattice animal, the lower bound follows from the corresponding last-passage bound. For the upper bound, we couple the lattice weights to a Poisson process and represent each animal by a polygonal route of length proportional to its size.

items.title: On the Critical Exponent for a Time--Space Fractional Reaction--Diffusion Equation with a Slowly Varying Time-Dependent Source
items.summary: We study the Fujita critical exponent for the Cauchy problem $\partial_t^αu+(-Δ)^{θ/2}u=h(t)u^p$ in $(0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^N$, $u(0)=u_0\ge0$, where $α\in(0,1]$, $θ\in(0,2]$, $p>1$, $\partial_t^α$ is the Caputo derivative, and $h(t)\sim t^γ\ell(t)$ for large $t$, with $γ\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\ell$ slowly varying at infinity in the sense of Karamata. For $α=1$ and every $θ\in(0,2]$ we obtain a complete classification. If $γ\le-1$, small data give global solutions for every $p>1$, so there is no Fujita threshold. If $γ>-1$, the critical exponent is $p_c(γ)=1+θ(γ+1)/N$: every nontrivial solution blows up for $1<p<p_c(γ)$, while small global solutions exist for $p>p_c(γ)$. At $p=p_c(γ)$ the slowly varying factor decides: blow-up occurs if $\int_1^\infty t^{-1}\ell(t)dt=\infty$, and small global solutions exist if this integral converges. Hence global existence may occur at the critical exponent, unlike the autonomous case. For $α\in(0,1)$, the memory of the Caputo derivative replaces $γ+1$ by $γ+α$. We prove small-data global existence for every $p>1$ when $γ\le-α$. When $γ>-α$, all nontrivial solutions blow up for $1<p<p_c(γ,α):=1+θ(γ+α)/(Nα)$. If $N<θ$, we also obtain global existence for $p>p_c(γ,α)$, so the classification is complete, and at $p=p_c(γ,α)$ the dichotomy is governed by the boundedness of $\ell$. If $N\geθ$, we obtain global existence for $p>1+(γ+α)/α$, which coincides with $p_c(γ,α)$ when $N=θ$. Finally, a second, purely local blow-up mechanism shows that for $N>θ$ and $γ>αθ/(N-θ)$, $p_c(γ,α)$ is not the Fujita exponent. Our results extend the theorems of Meier (1990) to the nonlocal setting.

items.title: Global existence for the 1D compressible Euler equations with time-decaying damping and spatial perturbations
items.summary: We study the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations with damping coefficient $b(t)+a(x)$, where $b(t)=λ(1+t)^{-μ}$ with $0<μ<1$, $λ>0$, or $μ=1$, $λ>2$, and $a\in C_b^1(\mathbb R)\cap L^1(\mathbb R)$ is nonnegative. We prove global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions for sufficiently small $C_b^1$ perturbations of a constant state, without assuming spatial decay or convergence of the initial data at infinity. No smallness condition is imposed on the spatially dependent damping coefficient, even though its contribution persists for all time. We also obtain decay estimates of order $\varepsilon(1+t)^{-μ}$ for the derivatives $u_t$, $v_t$, and $v_x$, together with a pointwise estimate for $u_x$ involving the spatial coefficient $a(x)$. The main ingredient is a time-uniform $L^\infty$ estimate for an inhomogeneous coupled transport system with a non-small spatial coefficient. Combined with suitable transformations of the Riemann-invariant derivatives, this estimate allows us to control the nonlinear terms and establish global $C^1$ bounds.

items.title: Critical Gaussian Asymptotics for Directional Superoscillations: STFT and Gabor Consequences
items.summary: We study directional Aharonov--Berry superoscillations in $\R^d$ with widening anisotropic Gaussian envelopes. We prove that the rescaled total $L^2$ mass has a sharp transition governed by the matrix $D=Q-(a^2-1)vv^T$. At criticality, $D$ has a one-dimensional kernel, and the mass obeys an exact $N^{d/2+1/4}$ law with an explicit Gamma-function constant. After anisotropic rescaling, the intensity converges globally in $L^1$ to a transverse Gaussian times a longitudinal quartic exponential. Moyal's identity gives the corresponding total STFT-energy law, but does not imply a local phase-space concentration theorem. We compare these global statements with the earlier quartic critical-window analysis of Berry and Shukla for periodic superoscillations. Supporting results include quantitative fixed-Gaussian STFT expansions, entire-growth convergence with a critical-step obstruction, and conditional Gabor-frame and dual-window expansions. Weighted STFT estimates for polynomial electric-field evolution are obtained as applications. No claim of priority is made for quartic criticality, qualitative STFT supershift preservation, or polynomial electric-field persistence as such.

items.title: A Batched Discrepancy Principle for Stochastic Landweber-Kaczmarz Iteration and its Application to EIT
items.summary: We consider an inverse problem given as ill-posed system of possibly nonlinear operator equations between Hilbert spaces. To solve the problem we use a stochastic mini-batch Landweber-Kaczmarz method, drawing uniformly a subset of equations in each step. As an a posteriori stopping rule, we introduce a batched version of the discrepancy principle, in which only the residual of the selected batches is monitored. Under the tangential cone condition, we establish the convergence of the iterates for exact data, the convergence of the regularized iterates for noisy data under an a priori choice of the stopping index, and the convergence of the method when it is terminated by the proposed batched discrepancy principle. Numerical experiments for the electrical impedance tomography problem illustrate the theoretical results and demonstrate the performance of the method for different batch sizes.

items.title: Global stability and nonlinear asymptotics for the three-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system with horizontal shear viscosity
items.summary: We study the three-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system with horizontal shear viscosity, a positive coefficient $λ+μ>0$ in the divergence term, and full heat conduction. Horizontal viscosity does not dissipate vertical shear derivatives, while thermal diffusion is coupled to the compressible variables. For small $H^2$ perturbations of a constant equilibrium, we construct global strong solutions. Additional spatial localization yields anisotropic decay through second order, convergence of the full $H^2$ norm, and horizontal Gaussian profiles determined by an effective velocity datum. The third-order behavior contains nonlinear contributions: horizontal viscous heating generates a differentiated Newton potential in temperature, while compressible transport slows the decay of the potential velocity. We prove the corresponding bounds with exponents $17/8$ and $2$; for each exponent, we construct a fixed datum in the corresponding class for which every larger exponent fails. For each fixed initial datum, however, the corresponding time-weighted norms tend to zero as $t\to\infty$. Smallness of the first vertical derivative of the initial velocity in the horizontal mixed norm improves the vertical decay estimates and restores the linear third-order temperature rate. Both the existence and decay results require only $H^2$ Sobolev regularity of the initial data.

items.title: Structure-Preserving Neural Approximation of Convex, Semiconvex, and Quasiconvex Functions
items.summary: Input convex neural networks provide a natural way to enforce convexity globally through architectural constraints. We study how this structure-preserving approximation framework extends to semiconvex, quasiconvex, and convex transformable functions. For $C^{1,1}$ convex functions on compact convex domains, we establish the sharp $W^{1,p}$ minimax rate $m^{-1/d}$ under max-affine approximation with $m$ affine pieces, and show that every max-affine function admits an exact bounded-width ICNN representation with complexity linear in $m$. The same $W^{1,p}$ approximation rate extends to semiconvex functions through quadratic lifting and to convex transformable functions through monotone composition. For general Lipschitz quasiconvex functions, we develop a quantitative finite-probe approximation theory based on monotone responses to affine projections and obtain a structure-preserving IqCNN with an $L^\infty$ approximation guarantee. We further show that these approximation results extend to ReLU-transferable smooth activations, including Softplus and ELU. Numerical experiments on PDE-based approximation problems compare the proposed architectures with parameter-matched MLPs and validation-tuned shape penalties, demonstrating global structural validity without penalty tuning while maintaining competitive approximation accuracy. Overall, the results identify recoverable convex latent structure as the key mechanism enabling gradient-level structure-preserving approximation beyond convexity.

items.title: A new upwind DG scheme for a Cahn-Hilliard-Darcy model of tumor growth
items.summary: In this work, we develop a new numerical scheme for a Cahn-Hilliard-Darcy model that describes tumor growth in a fluid-saturated porous medium. First, we derive a physically consistent model from the general framework proposed in [35] that guarantees mass conservation and pointwise bounds on the phase-field and nutrient variables, with a decreasing energy law. The resulting model couples the evolution of tumor cells via a Cahn-Hilliard equation with a diffusion equation for the nutrients through chemotactic interactions and extends the model in [1] by introducing the effect of a surrounding fluid described by Darcy's law. Subsequently, we propose a fully discrete scheme that combines an upwind discontinuous Galerkin method in space and a convex splitting strategy in time, which inherits the fundamental properties of the continuous model: mass conservation, pointwise bounds and a discrete energy law that mimics the one of the continuous model up to some residual terms. Our theoretical analysis is accompanied by numerical experiments that demonstrate the robustness of the proposed scheme and show the influence of the surrounding fluid on the tumor evolution.

items.title: Power projections, Gram structures, and finite-field lifting of Butson Hadamard matrices
items.summary: In this paper we investigate the algebraic properties of Hadamard powers of Butson Hadamard matrices $H\in \mathrm{BH}(n,3p)$, and show that for certain parameter values the cube root projection matrix $H^{\circ p}$ has the same structure as the adjacency matrix of a strongly regular graph. Then, by using a simple eigenvalue analysis we show, among other results, the nonexistence of $\mathrm{BH}(17,15)$ matrices. For other parameter values, a more in-depth study and in particular, a complete classification of all possible projection matrices is necessary. We carry out this task for the case of $\mathrm{BH}(16,15)$ matrices, and using finite field techniques we show that none of these projections can be lifted up to form a Butson matrix. In particular, we show the nonexistence of $\mathrm{BH}(16,15)$ matrices for the first time.

items.title: The shape function of last passage percolation up to constants
items.summary: We determine the diagonal shape function of lattice last passage percolation up to dimension-dependent constants and characterize its finiteness by a tail integral. The proof transfers estimates from an entropy-controlled Poisson model whose quadratic penalty makes the curvature dependence explicit. For critical tails of exponent $q$ in dimension $q\geq 2$, the mean passage time has order $n(\log n)^{(q+1)/(2q)}$, proving sharpness of the logarithmic exponent in the lower bound of Ganguly, Ginsburg and Nam.

items.title: Homeomorphic Sobolev Extensions to Jordan Domains and the inner distance
items.summary: Given a Jordan domain $Ω$, we characterize the situation where a given parametrization (or all parametrizations) $\varphi:\partial\mathbb D\to\partialΩ$ has (have) a homeomorphic $W^{1,1}$-extension $f_{\varphi}:\overline{\mathbb D}\to\overlineΩ$.

items.title: Finding four vertices of a square of area $n$ in a grid by geometric construction
items.summary: In this study, we consider geometric construction in an infinite square grid. Our purpose is to find efficient methods for constructing a square of area $n\in\mathbb{N}$ based on arithmetic properties of the sum of squares. As a consequence, for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, we derive the optimal number of construction steps required to determine the four vertices of the square. Furthermore, we classify all positive integers into three classes according to these optimal numbers.

items.title: Free Boundary Propagation of a Thin-Film Equation with Nonlinear Diffusion: Scale-Consistent Methods for Optimal Results
items.summary: We investigate the free boundary propagation of a non-linear degenerate parabolic problem with both fourth and second order non-linearities, which may be used to model viscous thin-film flow in the regime of weak slippage with an additional contributions from a singular disjoining pressure brought forth by inter-molecular forces. By carefully treating the individual scaling behaviors of the non-linearities, we obtain asymptotically optimal upper and lower bounds on the rate of forward support propagation. These rates show that the fourth-order operator dominates the propagation rate on short time scales, but the long-term rate of propagation is controlled by the second-order operator. We estimate further the time at which this trade-off in propagation rate occurs. Lastly, we examine sufficient conditions to ensure that the free boundary does not immediately advance in a given direction, leading to a detailed picture of how the competition between the second/fourth-order operators influence the free boundary dynamics of solutions.

items.title: Diffusion-Score-Based Joint Topology Identification and Generative Particle Filtering
items.summary: Inferring the interaction graph of a networked system while tracking its latent state is central to infrastructure, environmental, and brain networks. Joint identification of interaction topology and latent network states is challenging when observations are intermittent and transition noise is unknown and non-Gaussian. We develop TopoScore-FAF, a diffusion-score-based framework for joint topology identification and generative particle filtering. The graph governs a leaky-diffusion conditional mean, while a frozen diffusion emulator represents the centered transition residual, avoiding the structural ambiguity of unrestricted generative models. First, we establish a score--topology duality that expresses edge-wise transition likelihood gradients as projections of the residual diffusion score. This enables topology learning without evaluating transition densities or differentiating through the generative sampler. Second, we develop diffusion-score-based topology identification with guarantees of identifiability under intermittent observations and invariance of the population minimizer across diffusion noise levels. Sufficient smoothing yields global strong convexity for bounded-plus-Gaussian residuals. As smoothing vanishes, the asymptotic covariance of the state-pair estimator decreases toward the Cramér--Rao bound, with a strict advantage over Gaussian quasi-likelihood under an edge-relevant non-Gaussianity condition. Third, we construct a topology-conditioned generative particle filter that combines guided residual sampling with score-driven graph updates. We establish mean-square closed-loop error bounds under a step-size-independent small-gain condition. The resulting framework uses the graph to structure state propagation and the estimated states to refine the graph. Synthetic and real-data experiments demonstrate its benefits under non-Gaussian forcing.

items.title: The n-th Zbáganu constant
items.summary: In this paper, we introduce the $n$-th Zbáganu constant for Banach spaces and investigate its basic properties. We establish some inequalities which give the relationship between the $n$-th Zbáganu constant and two other constants, namely the $n$-th Von Neumann-Jordan constant and the $n$-th James constant. In addition, we determine the values of the $n$-th Zbáganu constant for Lebesgue spaces, Morrey spaces, and discrete Morrey spaces.

items.title: Boundaries of groups with compact-by-amenable decomposition
items.summary: We look at the Liouville property (triviality of harmonic functions) of topological groups G relative to a compact subgroup K. We show that Gelfand pairs have this property. Furthermore, we show that this property holds if and only if G admits a product decomposition G = K S for an amenable subgroup S. We identify the Poisson and Furstenberg boundaries of these groups. This applies in particular to reductive algebraic groups over local fields.

items.title: An Anchor-and-Propagate Scheme for Certified $O(n^2)$ Computation of Shapley Vectors in Cooperative Product Games
items.summary:
For a general cooperative game, the Shapley values of the players need not be related, but for cooperative product games they are closely linked; identifying and exploiting these relations is one purpose of this study. We consider a network of \(n\) devices that participate independently with probabilities \(p_1,\dots,p_n\), giving the plausibility game \(T(S)=1-\prod_{i\in S}(1-p_i)\), whose Shapley values are \(φ_i=p_i\int_0^1\prod_{j
e i}(1-p_jt)\,dt\). Since \(T=1-w\) for the product game \(w(S)=\prod_{i\in S}(1-p_i)\), the results transfer to product games with factors in \([0,1]\). Our main contribution is an \emph{anchor-and-propagate} scheme: once \(φ_1\) is computed exactly, the exact identities \(φ_i=c_iφ_1+p_i(p_i-p_1)B_i\) and \(φ_i=φ_1+(p_i-p_1)J_i\), with \(c_i=p_i/p_1\) and one-dimensional integrals \(B_i\le	frac12J_i\), give the remaining \(n-1\) values in \(O(n)\) total time with certified error bounds. For small \(S_i=\sum_{j
e1,i}p_j\) we use a truncated Bonferroni expansion of \(B_i\); for large \(S_i\), a new estimator with relative error \(O(m_i^2/S_i^2)\), \(m_i=\max_{j
e1,i}p_j\). The anchor is computed by Gauss--Legendre quadrature in \(O(n^2)\) operations or, without irrational nodes, exactly by polynomial expansion. The whole vector costs \(	frac32n^2+O(n)\) operations, about half the exact baseline and less than QuadraSHAP. For \(n=100\), the scheme uses \(1.8	imes10^4\) operations with errors below \(3.4	imes10^{-7}\), within a certified bound of \(2.1	imes10^{-6}\); permutation sampling (Castro et al.) needs \(4	imes10^7\) operations for an error of \(7.9	imes10^{-4}\), controlled only in probability. We also give an anchor-free closed-form approximation with an explicit error bound, and a self-contained derivation of Shapley's formula using combinatorial identities and the Beta function.

items.title: Two results on rich-neighbour $5$-colouring of subcubic graphs
items.summary: A rich-neighbour edge-colouring is a proper edge-colouring in which every non-isolated edge has an adjacent edge whose neighbours have pairwise distinct colours. Petruševski and Škrekovski conjectured that every connected subcubic loopless multigraph distinct from $K_4$ admits such a colouring with five colours. We prove the conjecture for two classes: claw-free subcubic loopless multigraphs and $2$-connected subcubic outerplanar loopless multigraphs. The bound is sharp in both classes, as witnessed by the diamond $K_4-e$.

items.title: A Well-Separated Pair Decomposition of Linear Size for Unit-Disk Graphs
items.summary: We prove that every connected Euclidean-weighted unit-disk graph on $n$ vertices has a $(1/\varepsilon)$-well-separated pair decomposition of size $O(n\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\varepsilon))$. This resolves an open problem posed by Gao and Zhang in 2003. We also show that this bound is tight: there are connected unit-disk graphs for which any $(1/\varepsilon)$-well-separated pair decomposition has size $Ω(n\varepsilon^{-2}\log (1/\varepsilon))$.

items.title: Smooth minimal fourfolds not connected by smooth elementary flops
items.summary: We first construct two smooth projective toric fourfolds of Picard number eight that are connected by elementary flops, but cannot be connected by elementary flops through smooth complete toric varieties. This answers a question raised by the first author in 2004. Then, by taking suitable double covers, we construct two smooth projective minimal fourfolds of general type with Picard number nine that are connected by elementary flops, but cannot be connected by elementary flops through smooth projective varieties.

items.title: Parameter estimation for discretely observed rough fractional interacting particle systems
items.summary: We study parametric inference for interacting particle systems driven by independent fractional Brownian motions, based on discrete observations of all particles over a fixed time horizon. Our goal is to estimate an unknown drift parameter in the joint limit as the number of particles increases and the observation mesh vanishes. For $H>\frac 12$, we construct contrast based estimators by extending the discrete time least squares approach of Neuenkirch and Tindel to the interacting setting. For the rough regime $H\in(\frac 14,\frac 12)$, we introduce a modified contrast and use the stochastic sewing lemma to handle the first order approximations available from discrete observations. Our analysis combines the propagation of chaos for the associated fractional McKean Vlasov equation with estimates controlling the temporal discretization error. When the Hurst parameter and the diffusion coefficient are known, we establish strong consistency and asymptotic normality of the proposed estimators. The asymptotic results reveal an interplay between the number of particles and the temporal discretization: the convergence rate with respect to the observation mesh changes at $H=\frac 34$, while the asymptotic normality holds in both regimes considered. We further develop a joint estimation procedure for the drift parameter, the Hurst parameter, and the diffusion coefficient, extending quadratic-variation methods for fractional Brownian motion to the interacting particle framework. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of the proposed estimators.

items.title: A characterization of uniformly discrete crystalline measures with unit weights
items.summary: We prove that every uniformly discrete set $\emptyset\neΛ\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ admitting a Fourier summation formula with a discrete set of frequencies $S(Λ)\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ arises from the Alon--Kummer--Kurasov--Vinzant construction using a Lee--Yang variety. In particular, every crystalline measure with uniformly discrete support and unit weights is a Fourier quasicrystal coming from the above construction. It also implies that every set $Λ\subset\mathbb{R}^d\subset\mathbb{C}^d$ as above is the common zero set in $\mathbb{C}^d$ of finitely many trigonometric polynomials, extending the one-dimensional theorem of Olevskii and Ulanovskii. As part of the proof, we generalize Meyer's notion of lighthouse measures to higher codimension and introduce lighthouse manifolds, which we characterize, up to a monomial change of coordinates, as the torus parts of Lee--Yang varieties.

items.title: Sparse Fault Detection in Linear Systems: Equivalence of GLR Tests and $\ell_1$-regularized Least Squares
items.summary: This paper studies the detection of an impulsive fault of unknown time and input channel in a linear system with unknown initial state and Gaussian measurement noise. First, we show that the generalized likelihood ratio test, after the initial state is eliminated by projection onto the parity space, is the zero-solution test of a weighted lasso with an unpenalized nuisance block; the regularization parameter is the test threshold, and for unknown noise variance the same holds for the square-root lasso. Second, we show that the null distribution depends on the system only through a Gram matrix, so that the threshold is computed exactly and offline, and we compare it with closed-form bounds. Third, we characterize the fraction of a fault that survives the projection: we give it in closed form through observability Gramians, we show that it converges to a geometrically decaying profile for strictly stable systems, and that, for systems with unit-modulus modes, it grows linearly with the fault time as a fraction of the record length. Numerical studies, including a two-input, two-output example, illustrate the results.

items.title: A complete classification of isometries of quasihyperbolic domains
items.summary: We classify all surjective quasihyperbolic isometries between arbitrary proper planar domains. Apart from Euclidean similarities, the orientation-preserving isometries are reciprocal maps on sectors or punctured planes and explicit complex-power maps on logarithmic spiral sectors. In particular, orientation-preserving planar quasihyperbolic isometries need not be Möbius. As consequences, we obtain similarity rigidity when either domain has finite inradius, for multiply connected domains other than punctured planes, and for $C^1$ domains other than half-planes. The $C^1$ conclusion strengthens Hästö's corresponding result for planar $C^3$ domains. Our planar classification, together with Richard's classification in dimensions $n\geq3$, completely solves the quasihyperbolic isometry problem between proper subdomains of $\mathbb R^n$ in every dimension $n\geq2$. As an application, we extend to dimension two the characterization of pointed Gromov--Hausdorff convergence of quasihyperbolic domains obtained by Herron, Richard, and Snipes.

items.title: Asymptotic analysis of a $3\times3$-doubly periodic random lozenge tiling model of a hexagon
items.summary: We study a random lozenge tiling model of a regular hexagon with weights that are doubly periodic with period $3$. This model features a smooth phase with six cusp points. We obtain explicit descriptions of the limit shape and the local scaling limits of the correlation kernel. Both limits are expressed as contour integrals on the Harnack curve that underlies the model, or on its double cover that is obtained by gluing together two copies along the support of an equilibrium measure in an external field. Our asymptotic analysis is based on the double contour integral representation of the correlation kernel due to Duits and Kuijlaars. This double contour integral contains a factor that is given in terms of the solution of a Riemann-Hilbert problem for matrix-valued orthogonal polynomials. The asymptotic behavior of this Riemann-Hilbert problem was recently studied by one of the authors using the Deift-Zhou method of steepest descent. In this work, we complement this approach with the asymptotic analysis of the double contour integral. The integrals are moved to the double cover of the Harnack curve. We analyze the effect of the first two transformations of the Deift-Zhou method, and deform the contours to the relevant saddle points. We visualize our asymptotic analysis on the amoeba of the Harnack curve, in the spirit of the work of Berggren and Borodin on the doubly periodic Aztec diamond.

items.title: One more curious property of $1729$: The only Carmichael number of the form $2^np^3+1$ with prime $p$
items.summary: Florian Luca recently proved that if $2^np^3+1$ is a Carmichael number for some prime $p$ and integer $n\ge1$, then $p=3$. Here we complete the cubic classification by proving that $1729$, Hardy--Ramanujan taxicab number, is the only Carmichael number of the form $2^np^3+1$ with $p$ prime and $n\ge1$. The proof identifies the unique possible multiplicatively dependent prime factor, sharpens the known bound on Fermat prime factors of $2^nk+1$ from $k^2$ to $2k$, derives the explicit bound $n\le2742$, and concludes with a short sieve requiring neither factorisation nor primality testing.

items.title: General Lagrangian formulations for mixed-antisymmetric tensor fields on flat backgrounds
items.summary: We present, for the first time, local Lagrangian formulations for (ir)reducible integer higher-spin massless and massive Poincare group representations subject to Young tableau with $k$ columns $Y[\hat{s}_1,\hat{s}_2,...,\hat{s}_k]$ in $d$-dimensional Minkowski space-time. The particles are described in a metric-like formulation by tensor fields carrying $k$ groups of antisymmetric Lorentz indices $Φ_{μ^1[{\hat{s}_1}],μ^2[{\hat{s}_2}],..., μ^k[{\hat{s}_k}]}$ using the BRST procedure with both the complete operator $Q$ and incomplete $Q_c$ BRST operators.
