items.summary: Virtual power plants (VPPs) trade in the same wholesale market and share distribution lines and transformers, and uncoordinated, profit-maximizing VPPs can push a shared transformer past its thermal limit or drive a feeder voltage out of band. The utility, which only observes the front-of-the-meter net injection at each bus, must keep the network safe from that net injection alone. We allocate a 24-hour active and reactive operating envelope to each VPP by a Benders decomposition: the utility sets a trial envelope, each VPP solves its private convex portfolio problem, and the returned value and dual gradient become supporting cuts that rebuild its value function while its schedule, state, and cost stay private. The envelope carries the transformer's thermal state across hours, bounds a joint conditional value-at-risk over forecast uncertainty, and is re-optimized each hour with the current hour committed. On a reduced IEEE-13 feeder with real load and prices, an active-power-only implementation lowers the transformer's peak-temperature CVaR from 254 to 97\,$^\circ$C at a 28\% value give-up and holds the transformer below its limit where nameplate access breaches it.

items.title: Pathology Randomization for Synthetic Priors and Zero-Shot Detection
items.summary: Hospital brain imaging archives hold a diverse array of pathology at sample sizes beyond prospective studies, particularly for underrepresented populations and diseases. To unlock uncurated clinical data and scale analysis, methods are needed to detect abnormalities across contrasts and resolutions. Synthetic data has provided robust, contrast-agnostic models for a variety of human neuroimaging tasks in healthy anatomy, but pathology detection and other tasks in clinical settings still require real patient data, contrast-specific models, or disease-specific generators. We propose PathoDraw, a generative model of brain MRI with pathology. A conditional distribution of lesions given the healthy anatomy is drawn into the label map before contrast-agnostic rendering, and a single network estimates healthy anatomy with exact signed intensity deviation of any input scan. The contrast-agnostic 3D UNet learns the healthy labels under the lesion and the signed deviation directly and identifies pathology via robust tissue statistics and learned features, despite no training on real pathology. We show zero-shot detection on public stroke, tumor, and white matter hyperintensity datasets as well as archived clinical data, spanning $T_1$w, FLAIR and $T_2$w at various resolutions under a recent unsupervised anomaly detection benchmark protocol. Our single model exceeds or performs comparably to contrast-specific anomaly detectors trained on real scans and keeps healthy anatomy intact. The same generator trains networks for super-resolution and for registration in the presence of pathology. Our model, robust across acquisition and disease, enables the use of uncurated, archived data for clinical analysis. Our code is available at https://github.com/agr78/Pathology-Randomizer.

items.title: Optimal Uniform Pricing for Multi-Interval Dispatch without Make-Whole Uplifts
items.summary: In a network with ramp-limited generators and inaccurate net-demand forecasts, practical rolling-window dispatch can drive locational marginal prices (LMPs) below generators' bid-in offers. In such cases, out-of-market (OOM) settlements are used to compensate generators and maintain dispatch-following incentives, but OOM can have negative consequences, including nontransparent real-time price signals, discriminatory compensation, and incentives for untruthful bidding. This paper presents an optimal uniform pricing rule that minimizes demand payments, eliminates OOM make-whole payments, preserves LMP-based congestion charges, and ensures revenue adequacy. We derive the proposed pricing rule in closed form and relate it to existing pricing schemes. Numerical comparisons demonstrate favorable generator profits and reduced price volatility. However, higher generator profits are accompanied by increased demand payments, reflecting the in-market, uniform allocation of ramping costs while preserving the LMP-based congestion charges widely used in real-time market settlements. The numerical results also show that, under LMP with OOM settlement, a price-taking generator has an incentive to inflate its offer, whereas this incentive is absent under the proposed pricing rule within the tested bid range.

items.title: Weight-space programming for tractor guidance controller: large language models natively write neural network weights that steer a real tractor
items.summary: Weight-space programming is a process where a large language model reads and writes the weights of a neural network directly, guided by a natural language specification, without an optimiser or gradient descent. This study applies it to automatic tractor guidance, where a 253-parameter neural network steers along paths of lines and arcs and must be adapted when the machine changes, such as a slower steering actuator. GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 (also 5.2) edited the network for our research tractor using a small budget of simulated evaluations to repair a network trained for another tractor and write a controller into a network with zero weights. We compared them with an evolution strategy, gradient descent and pure pursuit in simulation and on the real tractor. Both models read the network and analysed the closed loop with control theory correctly, and Fable's repair without simulation succeeded only occasionally. With simulated feedback, both models repaired the trained network in single sessions and wrote a working controller from zero weights, whereas from zero the evolution strategy found none. The controllers written from zero were sparse and in a classical cascaded structure; one model edited the trained network while the other replaced it. Gradient descent reached higher accuracy with far more simulation, and all language model controllers steered the real tractor without intervention, with errors of the same order as pure pursuit. Language models can program the weights of a neural controller directly, much as control engineers design one. We call this Weight-Space Engineering.

items.title: SCAN: Site-Aware Collaborative Privacy-Preserving Adaptation of Vision-Language Models for Neurological Disease Classification
items.summary: Worldwide neuroimaging data could strengthen diagnostic foundation models, but privacy rules often prevent centralizing brain MRI scans. We present SCAN, a site-aware collaborative adaptation framework for Neurological Disease Classification that lets new sites adapt a 3D medical vision-language model (VLM) without retraining or sharing patient scans. Each site keeps exact class prototypes for local prediction and can share privacy-protected class summaries: norm-bounded sums and counts perturbed once with calibrated noise. Using 7,641 scans from 67 sites across 12 countries, covering Alzheimer's disease (AD), stroke, epilepsy and controls, we assess local adaptation, cross-site benefits, and effects on existing sites. At seven unseen sites, the frozen VLM's zero-shot AUCs were 0.833-0.945 for AD and stroke. Training-free local prototypes improved epilepsy AUC at three sites from 0.598/0.625/0.508 to 0.684/0.729/0.762 and AD AUC at one site from 0.833 to 0.863, nearly matching a classifier trained at each site (mean AUC 0.757 vs. 0.759). With differential privacy ($ε$ = 4), new sites contributed without materially reducing accuracy at existing sites (AUC change $\leq$0.2%), although gains from sharing were limited, and membership attacks performed near chance. SCAN offers hospitals a worldwide framework to adapt and share brain MRI VLMs without exchanging scans or retraining.

items.title: Physics Informed Reinforcement Learning with Gibbs Priors for Topology Control in Power Grids
items.summary: Topology control for power grid operation is a challenging sequential decision making problem because the action space grows combinatorially with the size of the grid and action evaluation through simulation is computationally expensive. We propose a physics-informed Reinforcement Learning framework that combines semi-Markov control with a Gibbs prior, that encodes the system's physics, over the action space. The decision is only taken when the grid enters a hazardous regime, while a graph neural network surrogate predicts the post action overload risk of feasible topology actions. These predictions are used to construct a physics-informed Gibbs prior that both selects a small state-dependent candidate set and reweights policy logits before action selection. In this way, our method reduces exploration difficulty and online simulation cost while preserving the flexibility of a learned policy. We evaluate the approach in three realistic benchmark environments of increasing difficulty. Across all settings, the proposed method achieves a strong balance between control quality and computational efficiency: it matches oracle-level performance while being approximately $6\times$ faster on the first benchmark, reaches $94.6\%$ of oracle reward with roughly $200\times$ lower decision time on the second one, and on the most challenging benchmark improves over a PPO baseline by up to $255\%$ in reward and $284\%$ in survived steps while remaining about $2.5\times$ faster than a strong specialized engineering baseline. These results show that our method provides an effective mechanism for topology control in power grids.

items.title: Movable Antenna for Anti-Jamming Transmission: Continuous and Discrete Positioning Designs
items.summary: Movable antenna (MA) system holds big promise in further wireless communications due to the ability of reconfiguring the antenna position to enhance the spatial diversity. This paper investigates the joint design of beamforming and antenna positions in MA-assisted anti-jamming communications. We consider a multi-user multiple-input multiple-output downlink scenario where multiple malicious jammers exist. The goal is to maximize the sum-rate under the imperfect jammer channel state information. Then, we develop two distinct optimization frameworks for continuous and discrete antenna position designs, respectively. For the continuous position design, we propose an alternating optimization (AO) framework that integrates successive convex approximation and majorization minimization (MM) to handle the highly non-convex problem. For the discrete position design, based on the minimum mean squared error criterion and MM, we reformulate the problem as a sparse recovery task and propose a low-complexity heuristic block coordinate descent and simultaneous orthogonal matching pursuit, which enables joint design rather than AO. Numerical results show that the proposed discrete-position heuristic achieves higher sum rates than the adopted AO-based continuous-position algorithm. This observation highlights the trade-off between spatial resolution and optimization tractability, indicating that the sparse-recovery formulation can yield better performance than the continuous AO algorithm in the MA-assisted anti-jamming scenarios.

items.title: Higher-Order Interaction Reconstruction via Integral Physics-Informed Neural Networks
items.summary: Reconstructing higher-order interactions is a fundamental challenge in complex networked systems, with applications in ecological, social, and biological networks. This inverse problem is inherently difficult due to the combinatorial complexity of higher-order structures, the strong nonlinearity of the underlying dynamics, and the prevalence of noisy and sparse observations. In this article, we propose a novel integral physics-informed neural network (IntegralPINN) framework for higher-order interaction reconstruction. Instead of { penalizing derivative-based physics residuals,} we adopt an integral formulation over temporal intervals, which naturally suppresses high-frequency noise and mitigates derivative-induced instability. We further introduce a continuous parameterization of interaction tensors, enabling tractable identification of higher-order structures via gradient-based optimization. We provide theoretical analysis establishing a noise-robust error bound that is independent of derivative amplification when the integration window satisfies an excitation condition. Extensive experiments on ecological dynamics, social contagion, and neuronal synchronization systems demonstrate that IntegralPINN achieves accurate and robust reconstruction under noisy and sparse observations, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches.

items.title: Polylogarithmic Regret via Certainty Equivalence in Degenerate LQR
items.summary: Singular input penalties, as in minimum variance control, can reduce what must be identified to control an unknown linear system. In online linear quadratic control, certainty equivalence can achieve polylogarithmic regret when the optimal controller is identifiable from data collected under optimal feedback. With a positive definite input penalty, however, this condition is restrictive, since for an invertible state matrix it requires all unknown parameters to be identifiable under optimal feedback. We show that singular input penalties relax this requirement, expanding the class of problems in which certainty equivalence achieves polylogarithmic regret. Specifically, we prove that a certainty-equivalence algorithm with a short initial exploration phase achieves $O(\log^2 T)$ expected regret over $T$ interactions whenever controller identifiability holds. We complement this guarantee with an $Ω(\sqrt{T})$ minimax lower bound for a family containing a system where controller identifiability fails. For minimum variance control, knowing the range of the input matrix suffices for controller identifiability, a weaker requirement than knowing the full input matrix, as assumed in prior work with positive definite input penalties. This condition also covers underactuated systems, as we illustrate with a cart-pole example.

items.title: ALOHA Lightning: Learning Fast and Precise Manipulation
items.summary: Learning from human demonstrations has enabled robots to acquire a wide range of manipulation skills, but learned policies typically execute far slower than ordinary humans. This speed gap is mainly due to lack of an interface for collecting demonstration data at high speed, and the difficulty in training policies that can robustly execute high-speed motions. In this paper, we present ALOHA Lightning (Flash ALOHA), a system for learning fast and precise robotic manipulation. Our system uses kinesthetic teaching to intuitively collect near-human-speed demonstrations on a backdrivable bimanual platform, yielding natural and fast trajectories. We also present a learning pipeline that enables smooth high-speed execution through test-time action smoothing and aligns the visual data distribution between data collection and deployment with masking. Given 50 demonstrations for each task, ALOHA Lightning autonomously completes bimanual tasks such as ball tossing and catching, folding shorts, battery insertion, and bussing tables for over 80% success rates while close to human speed. Project website: https://flash-aloha.github.io/

items.title: Finite-Step Invariant Sets for Hybrid Systems with Probabilistic Guarantees
items.summary: Poincaré return maps are a fundamental tool for analyzing periodic orbits in hybrid dynamical systems by reducing the stability analysis of a periodic orbit to that of a discrete-time system. While linearization provides local stability information, assessing robustness to disturbances requires identifying invariant sets of the state space under the return dynamics. However, computing such invariant sets is computationally difficult, especially when system dynamics are only available through forward simulation. In this work, we propose an algorithmic framework leveraging sampling-based optimization to compute a finite-step invariant level set around a nominal periodic orbit using sampled evaluations of the return map. The resulting solution is accompanied by probabilistic guarantees on finite-step invariance. We provide theoretic analysis establishing sufficient conditions for which the algorithm terminates and demonstrate the approach on two low-dimensional systems and a Compass-Gait Walking model.

items.title: Large-Load Demand Flexibility as Virtual Storage
items.summary: Water electrolysis plants, hyperscale data centers, and aluminum potlines represent gigawatts of demand-side flexibility for bulk power system balancing, operational planning, and procurement services. Such loads are scheduled through per-interval power bounds and horizon energy windows, whereas co-located battery energy storage systems (BESS) operate under state-of-charge dynamics. The two formulations share no common mathematical structure, and the joint procurement value of co-located loads and storage goes unrealized as a result. This paper establishes the connection between the two formulations through a virtual storage (VS) equivalence. Every feasible large-load trajectory under power-bound and energy-window constraints is a valid charge trajectory of a VS device that operates at unity accounting efficiency in the grid power balance. Production and service-level costs lie outside this abstraction and enter the dispatch through curtailment opportunity costs. For a portfolio co-located with a BESS, aggregation reduces the constraint count from O(NT) to O(T) and yields a co-dispatch price for both resources. Validation on the IEEE RTS-GMLC with three representative load classes shows that virtual storage delivers the dominant share of joint procurement savings. In the tested case, savings are additive because the two resources dispatch to non-overlapping intervals, and the curtailment shadow price tracks the peak-price band onset rather than the daily peak price.

items.title: Tie-Line Scheduling Using Real-Time Contraction Metrics: Hierarchical Reachable Sets for Multi-Area Inverter-Dominated Grids
items.summary: Managing transmission congestion in multi-area power grids dominated by inverter-based resources (IBRs) requires bridging a severe timescale and modeling divide. Supervisory congestion optimizers -- such as Online Feedback Optimization (OFO) and two-tiered differentiable Model Predictive Control (MPC) -- rely on linearized, convex algebraic grid approximations that cannot guarantee dynamic stability during sub-second converter transients. Conversely, fast distributed consensus schemes like Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) depend on convex plant assumptions and iterative message exchanges that lag behind rapid tie-line surges. This paper replaces convex ADMM emergency consensus with a Distributed Nonlinear Separable Control Contraction Metric (SCCM) architecture spanning three nested tiers: the Device layer, the Area layer, and the Grid tie-line layer. By pairing online Prediction Error Method and Moving Horizon Estimation (PEM-MHE) parameter tracking with offline convex Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) synthesis, the controller executes a closed-form nonlinear feedback law online without solving real-time optimization problems. We derive the Pontryagin attainable (reachable) ellipsoids for each layer, prove hierarchical tube containment via Schur-complement matrix inequalities, and project the certified Grid reachable tube through Power Transfer Distribution Factors (PTDFs) to supply guaranteed safe thermal limits to the supervisory coordinator. Validation on modified IEEE 39-bus (100% IBR, zero synchronous generators) and 3-area IEEE 118-bus systems demonstrates an 82.8% reduction in cumulative tie-line thermal overload while maintaining strict exponential contraction ($λ_{\max} \le -2.43$) even under a 3 s communication blackout.

items.title: Differentiable-by-design Nonlinear Optimization for Model Predictive Control
items.summary: Nonlinear optimization-based control policies, such as those arising in nonlinear Model Predictive Control, have seen remarkable success in recent years. These policies require solving computationally demanding nonlinear optimization programs online at each time-step. The resulting solution map, viewed as a function of the measured state of the system and design parameters, may not be differentiable, which poses significant challenges if the control policy is embedded in a gradient-based policy optimization scheme. We propose a principled way to regularize the nonlinear optimization problem around the nominal solution, obtaining a surrogate derivative even if the solution map of the original problem is not differentiable. The surrogate problem is differentiable by design and its solution coincides with the solution of the unregularized problem. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in a free-final-time optimal control problem and a receding-horizon nonlinear MPC example.

items.title: Mechanism Design and Active Systems Theory: 60 Years of Parallel Development
items.summary: The survey compares two research traditions within the mathematical theory of designing the rules of interaction (mechanisms) for purposeful participants: mechanism design, together with contract theory and implementation theory, and the theory of active systems created by V.N. Burkov and developed into the theory of control in organizations (TCO) by D.A. Novikov's school; the main results of Yu.B. Germeier's school and of the domestic schools adjacent to active systems theory (AST) are covered as well. The problem statements and principal results of 2006-2026 are presented: for mechanism design (MD) - robust and dynamic mechanism design, multidimensional screening, information design, simplicity of mechanisms and credibility of the designer, market design, algorithmic and learning-based design, mechanisms for AI agents, and robust, relational, dynamic and algorithmic contracts; for AST and TCO - a general typology of control, strategy-proof and incentive-compatible planning mechanisms, decomposition of the agents' game, systems with distributed control and coalitional interaction, reflexive games and informational control, control of staff and structure, dynamic active systems, and project management. A correspondence between the classical results is established (the fair play principle and the revelation principle, the serial resource allocation mechanism and the uniform rule, active expertise mechanisms and generalized median schemes, quasi-compensatory incentive schemes and contracts under observable actions), and priorities are delineated by uniform rules; the areas where the two traditions diverge are identified, as are the dimensions of the problem (staff, structure, institutions, awareness, agents' beliefs) covered only by TCO.

items.title: The Impact of Scenario Representation in Scenario-based Optimization Certification
items.summary: Scenario-based optimization provides finite-sample guarantees for decisions constructed from sampled uncertainty, but its certification procedures can be sensitive to how those samples are represented. We investigate this sensitivity under lossless scenario regrouping, which preserves the sampled information, feasible region, optimizer, and primitive violation probability. For an equal-allocation support-subsample certificate, we derive the distortion factor \(k^2(1-ε)^{k-1}\), establish certification reversals between equivalent representations, and provide sufficient conditions for acceptance dominance under nested coarsening. We further apply nondegeneracy-free Wait-and-Judge theory to coordinatewise scenario envelopes, enabling stronger certification directly from the primitive observations. In paired scenario-MPC experiments, exact regrouping increases certification availability from 318 to 471 of 480 attempts without changing the samples, numerical proposals, or requiring any reduction in witness cardinality. Primitive Wait-and-Judge certification accepts the same 471 attempts without regrouping. These results demonstrate that apparent scenario sample-efficiency gains can arise from certificate accounting rather than additional information or reduced decision risk.

items.title: Beyond Reconstruction: A Unified Framework for Trustworthy and Explainable EEG Artifact Removal Evaluation
items.summary: Deep-learning methods have achieved strong performance in EEG artifact removal, but evaluation remains dominated by reconstruction metrics such as error, correlation, and signal-to-noise ratio. Although these metrics assess similarity to clean EEG, they do not establish whether models effectively suppress artifacts, preserve neural activity, or provide reliable explanations. To address these limitations, we propose TriX-EEG, a three-level framework for trustworthy and explainable EEG artifact removal. Level 1, Signal Validity (SV), evaluates reconstruction quality and neural band-power preservation. Level 2, Removal Faithfulness (RF), assesses the removed component through artifact error and residual artifact/neural leakage. Level 3, Explanation Reliability (ER), examines model behavior through temporal alignment, causal relevance, and stability. We evaluate TriX-EEG using nine published neural denoisers across three public benchmarks derived from EEGDenoiseNet and the PhysioNet Motion Artifact Contaminated EEG Dataset, covering EOG, EMG, and motion artifacts. Results show that reconstruction metrics alone are insufficient for trustworthy denoiser assessment: RF complements it by revealing whether errors stem from residual artifact or suppressed neural activity, while ER captures distinct aspects of explanation behavior, supporting joint evaluation of three aspects within a unified framework rather than reliance on any single factor. External validation on an independent EEG/EOG dataset and the BCI Competition IV-2a motor-imagery dataset further demonstrates broadly consistent rankings under dataset shift. Higher-ranked denoisers generally preserve more task-relevant information or cause less downstream performance degradation. Overall, TriX-EEG provides a comprehensive basis for EEG denoiser assessment, encouraging models that are not only accurate but also faithful and explainable.

items.title: Transient State Preservation of a Dissipative Qubit via Lyapunov Control
items.summary: Preserving quantum states in the presence of environmental decoherence remains a fundamental challenge for quantum information processing. This work investigates whether Hamiltonian Lyapunov feedback can transiently preserve the state of an open qubit by reshaping its trajectory under Markovian dissipation. A state-error Lyapunov function is adopted to derive an analytical feedback law for Lindblad dynamics, ensuring a nonincreasing Lyapunov function whenever the control sensitivities are nonzero. The analysis identifies the geometric conditions under which the feedback becomes ineffective, showing that control authority vanishes when the current and target Bloch vectors are collinear. Numerical simulations are performed for amplitude damping and pure dephasing using selected target states. Performance is evaluated through fidelity, accumulated infidelity, dwell time above a fidelity threshold, coherence, and control effort. The results demonstrate that the proposed feedback cannot eliminate irreversible dissipation or achieve universal asymptotic stabilization, but it can provide transient benefits for selected target-channel combinations. In particular, under amplitude damping, the controller significantly reduces accumulated infidelity and substantially extends the interval during which the system remains above a prescribed fidelity threshold. In the pure dephasing cases examined, improvements in fidelity are generally limited, although transient coherence preservation is observed for the oblique target considered, revealing a trade-off between coherence and state fidelity. These findings indicate that Lyapunov-based Hamiltonian feedback is best suited as a transient preservation mechanism and motivate its application to gate operations and preservation of prepared states during finite time intervals before their use or readout.

items.title: Hyperlyve: Parallelized Enumeration and Exact Lyapunov Stability Certification for Deep ReLU Networks
items.summary: We introduce Hyperlyve (Hyperplane Partitioned Lyapunov Verification and Enumeration), a framework for proving the asymptotic stability of nonlinear dynamical systems, including those with neural network controllers. Hyperlyve learns and formally certifies continuous piecewise-affine (CPA) neural Lyapunov functions within a counterexample-guided inductive synthesis (CEGIS) loop. Hyperlyve's key innovation is a parallel algorithm that enumerates the hyperplane arrangement formed by the ReLU activations of deep networks and certifies that Lyapunov conditions hold within each polyhedral region. We derive sound and complete regional tests to verify the asymptotic stability of the exact smooth dynamics (rather than a piecewise-linear approximation) within a compact domain of interest. Furthermore, we formally characterize the computational complexity of the CPA neural Lyapunov verification problem as co-NP-complete, filling a key gap in the literature. Empirical results demonstrate that Hyperlyve enumerates ReLU networks over 150-times faster than competing tools, which contributes to Hyperlyve proving the asymptotic stability of systems that are currently intractable for state-of-the-art verifiers.

items.title: Projection-Based Partitioned MiLAC Architecture for MU-MIMO Precoding
items.summary: This work proposes a partitioned Microwave Linear Analog Computer (MiLAC) architecture for user-specific MU-MIMO precoding based on independently configured analog subnetworks. The proposed method reformulates user-level interference suppression as an invertible projection-based transformation, which is computed from the channel and synthesized into the MiLAC admittances. While the resulting offline configuration incurs higher computational complexity than conventional ZFBF and regularized ZFBF, it remains substantially below fully digital Block Diagonalization. Once configured, the Sub-MiLACs perform the precoding operation in the analog domain, yielding significantly lower online processing complexity. Under ideal conditions, the proposed method achieves performance close to fully digital BD.

items.title: Fundamental Tradeoffs in Sampling, Transmission and Information Freshness: Instantaneous Feedback
items.summary: We study a time-slotted generate-at-will status-update system over an erasure channel with transmission success probability $q$, subject to average sampling- and transmission-rate constraints $f_s$ and $f_r$, respectively. The sampler-transmitter pair jointly decides whether to idle, retransmit a stale packet, or replace it with a fresh sample. We derive a universal lower bound on the optimal average age of information, analyze a class of stationary randomized policies, and obtain an optimal policy within this class that provides a $4$-approximation guarantee. The joint problem reduces to the sampling-constrained problem when $f_s\leq qf_r$ and the transmission-constrained problem when $f_s\geq f_r$. For $qf_r<f_s<f_r$, we formulate a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP) and introduce the class $\barΠ$ of $(W,R)$ policies, where $W$ specifies a waiting threshold for transmission and $R$ specifies a packet-replacement threshold. We prove that, for every choice of Lagrange multipliers, the corresponding Lagrangian-relaxed Markov decision process admits an optimal policy in $\barΠ$. We then formulate a linear program (LP) over distributions of $(W,R)$ policies and prove that choosing a policy according to an optimal LP solution yields an optimal CMDP policy. Moreover, there exists an optimal LP solution assigning positive probability to at most three $(W,R)$ policies. Since $\barΠ$ is countably infinite, for every $ε>0$ we construct a finite subset $\barΠ_ε\subset\barΠ$ and show that the LP restricted to this set yields an $ε$-optimal policy. Finally, we derive a stronger pair of lower bounds by considering systems with only the sampling-rate or transmission-rate constraint. Using these bounds, we construct a policy randomizing among four $(W,R)$ policies with a $2$-approximation guarantee for $qf_r<f_s<f_r$.

items.title: How Much Does Saliency Accuracy Matter for Saliency-Guided 360-degree Image Compression?
items.summary: Saliency-guided coding allocates bits to the regions viewers are most likely to attend, but accurate 360-degree saliency prediction is computationally expensive, an obstacle for low-latency immersive streaming applications such as robot teleoperation. We quantify how much saliency-prediction accuracy actually translates into compression gain. Building on a saliency-guided rate-distortion-optimized (RDO) learned codec, modified so that the training-time latent mask is driven by ground-truth saliency, which yields a single, predictor-agnostic codec, we evaluate saliency predictors spanning two orders of magnitude in compute on both the learned codec and H.265/HEVC. The results show that higher saliency-prediction accuracy yields diminishing compression gains: a lightweight predictor fast enough for live use (52 frames per second) captures 65% of the ground-truth oracle's bit-rate saving, a 3.3x heavier one reaches 74%, and a further 38x increase in compute adds no measurable benefit, on either codec. Therefore, lightweight predictors might also be a practical choice for latency-constrained 360-degree streaming.

items.title: Physical Sensing Verification for Cognitive ISAC against UAV Spoofing via Digital Twins
items.summary: As integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) lets 5G and 6G base stations detect drones, software agents will act on these detections, so a replayed signal can plant a phantom drone that triggers real actions. This paper proposes a wall-based physical check for such cognitive ISAC systems. A digital twin (DT) predicts the delay and angle of a genuine target's wall echo. A relay can fake the direct echo's range but, standing elsewhere, not the direction of its own wall echo. The paper proves that line-of-sight beam steering cannot expose a matched relay, and that, under stated conditions, a single-antenna relay faking a wall echo leaves a telltale echo where a genuine target leaves none. In a pre-registered ray-tracing study, the twin's evidence separated genuine targets and replays perfectly (AUC 1.000), and a later-registered passive check without extra transmission accepted every held-out genuine target and no replay. The primary active probe was inconclusive (5.3% false acceptances against a 5% limit), lacking threshold margin. At the evaluated relay positions, the conditional bound certifies 3 of 24 held-out streets against adaptive or fixed single-antenna relay signals meeting its conditions, reproduced on fresh streets. Doubling the bandwidth raises this to 11 of 24.

items.title: A Scalable Decentralized Event-Triggered Topology-Switching Protocol for Verifiable Safety in Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: This paper develops a decentralized event-triggered topology-switching protocol that allows agents to disconnect from the communication network while preserving state safety and excluding Zeno behavior. We establish a robust barrier function condition that guarantees safety as long as the estimation error remains within a prescribed threshold. Each agent uses locally computable certificates to determine when to connect and disconnect from the network. The certificate construction improves scalability by reducing the complexity of topology-dependent computations from $O(2^N)$ to $O(N)$, where $N$ is the number of agents. We formally prove that the protocol ensures the estimation error does not exceed the prescribed threshold and is non-Zeno. An alternating method computes an error-weighting matrix and a quadratic barrier function that guarantee safety under the proposed protocol. Finally, we evaluate the protocol on four interconnected microgrids. Compared with maintaining network connectivity at all times, the protocol reduces the time agents remain connected while keeping phase and frequency within their safe operating region.

items.title: SPDMX: Large-Scale Open Stem Audio From Symbolic Music
items.summary: Large public datasets have driven recent progress in machine learning, from text and vision to speech and general audio. Music remains an outlier, as copyright blocks redistribution of training audio, in particular for modern tasks that need individual stems rather than mixtures. Existing multitrack resources trade off realism, scale, and licensing, as synthetic alternatives rely on proprietary VSTs or naive open rendering that yields weak stems. We introduce SPDMX, an openly-licensed stem corpus rendered from the public-domain PDMX dataset. SPDMX comprises $5{,}469$ song-hours ($2{,}734$ song-hours, or $34.8\%$, of which are multitrack scores) at $44.1$ kHz under CC BY 4.0, with paired MIDI and identifiers that link our dataset to PDMX's original metadata. To our knowledge, SPDMX's multitrack subset constitutes the largest openly-licensed synthetic multitrack subset by song-hours. We then demo SPDMX as a dataset for both source separation and transcription, showing how its increased scale can enable better training of models on synthetic data. We release SPDMX, as well as the open creation pipeline for reuse on other symbolic music datasets.

items.title: Exponential Quantum Memory Advantage for Late-Graph Smoothness and Spectral Estimation
items.summary: Graph signal processing tests how smoothly the decisions of next-generation massive sensor networks with $N$ nodes vary over their neighbour graph. Memory becomes the bottleneck when the neighbour graph arrives only after data erasure, a late-graph setting motivated by dispersed sensor networks and telemetry. We analyse three collection scenarios, reliable rounds, continuous broadcast and ordered capture, and test the Dirichlet energy $\mathcal E_G=\mathbf z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf L\mathbf z/N$ of the fused decision map $\mathbf z\in\{\pm1\}^N$, with late-graph Laplacian $\mathbf L$, against two thresholds. Hidden Matching uses $O(\log N)$ qubits on fused bits, but in reliable rounds and continuous broadcast, where nodes report $b$ sub-bits separately, a classical record buffer before it uses $O(N b)$ bits; classical methods need $Ω(\sqrt N)$ bits in the worst case. The recently introduced Quantum Oracle Sketching builds quantum oracles from random data streams without storing them. We combine coherent loading of separately reported sub-bits, exact in reliable rounds and by Quantum Oracle Sketching in continuous broadcast, with nonlinear fusion and Hidden Matching readout. The register count $R$ does not grow with $N$, and the memory is $O(\log N)$ logical qubits and classical bits, at fixed $b$, graph bounds, thresholds and error targets: an exponential memory advantage over every classical receiver and over Hidden Matching with that buffer. We prove unbiasedness in reliable rounds, preparation bounds in continuous broadcast, classical lower bounds and, for a planner-supplied multi-hop coefficient stream, spectral error bounds. Broadcast simulations match analytic averages at $N=1024$, without resolved bias growth up to $N=2^{20}$. Fault-tolerant hardware, gate rates and, in continuous broadcast, report counts remain open.

items.title: Location Privacy for ISAC Systems: Rate, Sensing, and Privacy Tradeoff
items.summary: In this paper, we design a beamformer for transmitter location privacy in an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where the transmitter communicates with a receiver while sensing a point target. We adopt the direction-of-arrival obfuscation power ratio (DoA-OPR), the ratio of the received power in a prescribed fake direction to that in the actual direction, as the location privacy metric. To design the beamformer, we formulate an achievable rate maximization problem subject to constraints on total transmit power, target sensing, location privacy, and the number of data streams. The resulting problem is nonconvex and is addressed through an eigenmode-selection and power-allocation framework. To reduce the computational complexity of the solution, we develop strategies that eliminate infeasible candidate solutions. Furthermore, we propose a fake angle selection technique in which the transmit power for target sensing aids location privacy. Numerical results illustrate the achievable rate-sensing-privacy tradeoff and show that the proposed fake angle selection technique performs better than the random fake angle selection technique.

items.title: Robust Transmission Design for RIS-Assisted RSMA-SWIPT Systems With Movable Antennas Under Hardware Distortions
items.summary: To support joint information and energy delivery to energy-constrained users, this paper investigates robust transmission design for a multi-user rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA)-based simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) system empowered by movable antennas (MAs) and a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) under channel state information (CSI) uncertainty and residual hardware impairments (HIs). Unlike fixed-position antenna systems, MAs-enabled systems exhibit position-dependent channels, making CSI uncertainty relevant to both active and passive beamforming and antenna position adaptation. Residual HIs alter the effective signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratios and further couple transmit beamforming, RIS reflection control, common-rate allocation, power-splitting ratios, and antenna positions. These effects jointly yield a highly coupled resource allocation problem. To address this challenge, we propose a robust framework that maximizes the achievable sum-rate by jointly optimizing these variables subject to practical system constraints. A non-linear energy harvesting model is incorporated to capture practical SWIPT operation. The resulting non-convex problem is addressed through successive decomposition into active beamforming, RIS reflection design, power-splitting ratio optimization, and MAs position optimization subproblems, with tractable convex surrogate functions constructed to facilitate computationally efficient solutions. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, showing significant achievable sum-rate gains over benchmark schemes and favorable robustness and convergence behavior.

items.title: RemoteRF: A Global, Open-Source Sandbox for Wireless Research and Education
items.summary: Software-defined radios (SDRs) are powerful tools for research and education in wireless communications, but their cost and complexity put them out of reach for many researchers and institutions worldwide. To address this, we introduce RemoteRF, an open-source platform for creating large-scale testbeds of distributed SDRs and multi-modal peripherals that can be managed by a single server and shared across many users. Through a reservation-based framework, users can control devices over the internet via Python scripting, with only device-related commands routed to the server. In research, RemoteRF can be used to evaluate and reproducibly benchmark new physical-layer and full-stack 5G/6G techniques, collect real-world data for machine learning, and give AI agents controlled access to hardware for autonomous experimentation. In education, RemoteRF allows students in virtually any sized class to share a handful of SDRs to learn communication fundamentals through hands-on implementation with actual radios. The software powering RemoteRF is open-source and extensively documented online, allowing anyone to deploy their own instance in a matter of minutes. Beyond local use, instances can also connect to the RemoteRF Global network to share hardware across partner institutions or make devices publicly accessible worldwide. Since being deployed at UCLA, RemoteRF has logged over 4,000 hours of use across more than 250 researchers and students.

items.title: Evolution Toward Sensing-Enabled RAN: Practical Bistatic Sensing via Uplink
items.summary: This paper considers uplink channel state information (CSI)-based sensing as an opportunistic approach to enabling sensing in cellular networks, with minimum required modifications to the infrastructure. A practical sensing signal processing procedure is presented, combining 5G positioning function with multi-antenna array processing for passive target localization. The approach is validated through simulation and practical experiments with a software-defined radio-based setup, utilizing open-source software frameworks and commercially available hardware components. Results demonstrate feasibility of the uplink CSI-based sensing for detection, localization and tracking of moving targets over local areas.

items.title: Input-to-State Stability in Distributed Adaptive Identification of Nonlinear Systems without Input Sharing
items.summary: This paper studies continuous-time distributed adaptive identification of unknown nonlinear systems over directed communication networks without requiring source or neighboring inputs to be shared. Each sensing node reconstructs the source state while adapting local estimates of the unknown linear and nonlinear dynamics using only locally available information and neighboring state estimates. A network-level error representation is derived to characterize the interaction among the communication topology, observer dynamics, parameter uncertainty, and nonlinear mismatch. Norm-based, structured Lyapunov, and robust LMI conditions are established to guarantee that the resulting coupling operator is Hurwitz. Unlike the corresponding discrete-time formulation, the proposed continuous-time adaptive laws do not require normalization. A Lyapunov analysis establishes boundedness of the adaptive parameters and asymptotic convergence of the estimation and source-tracking errors in the unperturbed case. Input-to-state stability is further established under bounded predictor mismatch and source disturbances. Numerical studies over star, cyclic, and path topologies support the theoretical results and demonstrate approximately linear computational scaling with the number of sensing nodes.

items.title: RESILAGENT: A Three-Pillar Architecture for Cyber-Physical Resilience in Electrical Power and Energy Systems
items.summary: Electrical Power and Energy Systems face hybrid threats that combine cyber intrusions, physical sabotage and climate-driven stress, and routinely outpace today's siloed monitoring stacks. We present RESILAGENT, a concept architecture organised around three operational pillars, Sensing & Data Intelligence, Resilience Analytics & Reporting, and Incident Response & Recovery, mediated by a Cloud-based Orchestrator and exercised through a closed Detect-Simulate-Decide-Sign loop. The framework fuses agentic artificial intelligence and multimodal large language models for cross-modal detection, real-time digital twins for what-if simulation, and a permissioned blockchain anchor for tamper-evident threat intelligence and CER/NIS2-aligned evidence. We instantiate it on two scenarios, a transmission operator under coordinated cyber compromise, sabotage and heatwave, and a distribution operator under a supply-chain compromise during a storm, and report an IEEE-bus micro-benchmark that quantifies each pillar through false-data-injection attack detection, cyber-physical fusion lift, N-1 contingency screening and anchor cost.

items.title: Warm Starting Neural Dynamics Models From Few Jacobian Samples
items.summary: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) leverages a model of the environment, used for planning and generating samples without interacting with the real world. Motivated by evidence that informed initialization significantly improves the efficiency of MBRL, we propose TDec-Init, an algorithm to warm-start neural dynamics models using transition Jacobians. Using a decoupling algorithm based on the decomposition of a tensor of stacked Jacobian samples, we recover weights and flexible nonlinearities, and use them to initialize a feedforward neural network. In the low-data regime, we show on several benchmark environments that our approach outperforms random initialization and value training, and either matches or outperforms Sobolev training, while requiring fewer training steps between episodes.

items.title: Making Tensor Decoupling More Robust and Less Parametric
items.summary: Tensor decoupling algorithms recover compact representations of multivariate functions by combining linear factor matrices with univariate internal nonlinearities. We identify two limitations of recent methods. First, their performance is not invariant to mismatched output or gradient magnitudes, and second, their spline internals require manual tuning of their degrees of freedom. We propose two lightweight fixes. The first is a preprocessing step that rescales the input Jacobian tensor, removing both the bias towards larger magnitude outputs and the ill-conditioning of certain factor updates caused by such a mismatch. The second replaces B-spline internals by penalized splines coupled with generalized cross-validation, making the method less dependent on the user selecting the right number of control points. Finally, we release an efficient open-source JAX implementation of our algorithm.

items.title: Robust Action Clusters and Cascades in Opinion Dynamics with Heterogeneous Action Thresholds
items.summary: We study the preservation and propagation of public actions in networks whose agents hold continuous private opinions. Agents update their opinions from their neighbors' observed actions and express them through action rules whose thresholds differ across agents. We characterize groups of agents that preserve a given common action regardless of the outsiders' actions. We call such a group, paired with that action, a robust action cluster. We show that a group is a robust action cluster for that action if and only if each member places enough of its influence weight on the group, where the required influence depends on the member's own action rule. We further give a sufficient condition under which an agent outside the cluster permanently adopts the cluster's action, and we iterate it to obtain a cascade of agents that are guaranteed to adopt that action. Finally, numerical examples show that replacing heterogeneous thresholds by their mean can change both the propagation of an action and the presence of robust action clusters.

items.title: Quantum Optimization Algorithm for Pinching-Antenna Activation with Max-Min Fairness
items.summary: In this letter, we propose a training-free quantum approximate optimization algorithm with a linear-ramp schedule (LR-QAOA) for antenna activation in pinching-antenna systems (PASS). Since all active pinching antennas (PAs) share one feed and split its power, maximizing the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the weakest user becomes a combinatorial max-min problem that must be re-solved whenever the users move. We formulate the problem as a two-local Ising Hamiltonian with one qubit per PA and no penalty terms, employing a weightedsum surrogate to prioritize weaker users. Instead of training the circuit with a classical optimizer, the proposed LR-QAOA method tunes its parameters via a linear ramp; the measured patterns are ranked by the exact max-min objective, and the best ones are refined with a short local search using the same number of evaluated patterns. Monte Carlo simulations show that the proposed LR-QAOA method outperforms greedy activation, projection-guided activation, and semidefinite relaxation-based classical baseline methods when all methods test the same number of PA on/off patterns. Experiments on real IBM Quantum hardware further show that the execution time remains nearly constant as the number of PAs grows, whereas exhaustive search grows exponentially. However, gate noise in the NISQ era restricts near-optimal hardware solutions to small numbers of antennas only.

items.title: FDIR: Fidelity-Anchored Decompressed Image Restoration for Human and Machine Perception
items.summary: Evaluating restored images requires considering pixel fidelity, human perception, and machine preference. However, existing compressed image restoration methods rarely satisfy all three criteria at once. Regression models preserve pixel fidelity but often produce overly smooth results. Conversely, generative models create realistic textures but tend to drift from the ground truth. To address this trade-off, we propose FDIR (Fidelity-Anchored Decompressed Image Restoration), a framework that uses generative priors while preserving strong pixel fidelity. FDIR works in two stages. First, a quality-guided one-step flow model (QO-Flow) adapts a pretrained latent flow backbone with LoRA to generate a structural prior in a single forward pass. Second, rather than outputting this generated image directly, a flow-conditioned detail refinement network (FCDR) uses it to predict a pixel-space residual on the decompressed input. This design brings in perceptual details while keeping the final output faithful to the original image. We evaluate FDIR on LIVE1 and DIV2K under severe compression at quality factors 1 and 5. Across all four settings, FDIR achieves the highest PSNR among the seven compared methods and beats the strongest perceptual baseline, CODiff, by 1.3 to 2.1 dB. It also ranks second on LPIPS in all four settings and on FID and DISTS on DIV2K-Val, right behind CODiff. For downstream detection, segmentation, and retrieval at quality factors 20 and 30, FDIR ranks second on every individual metric and achieves the best average rank across all ten metrics. Overall, FDIR is the only method to maintain a top-two average rank across fidelity, perception, and machine preference.

items.title: Data-Driven Predictive Control for Autonomous Vehicle Racing under Varying Friction
items.summary: Data-driven predictive control (DPC) predicts future outputs by combining recorded input-output trajectory data such that the combined trajectory approximately matches a measured initial trajectory and tracks a provided reference. This paper investigates to what extent and under which conditions DPC using data pooled across operating conditions retains the prediction accuracy of DPC using data from the current operating condition. In autonomous vehicle racing, the tire-road friction varies between racetrack sections and tire sets. If the initial trajectory and the recorded data originate from different frictions, prediction accuracy of DPC degrades. Ensuring the frictions match requires knowing the friction during recording and estimating the current friction explicitly. Instead, we pool data recorded at different frictions. We compare the prediction accuracy of DPC using data recorded under the current friction (matched), a different friction (mismatched) and data pooled from both frictions. We evaluate in simulation and small-scale vehicle experiments in the Cyber-Physical Mobility Lab (CPM Lab). Our results show that pooled data keep the multi-step root-mean-square prediction error within 1.5 times that of matched data, whereas mismatched data increase it by a factor of 2.2 to 3.4. To assess how this prediction accuracy carries over to control, we evaluate the tracking error from the raceline in closed loop. In simulation, DPC with pooled data tracks comparably to nonlinear model predictive control (13.7 cm versus 13.3 cm) and close to DPC with matched data in the CPM Lab, differing by 0.1 cm on the low-friction tires (1.6 cm versus 1.5 cm) and by 0.2 cm on the high-friction tires (0.9 cm versus 1.1 cm). DPC thus provides partial adaptation to varying friction, without a dedicated adaptation method.

items.title: From very fine Vertical Resolution to Range Super-Resolution on BIOMASS P-BAND SAR Data
items.summary: This paper demonstrates range super-resolution over arid regions using SAR tomography data with very fine vertical resolution from the European Space Agency's BIOMASS mission. As the first civilian spaceborne P-band SAR mission, BIOMASS is operating with a bandwidth limited to 6~MHz by International Telecommunication Union regulations, yielding a native slant-range resolution of approximately 25 m. The large spatial baseline data acquired during the commissioning phase in July and August 2025 provide a valuable opportunity to enhance range resolution based on the InSAR wavenumber shift principle. According to this principle, a wider effective bandwidth can be synthesized by combining complementary sub-bands of the ground reflectivity spectrum sampled across acquisitions at different look angles. Unlike existing literature, this paper offers a novel interpretation of this problem from the perspective of SAR tomography. Furthermore, the proposed method also accounts for residual topography errors. The range resolution enhancement performance is validated using all 20 available acquisitions from the July-August 2025 commissioning phase over Lop Nur, China, and Wadi al-Hayat, Libya, achieving spatial detail comparable to optical satellite imagery in a grid finer than 2 m. Furthermore, the reconstructed range spectrum of the central Libyan oasis exhibits an effective bandwidth exceeding 70 MHz. The point spread function (PSF) of a point like target in the scene demonstrates a slant-range resolution finer than 2.1 m, representing more than a twelvefold improvement over the native resolution.

items.title: Harmonic-Constrained Hosting Capacity of Active Distribution Networks Using ESS Compensation and Certified Adaptive Decision-Tree Envelopes
items.summary: Active distribution networks increasingly rely on coordinated inverter-based resources to accommodate renewable generation, while harmonic limits constrain the capacity that can be connected. This paper proposes a harmonic optimal power flow (HOPF) method with active energy-storage-system (ESS) support. ESS charging, discharging and harmonic-current compensation are jointly scheduled under state-of-charge dynamics and a shared converter-current rating. An adaptive decision tree learns voltage-current partitions from OPF operating points. Within each leaf, an affine plane is fitted on an analytic grid and certified as a lower envelope. A disaggregated mixed-integer formulation embeds these envelopes in a second-order-cone-relaxed network model. Annual hourly data are assessed through daily capacity optimization, followed by componentwise capacity aggregation and chronological full-year feasibility validation. In the case study, the OPF reference of 65.572 MW exceeds the adopted harmonic bounds, whereas HOPF without harmonic support yields an annually validated capacity of 56.892 MW. With each generator capacity bounded by its OPF reference, the proposed method recovers the complete reference allocation. Coordinated energy dispatch and harmonic compensation thus recover generation capacity within the installed ESS converter ratings.

items.title: Strong nonlinear detectability and moving horizon estimation for nonlinear systems with unknown inputs
items.summary: This paper investigates state estimation for general nonlinear discrete-time systems subject to measurement noise and possibly unbounded unknown inputs. To approach this problem, we first propose the concept of strong nonlinear detectability, which proves to be a nonlinear counterpart to strong* detectability. Based on the proposed detectability notion, an unknown input state estimator (UISE), which yields bounded estimation error even for unbounded unknown inputs, is designed via a moving horizon estimation strategy using past and current measurements. Next, we tighten this detectability notion to develop a two-stage MHE-based UISE that is computationally more efficient. In a simulation example, both variants of MHE-based UISEs are compared with a conventional MHE to illustrate the merits of the proposed methods.

items.title: Balancing Confidentiality and Attack Detectability in Networked Control Systems over Lossy Wireless Channels
items.summary: We study the joint protection of a networked control system (NCS) against eavesdropping and data integrity attacks over a lossy wireless channel. The eavesdropper intercepts the transmitted sensor measurements and control inputs to reconstruct the system state. In contrast, the integrity attacker in this study replaces the sensor measurements with fabricated data to drive the system to undesired operating conditions. Although these two threats are typically studied separately, a wireless NCS should be protected against both simultaneously, and a defence against one affects the other. We employ an observation-encoding scheme that renders the eavesdropper's state-estimation error covariance unbounded under packet drops, and show that transmission energy governs how long this error remains bounded. In particular, lower transmission energy improves confidentiality. For integrity protection, we combine stochastic physical watermarking with a CUSUM-based sequential change detector. The proposed attack detection scheme accounts for intermittent communication and encoded measurements. The detection delay is governed by the Kullback--Leibler divergence (KLD) between the pre- and post-attack distributions of the test signal, and we show that a higher transmission energy increases the KLD and thereby reduces the detection delay. Furthermore, we derive analytical expressions for the eavesdropper's estimation error and the worst-case expected KLD, providing guidelines for selecting transmission energy to balance confidentiality and integrity protection and characterising the privacy--security trade-off. Finally, we run numerical simulations to validate our theoretical findings and demonstrate the privacy--security trade-off in practical scenarios.

items.title: Reference Replay for Excitation Injection and Subsequent Exponential Convergence under Concurrent Learning Adaptive Control
items.summary: Concurrent learning (CL) guarantees precise identification of unknown parameters---if data with finite excitation (FE) happens to be collected online. To improve the reliability of CL, this work establishes a mechanism allowing FE-occurrence to be verified a priori: We propose replaying a given training segment in the reference until data with finite excitation is collected online. Provided the training segment fulfills a certain off-line excitation test, FE then occurs in unknown, but finite time. Moreover, we provide an upper bound on the time-to-FE. Even though this bound involves a dependency on the unknown initial Lyapunov-function value, its structure shows that FE occurs in arbitrarily early replay cycles when increasing the control gain; which may motivate employing a high-gain strategy. The theoretical findings are verified on an academic simulation example.

items.title: Robust Optimal Network Reduction for Distribution Systems
items.summary: Network reduction replaces large networks with smaller equivalents to speed up power flow and optimization studies. Optimal Kron-based Reduction of Networks (Opti-KRON) finds the optimal set of nodes to faithfully represent a large-scale radial network for representative loading scenarios. Under unseen nodal injections, however, its accuracy can drop. This paper extends Opti-KRON to uncertain nodal injections using robust uncertainty sets and a Wasserstein ambiguity set, with voltage magnitude error guarantees. To improve scalability, we develop a presolve screening step to eliminate redundant constraints and variables while preserving the feasible set. We also adopt adversarial constraint generation to reduce memory requirements by iteratively adding worst-case nodal injections. On a real 8,387-node feeder at a threshold of 0.001~p.u., the reduction removes 49.9% of the nodes. For one uncertainty set, adversarial constraint generation cuts the required memory by a factor of more than 18.

items.title: Quantum-Assisted D-FACTS Scheduling for Moving Target Defense under Switching Limits
items.summary: Moving target defense with distributed flexible alternating-current transmission system (D-FACTS) devices re- quires activation decisions as operating points change. Switching limits couple these decisions, but period-by-period rankings can overlook combinations needed to complete low-activation schedules. This paper proposes cross-period candidate sharing and schedule-completion evaluation to allocate limited physical checks in quantum-assisted D-FACTS scheduling. The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) generates activation candidates, while classical scheduling enforces operating and switching constraints. We also quantify model-based activation requirements and test detection through noisy nonlinear trials. A modified IEEE 118-bus study assesses recovery of reference activation and switching objectives within the evaluated set. Combining candidate sharing and schedule-completion evaluation improves final-budget recovery over period-by-period ranking in the primary operating window for every tested candidate generator. The results show that quantum and classical candidates yield identical recovery curves under combined checking, so the same allocation policy applies to either source.

items.title: Hybrid Optimization-Generative Motion Planning for Multiagent Affine Formations
items.summary: Formation maneuver control enables a multiagent system to cooperatively navigate through constrained environments in collective motion. While various formation controllers exist, they rely heavily on high-quality and dynamically feasible reference trajectories provided a priori, making formation motion planning (FMP) essential. To address the computational challenges for high-dimensional joint trajectories faced by conventional constrained optimization-based solutions, this paper introduces a hybrid optimization-generative framework with a focus on affine formations, which provide the necessary spatial flexibility. By formulating the planning task as a constrained Maximum-a-Posteriori estimation, we decouple multiagent objectives to leverage pre-trained single-agent diffusion priors for dynamic feasibility, obstacle avoidance, and smoothness. We then interleave the generative process with projected gradient descent (PGD) to strictly enforce affine geometric constraints with safety guarantees. Simulations demonstrate that our framework generates highly smooth, collision-free plans that are readily trackable by common distributed controllers and outperforms state-of-the-art planners in various metrics.

items.title: Leveraging Binary Hashing for Scalable Index Assignment in Semantic Communications
items.summary: Transmitting semantically structured embedding vectors over digital channels is costly in bit rate, while conven- tional vector quantization approaches face limitations in scalabil- ity, encoding complexity, and index assignment. This paper inves- tigates binary hashing techniques from the information retrieval literature as semantic indexing strategies for general-purpose networks. We study random Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) along with Principal Component Analysis (PCA)-, Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA)-, and ITQ (Iterative Quantization)- based variants in a semantic communication pipeline over a Binary Symmetric Channel. Embeddings are compressed into binary codes, reconstructed through Hamming retrieval from a shared table, and evaluated on downstream classification. Ex- periments on the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) and the Banking77 dataset show that data-dependent hashing improves upon random LSH, while ITQ refinement increases robustness to channel noise. Among the evaluated methods, CCA- ITQ achieves the best classification accuracy across the tested channel conditions. These results indicate that binary hashing is an efficient and scalable alternative to quantization-based embedding compression for semantic communications.

items.title: Continuous Phase-Coherent Readout of a Magneto-Mechanical Resonator Using a Phase-Locked Loop
items.summary: Magneto-mechanical resonators are wireless sensors that encode a measurand in their natural frequency. Existing systems estimate this frequency from repeated cycles of excitation and ring-down, which limits the precision and bandwidth range. Here, we introduce a continuous, phase-coherent readout based on a phase-locked loop. In a benchtop setup, one record stayed within 4 % of the precision-bandwidth limit over more than three decades of bandwidth, while conventional readouts remained about a factor of 4 above it.

items.title: Heteroscedastic Gaussian Process Q-learning for Sample Efficient Experimentation
items.summary: Self-driving laboratories must learn to control a process from tens to hundreds of expensive experiments, too few for deep reinforcement learning (RL). We learn the Q-function directly with a Gaussian process (GP), which avoids learning the dynamics, and show that the GP posterior supplies the learning rate of Q-learning. If each Bellman target is treated as a noisy measurement of the Q-function, the learning rate that minimises the mean squared error is the Kalman gain, and applying it to every observed transition is equivalent to GP regression. Heteroscedastic Gaussian Process Q-learning (HGPQ) sets the noise variance of each target with a heteroscedastic GP, which learns how unreliable the targets are across the states and inputs. Targets from noisy operating conditions, or from regions where the value function has large gradients, then move the estimate less than targets from low-noise regions, so HGPQ learns quickly where the data are reliable without being misled where they are not. For kernel value iteration with per-target variances that are assigned when a target is collected, we prove a high-probability bound on the error of the value estimate, uniform over the explored region. Pooled over five simulated benchmarks, which include a chemical reactor and a bioprocess, HGPQ approaches the best return found by any method in fewer episodes than GP, kernel and deep RL baselines.

items.title: Neurosymbolic Synthesis of Contraction Metrics with Certified Verification
items.summary: We study counterexample-guided synthesis of contraction metrics for continuous-time autonomous systems on compact domains. A learner proposes a metric; a sound verifier certifies its matrix inequality or returns diagnostic points for retraining. The neural extension pairs a learned metric factor with symbolic contraction conditions and rigorous numerical verification; main ablations use polynomial features. We give computable polynomial bounds in arbitrary dimension and outward-rounded verification for polynomial, trigonometric, and neural representations. Loop soundness is separated from conditional finite-grid termination under idealized feasibility assumptions. We analyze why scaling and fixed-margin training can leave valid metrics uncertified. The scaling construction requires a scale-closed family, which the experimental fixed-floor class generally lacks. Verified slack improves the contraction rate and quantifies model-error tolerances using certified residual and Jacobian bounds. Finite-distance conclusions require connecting paths whose flows stay in the verified region. Experiments include controlled ablations, three-dimensional verification, and transfer from a fitted surrogate with known-truth residual certification. A physical swing-model study compares neural learning objectives with shared verification and invariant energy regions. Verified constant metrics certify the polynomial benchmark and smallest swing-model domain; neither result requires neural state dependence. Exploratory refinement certifies additional frozen candidates at a larger verification budget. In matched polynomial operating-grid experiments, trace normalization and margin coupling did not demonstrate a certification-count advantage within the tested budgets. These choices address specific failure mechanisms without guaranteeing optimizer convergence or general empirical superiority.

items.title: Slower but Faster: When Self-Organized Traffic Flows Beat Traffic Signal Control
items.summary: Urban traffic flow networks are complex adaptive systems, whose variability challenges centralized, top-down control. We study decentralized alternatives in which order emerges from local interactions, comparing the network-wide performance of roundabouts in SUMO against fixed-time and actuated control as well as self-organizing signals on a 4$\times$4 grid and a rewired, irregular variant of it, across demand levels and periodic surge amplitudes. In our computer simulations of the regular grid, converting the single most central intersection already lowers delays by 2 to 3\% relative to actuated control; each additional conversion lowers them further, and full conversion outperforms every signalized alternative under all conditions studied. In the irregular traffic flow network with full conversion of all intersections into roundabouts, this holds only up to a critical load, where traffic flow breaks down sharply, when the time-averaged demand reaches about 3.1 times the base load. Beyond that point, the self-organizing traffic signals show the lowest delay of any network-wide strategy and is nearly insensitive to surges. Interestingly, roundabouts are favorable solutions even at lower speed limits: in the regular grid, compared to the mean speed under actuated control at a speed limit of 50\,km/h, roundabouts match that speed at a speed limit of about 40\,km/h. Compared to traffic signal control, this establishes a slower-is-faster effect. Furthermore, travel times in self-organized traffic flows are more predictable than in networks with conventional signals.

items.title: Recursive Spectral Graph Partitioning Coding for Index Assignment in Semantic Communications
items.summary: Transmitting quantized semantic embeddings over a bit-flip channel requires a binary mapping that minimizes expected reconstruction distortion. The classical Binary Switching Algorithm (BSA) ($\mathcal{O}(K^3 \log K)$ for $K$ centroids) yields locally optimal assignments but ignores hierarchical bit significance, making it incompatible with Unequal Error Protection (UEP). We propose Recursive Spectral Graph Partitioning (RSGP), which recursively bisects the centroid affinity graph along the Fiedler eigenvector so that early bits separate semantically distant groups while later bits refine local structure. RSGP runs in $\mathcal{O}(K^3)$ with no iterative outer loop, and is the only method studied to show a systematic positive UEP gain: protecting early bits over later ones improves accuracy for RSGP, while being neutral or harmful for unstructured assignments. Experiments on the Banking77 dataset and the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) confirm that RSGP consistently matches or exceeds BSA accuracy across codebook sizes and error profiles.

items.title: Investigating the Benefit of Transfer Learning from the Locus Coeruleus for Substantia Nigra Pars Compacta Segmentation
items.summary: The substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) is a small midbrain nucleus that degenerates early in Parkinson's disease (PD). T1-weighted FLASH MRI enables its visualization and may support early detection of neurodegeneration. However, manual segmentation is difficult and time-consuming, and deep learning models often suffer from the limited availability of labeled data. Transfer learning (TL) may help by adapting pre-trained models to small datasets. We investigate whether TL from a model trained on the locus coeruleus (LC), a nucleus with a similar appearance in this sequence, improves SNpc segmentation. Several TL strategies were evaluated using a 3D U-Net. With as few as 5-14 labeled subjects, TL and training from scratch achieved similar performance, reaching a Dice similarity coefficient of up to 0.77, close to reported inter-rater agreement. No TL strategy differed significantly from training from scratch, suggesting that initialization from the LC offers no significant benefit for SNpc segmentation.

items.title: Estimation of aboveground biomass in a tropical dry forest: An intercomparison of airborne, unmanned, and space laser scanning
items.summary: Accurate aboveground biomass (AGB) estimates are needed to report forest carbon under the Paris Agreement, yet tropical dry forests (TDFs) remain among the least studied tropical ecosystems. We present a plot-level intercomparison of airborne (ALS), unmanned (ULS) and simulated spaceborne full-waveform (SLS, GEDI simulator) laser scanning for AGB estimation in ten permanent plots of Santa Rosa National Park, Costa Rica, covering early to late succession. Reference AGB (22-220 Mg/ha) was computed from the 2021 census with a documented procedure that screens diameter time series and propagates measurement, wood-density and allometric errors (plot uncertainty 3.5-14.5%). We compared ordinary least squares (OLS), a log-log model of mean canopy height fixed a priori and a single-metric model selected from the data, with support vector machine regression (SVM). Predictor selection, scaling and hyper-parameter tuning were nested within leave-one-plot-out validation. ALS gave the lowest errors: the a priori OLS model reached an RMSE of 32.3 Mg/ha (29%, R2_LOO = 0.77) and SVM 35.8 Mg/ha (32%). SVM did not improve on OLS for any platform and was significantly worse with ULS (p = 0.01). The best ULS and SLS models reached 33% and 37%; differences between platforms were not significant with ten plots. Selecting predictors on all plots before cross-validation lowered the apparent SVM error by up to 23 percentage points, and footprint coordinates, ALS point density and terrain elevation from the GEDI simulator produced spurious skill; these effects explain the higher accuracies reported in an earlier version of this work. Model errors remained at least 2.5 times larger than the field-AGB uncertainty. With small plot networks, a height-based OLS model with ALS is the most robust choice, and more and larger plots are needed before nonlinear models can be shown to add value in TDFs.

items.title: BoBDeLaN: Bounded-Bandwidth Context Adaptation for Deep Lagrangian Robot Control
items.summary: Learned physics-based models provide structure for robot control, but uncertain payloads and unmodeled dynamics limit their predictive accuracy. Context-aware Deep Lagrangian Networks enable adaptation through a latent context inferred from measurement histories while retaining Lagrangian structure for each fixed context. However, this structure alone does not constrain sensitivity to measurement disturbances. We introduce BoBDeLaN, which combines a contracting, gain-bounded Recurrent Equilibrium Network context encoder with stable linear filtering to shape disturbance sensitivity across frequencies. This architecture guarantees exponential forgetting of the recurrent initialization and admits a finite-horizon, frequency-weighted bound on context perturbations, which extends to residual torque prediction under a Lipschitz continuity assumption on the context-conditioned dynamics model.
